records.title: Parkes observations for project P1365 semester 2026APRS_06
records.description: Following the successful demonstration of a pilot first-pass (shallow) search of a small fraction of the sky, the second-pass processing has commenced for the SMART pulsar survey, which involves deep searches of 80-minute observations. Over the past year, this second-pass processing has led to the discovery of 16 new pulsars (including two millisecond pulsars), bringing the total number of SMART discoveries to 20 when combined with the first-pass results. These outcomes hint at the exciting promise of this first southern-sky pulsar survey in the frequency band of SKA-Low. All new pulsars require timing observations to determine their spin and astrometric parameters. Another important aspect of timing newly discovered pulsars is to identify specialised targets for further detailed follow-ups. Since the MWA no longer supports routine pulsar observations from 2025, timing follow-ups rely on other telescopes. The data will also allow us to study pulse profiles, polarisation, and flux densities from ~100 MHz to 4 GHz. The analysis/results will be included in a publication in preparation that will detail the deep-search pipeline and report on initial pulsar discoveries.

records.title: Parkes observations for project P1054 semester 2026APRS_23
records.description: With this proposal we ask time to continue our timing follow-up campaign of pulsars discovered with the MeerKAT telescope. Fiftythree sources have been discovered in targeted observations of Fermi unidentified point sources, two towards Supernova Remnants, 27 in the Magellanic Clouds, 109 in Globular Clusters and 96 in a survey of the Galactic plane. A large fraction of the new discoveries are recycled pulsars (including a few relativistic systems, a pulsar with a planetary companion and several 'spider' binaries), or young pulsars. Timing observations have an essential role in exploiting the full potential of any pulsar discovery, allowing for the precise measurement of rotational, astrometric and orbital parameters which, in turn, give us powerful tools to improve our understanding of the physics in extreme environments as well as of the population of neutron stars as a whole. The UWL receiver of the Parkes telescope is a sensitive, versatile instrument that is allowing us to successfully time these new sources, in the bright-end of TRAPUM discoveries.

records.title: Parkes observations for project P1398 semester 2026APRS_07
records.description: Low-frequency (< ~1 GHz) Galactic-plane pulsar surveys are strongly limited by sky background noise, interstellar scattering, and dispersion smearing, leading to an incomplete census of the pulsar population. High-frequency (> 2 GHz) observations mitigate these effects and have recently enabled the discovery of pulsars that remain undetectable at low-frequency. We analyzed archival data from the 2008 Parkes 6.5-GHz pulsar survey using modern search techniques. This reprocessing has revealed four previously unknown millisecond pulsar candidates with spin periods of 3-11 ms and dispersion measures of 20-170 pc/cc. Two candidates exhibit significant line-of-sight acceleration, indicating likely membership in compact binary systems. We request a total of 8.4 hours of follow-up observations with the Parkes (Murriyang) Ultra-Wideband Low (UWL) receiver to confirm these candidates and characterize their emission across 704-4032 MHz. Confirming these sources would expand the population of high-frequency selected pulsars and demonstrate the continued importance of high-frequency searches for uncovering exotic systems obscured in conventional low-frequency surveys.

records.title: Long-term project observations for project L124 semester 2026APRS_07
records.description: We propose a long-term project to monitor a very active repeater, FRB 20190520B, with Murriyang's UWL system. Our previous observations show that FRB 20190520B is not only among the most active FRBs that can be observed with Murriyang, but also shows extreme rotation measure (RM) and dispersion measure (DM) evolution, along with distinctive behavior at 3GHz frequency. This makes the UWL receiver uniquely suited for detailed studies and long-term monitoring of this repeating FRB. Through this program, we anticipate detecting a large sample of bursts from this FRB. In collaboration with FAST, we aim to investigate the time evolution of various properties of FRB 20190520B, enhance our understanding of polarisation across an extremely wide bandwidth with high sensitivity, and gain deeper insights into the local environment and emission mechanisms of FRBs.

records.title: Parkes observations for project P1411 semester 2026APRS_19
records.description: Conventional blind pulsar surveys that search for periodic signals in high-time-resolution data are increasingly limited by interstellar scattering at high dispersion measure (DM), orbital modulation in compact binaries, scintillation effects, and intensive computational demands. records.title: Parkes observations for project P1416 semester 2026APRS_01
records.description: Radio pulsars in orbit around high-mass stellar companions offer a rich source of extreme physics for both observational astronomers and theorists alike. Despite being discovered 25 years ago, PSR J1638-4725 remains a veritable mystery compared to similar pulsar binary systems. Long-term monitoring has revealed extended `eclipses' where the pulsar is undetectable for months around periastron at GHz frequencies, along with intense variations in the observed pulsar dispersion measure, scatter broadening and flux density throughout the entire orbit. Preliminary spectroscopic characterisation of the companion star suggests it may be an O/B star, albiet one without a circumstellar disc of ejected material. This raises the unique opportunity to answer test the structure and origin of the near-wind regime of high-mass stars. In this proposal we will conduct an ambitious monitoring campaign of PSR J1638-4725 with both the ultra-wideband low and MARS recievers on Murriyang. We will track changes in the pulsar dispersion and scattering as it swings around the companion star, providing unique insights into the density and temperature distribution of the stellar wind from the companion star before and after the pulsar swings through periastron. These observations will also play a pivotal role in a broader multi-wavelength campaign to fully capture the upcoming 2026 periastron passage.

records.title: Parkes observations for project P1423 semester 2026APRS_11
records.description: Pulsars are rapidly rotating, highly magnetized neutron stars whose radio emission provides unique probes of extreme gravity, plasma physics, and magnetospheric processes. Millisecond pulsars(MSPs) exhibit exceptional rotational stability, making them fundamental components of Pulsar Timing Arrays used to detect nanohertz gravitational waves, while also enabling precision tests of general relativity, binary evolution, and studies of the interstellar medium(ISM). Normal pulsars(NPs), on the other hand, serve as powerful laboratories for investigating neutron-star interiors, supernova remnants, magnetospheric physics, pulsar winds, and glitch phenomena. Their polarization measurements are crucial, as they constrain emission geometry, magnetic-field configuration, and propagation effects such as Faraday rotation, while enabling robust determination of rotation measures(RM). For MSPs in particular, polarization studies improve timing-template fidelity and help correct frequency-dependent propagation effects that impact high-precision timing experiments. GMRT low-frequency surveys have significantly expanded the known pulsar population, yet many GMRT-discovered pulsars lack broadband polarization measurements, leaving their emission geometry and frequency-dependent profile evolution poorly constrained. We propose 21 hours of observations with the Parkes 64-m telescope using UWL receiver to conduct a spectro-polarimetric study of six GMRT-discovered pulsars: three MSPs(J1207-5050, J1227-4853, J1646-2142) and three NPs(J0514-4407, J0418-4154, J0702-4956) to conduct a spectro-polarimetric study. These targets exhibit unresolved or contradictory polarization behaviour, including profile evolution, eclipse-driven interaction signatures, incomplete detections, or absence of full-Stokes information. The proposed wideband, high-sensitivity observations will provide robust RM measurements, broadband polarization profiles, and frequency-dependent beam mapping, filling key observational gaps and enhancing the scientific value of GMRT-discovered pulsars for magnetospheric studies and pulsar timing science.

records.title: Parkes observations for project P1183 semester 2026APRS_07
records.description: After nearly four years of monitoring with both the Parkes and FAST telescopes, FRB 20220529 has been established as an extremely active repeater. It exhibits one of the longest known activity durations and shows evidence for a potential periodicity. Owing to the frequent observations carried out with Parkes and FAST, two abrupt rotation-measure (RM) flares have been detected in this source. These constitute the first RM flares ever observed in a fast radio burst (FRB), indicating that a dense, magnetised plasma clump passed across the line of sight. The second RM flare in particular makes a binary-origin scenario for FRB 20220529 especially compelling. If confirmed, the periodicity and RM flares would mutually reinforce one another, serving as a smoking gun for a binary origin. Previous analyses have shown that observations from both Parkes and FAST are essential. FAST's exceptional sensitivity enables the detection of many bursts, whereas the Parkes UWL receiver provides a stable burst-detection rate even during low-activity phases. To further investigate FRB 20220529, we have scheduled regular FAST observations every fortnight. We therefore propose to continue monitoring FRB 20220529 with the Parkes UWL receiver as well. The FAST and Parkes sessions are expected to be separated by a few days, ideally about one week. A cadence of approximately one week offers an excellent opportunity to capture detailed structure during the onset of RM decreases, as demonstrated by previous monitoring.

records.title: Source or sink. Precipitation shapes future terrestrial carbon uptake in Australia: research data
records.description: This collection contains scripts and data to reproduce all analysis and figures in the research publication Source or sink? Precipitation shapes future terrestrial carbon uptake in Australia. These data were produced from simulation output created by the CABLE-POP land-surface model using projected meteorological forcing under SSP1-2.6 and SSP3-7.0 from seven CMIP6 global climate models that were dynamically downscaled using CCAM and bias-corrected using the ECDfm method. Data format are comma separated value (.csv) files, .txt files and R scripts. Additional details on the data structure and usage are available in the associated README.txt CABLE-POP model version: https://github.com/CABLE-LSM/CABLE/releases/tag/pub-1ad09981 CCAM data: CORDEX-CMIP6, CCAM, high resolution projections available in the NCI Data Catalogue (https://geonetwork.nci.org.au/)

records.title: Long-term project observations for project L101 semester 2026APRS_04
records.description: The Parkes Pulsar Timing Array (PPTA) project has three primary goals: (a) detection of gravitational waves from astronomical sources, (b) establishment of a pulsar timescale, and (c) improvement of our understanding of Solar-system dynamics. We are now in an exciting regime where a signal detected in our (and other data sets) has the form expected for a gravitational wave background. We, along with the international community, are now working hard to either confirm or deny this result, and to determine the astrophysical origin of this signal. With this proposal, we aim to maintain our pre-eminent position in the field. This is a continuing proposal for which observations of millisecond pulsars (MSPs) will continue to improve bounds on ultra-low-frequency gravitational waves until they are detected with confidence. Continued Parkes observations will remain valuable at least until the first stage of the SKA is able to improve on our sensitivity and observing cadence. Even after the gravitational wave background is detected, continued observations will resolve the background origin and individual sources will be identified; advancing the nascent field of gravitational wave astronomy.

records.title: Glossy Black-Cockatoo population genomic data
records.description: MtDNA, microsatellite and SNP data from publication - Kearns, Lee, Sarre, Pedler and Joseph "Genetic diversity, population genetic structure and comments on the historical distribution of the Glossy Black-Cockatoo". Emu in press. Abstract: We report on a genetic survey of the Glossy Black-Cockatoo Calyptorhynchus lathami from throughout its range except far north Queensland. We used mitochondrial DNA, microsatellites and single nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) to ask whether Evolutionarily Significant Units or Management Units can be diagnosed within the species. Nuclear DNA diversity estimated from both SNPs and microsatellites supported differentiation between the isolated Kangaroo Island and mainland populations. SNP data were limited by sampling issues but show the differentiation that can be reasonably expected between Kangaroo Island (KI) and Queensland populations. Support for genetic differentiation within the mainland populations was generally weak but our data are preliminary. Mitochondrial DNA identified a single unique haplotype on KI but did not support reciprocal monophyly or clear genetic distinction of mainland and KI populations. Our data best support recognition of at least two Management Units (KI vs all eastern mainland populations). We urge continuation of all conservation efforts for all populations especially that on KI. We discuss and favour dismissal of all post-European settlement distribution records of C. lathami from far south- western Victoria and south-eastern South Australia. These have long been problematic due to confusion with Red-tailed Black-Cockatoos C. banksii. There is much scope for further work to achieve finer resolution on questions such as the genetic connectivity or otherwise of scattered populations across western and central New South Wales and the genetic health of those populations and the isolated KI population.

records.title: shadesheltr: spatial modelling of shade, shelter and productivity effects of farm trees
records.description: The shadesheltr package rovides a spatially explicit framework for modelling the effects of trees on farms, including shade, shelter, and productivity impacts on agricultural land uses. The package implements geometry-based interactions between production areas and tree assets, rasterises resulting effects on a common analysis grid, and supports aggregation and accounting of ecosystem service benefits for scenario comparison and reporting. The design emphasises modularity, reproducibility, and transparency for farm-scale analysis. Note these models are designed for planning and assessment of ecosystem services, and are based on generic response functions as detailed in the supporting manuscript and technical report.

records.title: A Standard Metadata Template for Representing Mineral Spectral Reference Samples
records.description: This dataset provides a standardized template for representing metadata associated with mineral spectral reference samples within the CSIRO Mineral Resources Discovery program. It captures key sample attributes such as specimen name, identifier, type, and location, together with contextual metadata including project information, sampling context, hazard declarations, and physical storage details. Developed iteratively with input from researchers and laboratory technicians, the template supports the systematic curation and management of mineral reference samples through the CMR Specify collection management system. It is designed to facilitate the cataloguing of reference samples collected by the program, including specimens from the National Virtual Core Library (NVCL) collection. By standardizing metadata entry, the template reduces duplicate data entry and metadata redundancy, while improving the consistency, management, and discoverability of physical sample collections.

records.title: Long-term project observations for project L147 semester 2026APRS_04
records.description: We propose to carry out a deep Galactic Bulge pulsar survey (GBps), covering the core of the Bulge region using the new cryoPAF system on Murriyang, the Parkes radio telescope. Such a deep survey is expected to discover a population of millisecond pulsars in the Galactic Bulge and reveal their distribution and gamma-ray emissions. With these, we will lead pioneering studies on the origin of gamma-ray emission in the Galactic Bulge, a longstanding mystery in modern astronomy. The outcome of this project will significantly advance our knowledge of the formation and evolution of millisecond pulsars in the Galactic Bulge, the origin and properties of high-energy emissions, and the nature of dark matter annihilation in the Galactic Centre. A total of 200 observations with the cryoPAF is required to cover a 400 square degree region (|gl|<10 deg, |gb|<10 deg). The survey is expected to be carried out over four semesters, from April 2026 to October 2027.

records.title: Parkes observations for project P1409 semester 2026APRS_05
records.description: To investigate the physical origin and local environment of the repeating fast radio burst FRB 20230607A, which exhibits an exceptionally high rotation measure, we propose to observe this repeater with 24-hour observations using the Ultra-Wideband Low-frequency (UWL) receiver of the Parkes radio telescope (Murriyang). This proposal aims to monitor the secular evolution of the Faraday Rotation Measure, studying the cause of its low linear polarization, and resolve the specro-polarimetric structure of repeat bursts. The possible findings are critical to unveiling the extreme magnetized environment of the source, understanding emission mechanisms and propagation effects, and thereby shedding light on the physics origin(s) of repeating fast radio bursts.

records.title: Introduced Scarabaeinae dung beetles in grassland pastures in SW Australia 1977-1985
records.description: For this project we collected data from the SW of WA during 1977-1985. We have broken the data into 5 files which are listed below. See file “_Description_of_all_dataSets_csiro_wa.docx” for more information on details of each column within the file, including insect counts for each species. csiro_wa_1977_1985_trap.csv Description: This is the main file with the abundance counts for Scarabaeinae, Aphodiinae (both generally to species level), Histeridae, Hydrophilidae and Staphylinidae (to family level only) collected from traps deployed in pastures in SW Western Australia from 1977-1985. There are 1,284 trap records. csiro_wa_1977_1985_trap_sex.csv Description: For some species and some trap samples in the csiro_wa_1977_1985_trap.csv data, the counts from the traps were split by sex. This spreadsheet provides those counts (i.e. the counts for males and females). There are 308 trap records in these data, each of which has two data rows (one for females and one for males). csiro_wa_1977_1985_sites.csv Description: Summary data giving the site names and geographic coordinates. Could be included as a data file or as part of the metadata. csiro_wa_1977_1981_morphology.csv Description: Body length (mm) and Dry mass (g) data for individual specimens of Australaphodius frenchi, Onitis alexis, Onthophagus binodis, Onthophagus ferox, Onthophagus haagi and Aphodius pseudolividus. Each row in the data represents an individual beetle. There are measurements from 170 beetles. csiro_wa_1977_1984_dissections.csv Description: Dissection data for individual specimens of Euoniticellus pallipes, Onthophagus binodis, Onthophagus ferox and Onthophagus haagi used for age-grading dung beetles. records.title: Interpolated climate variables for the Himalayan Kingdom of Bhutan
records.description: Monthly (1985-2020) and monthly mean (1986-2015) surfaces of maximum temperature, minimum temperature, vapour pressure and precipitation for the Himalayan Kingdom of Bhutan at a spatial resolution of 250 m. These climate surfaces are novel, in that the weather stations (n = 69) used in their development have rarely been made available or incorporated into contemporary climate products. Multiple calibration methods are provided for maximum and minimum temperature, following the methods described in by Stewart et al. (2017). Please refer to the attached documentation for a detailed description of methods applied, statistical performance, and comparisons against other contemporary products.

records.title: Parkes observations for project P1422 semester 2026APRS_12
records.description: Interplanetery Scintillation (IPS) is a powerful observing technique for measuring the size and structure of radio sources, as well as characterising solar wind turbulence. Murriyang was used for IPS in the 1960 and 1980s for IPS observations. However, with the the UWL's ultra-wide bandwidth, we believe that Murriyang IPS observations can once again provide a unique science opportunity. Recent observations with the Five-hundred-metre Aperture Spherical Telescope revealed an unexpected trend of scintillation timescale with frequency. Murriyang is the perfect instrument to corroborate this finding. Furthermore, we believe this effect is due to the inner scale of the turbulence, which can be uniquely probed with the high sensitivity and bandwidth of Murriyang in unprecedented detail, with a modest amount of observing time. As well as providing the most detailed study of the Heliosphere's inner scale yet, we can also determine if it can act as a new and direct probe of heliospheric density: an important complement to IPS and extremely useful for understanding the impact of the solar wind to pulsar DM variations. Finally, these observations will also provide useful insights for instrumental systematics on timescales rather longer than pulsar periods (1-10s) but similar to the timescales of the new class of Ultra-long period magnetars. Thus we can better understand whether Murriyang has a role to play in this important discovery space.

records.title: Parkes observations for project P1390 semester 2026APRS_03
records.description: We propose 18.9 hours of Parkes Ultra-Wideband (UWL) observations to investigate PSR J1606-0854, a remarkable nearby Galactic pulsar discovered via the ASKAP CRACO backend. This source exhibits unprecedented emission properties that challenge conventional classification boundaries: it produces ultra-bright bursts (up to 900 Jy ms) with broad durations (~ 20 ms), extremely faint RRAT-like emission (0.02-0.5 Jy ms), but notably lacks intermediate-fluence pulses (1-10 Jy ms). The fluence distribution spans five orders of magnitude, with a surface magnetic field strength of B_surf ~ 1.3e14 G comparable to magnetars, and is the highest among known RRATs. High-sensitivity FAST observations conducted since July 2025 have detected over 100 pulses. With Parkes complementary sensitivity and wideband spectral coverage (0.7-4 GHz), we will search for the missing intermediate-fluence pulses and characterize the source's broadband spectrum. This study provides a unique laboratory for understanding neutron-star emission mechanisms across an unprecedented dynamic range, probing the faint end of the neutron-star emission continuum, and investigating the evolutionary connections between classical pulsars, rotating radio transients, and magnetars.

records.title: Parkes observations for project P1423 semester 2026APRS_12
records.description: Pulsars are rapidly rotating, highly magnetized neutron stars whose radio emission provides unique probes of extreme gravity, plasma physics, and magnetospheric processes. Millisecond pulsars(MSPs) exhibit exceptional rotational stability, making them fundamental components of Pulsar Timing Arrays used to detect nanohertz gravitational waves, while also enabling precision tests of general relativity, binary evolution, and studies of the interstellar medium(ISM). Normal pulsars(NPs), on the other hand, serve as powerful laboratories for investigating neutron-star interiors, supernova remnants, magnetospheric physics, pulsar winds, and glitch phenomena. Their polarization measurements are crucial, as they constrain emission geometry, magnetic-field configuration, and propagation effects such as Faraday rotation, while enabling robust determination of rotation measures(RM). For MSPs in particular, polarization studies improve timing-template fidelity and help correct frequency-dependent propagation effects that impact high-precision timing experiments. GMRT low-frequency surveys have significantly expanded the known pulsar population, yet many GMRT-discovered pulsars lack broadband polarization measurements, leaving their emission geometry and frequency-dependent profile evolution poorly constrained. We propose 21 hours of observations with the Parkes 64-m telescope using UWL receiver to conduct a spectro-polarimetric study of six GMRT-discovered pulsars: three MSPs(J1207-5050, J1227-4853, J1646-2142) and three NPs(J0514-4407, J0418-4154, J0702-4956) to conduct a spectro-polarimetric study. These targets exhibit unresolved or contradictory polarization behaviour, including profile evolution, eclipse-driven interaction signatures, incomplete detections, or absence of full-Stokes information. The proposed wideband, high-sensitivity observations will provide robust RM measurements, broadband polarization profiles, and frequency-dependent beam mapping, filling key observational gaps and enhancing the scientific value of GMRT-discovered pulsars for magnetospheric studies and pulsar timing science.

records.title: Long-term project observations for project L125 semester 2026APRS_20
records.description: The atomic interstellar medium shows tiny-scale optical depth fluctuations on the scale of 0.1~10,000 AU, whose origin and nature are poorly understood. The existence of this Tiny-Scale Atomic Structure (TSAS) has significant implications, potentially calling into question our fundamental understanding of heating, cooling and dynamical processes in the interstellar medium. Yet observations remain sparse. This long-term project plans to search for temporal variations in HI absorption spectra seen against background pulsars to characterise TSAS in the Milky Way interstellar medium (ISM). These observations constitute the largest number of sightlines and densest temporal sampling ever performed in a single experiment, and will test predictions that TSAS is the tail end of a turbulent cascade, constrain its minimum size scale (down to resolutions of ~0.05 AU) and potentially provide the first direct measurements of pressures in "large" TSAS features of > 1000 AU. We make use of the phase-resolved spectral line mode that we have recently implemented on Parkes, which has cut data rates and processing times by factors of ~1000 compared to past studies. This is an expansion of our pilot P1321 to a long term study.

records.title: Parkes observations for project P1365 semester 2026APRS_08
records.description: Following the successful demonstration of a pilot first-pass (shallow) search of a small fraction of the sky, the second-pass processing has commenced for the SMART pulsar survey, which involves deep searches of 80-minute observations. Over the past year, this second-pass processing has led to the discovery of 16 new pulsars (including two millisecond pulsars), bringing the total number of SMART discoveries to 20 when combined with the first-pass results. These outcomes hint at the exciting promise of this first southern-sky pulsar survey in the frequency band of SKA-Low. All new pulsars require timing observations to determine their spin and astrometric parameters. Another important aspect of timing newly discovered pulsars is to identify specialised targets for further detailed follow-ups. Since the MWA no longer supports routine pulsar observations from 2025, timing follow-ups rely on other telescopes. The Parkes Murriyang telescope, with an identical sky coverage, sensitivity and the wide frequency coverage, offers the best option to time SMART discoveries. We have demonstrated Murriyang's suitability for this through previous semesters and are now extending the project to a sample of 11 pulsars, including six from the last semester. The data will also allow us to study pulse profiles, polarisation, and flux densities from ~100 MHz to 4 GHz. The analysis/results will be included in a publication in preparation that will detail the deep-search pipeline and report on initial pulsar discoveries.

records.title: Parkes observations for project P1402 semester 2026APRS_17
records.description: We propose a dedicated Parkes/Murriyang timing campaign of the newly confirmed narrow-duty cycle (~6 %) millisecond pulsar (MSP) PSR J2147-3604. This source was identified in a reprocessing of the Green Bank North Celestial Cap (GBNCC) survey as a high-confidence candidate with a spin period of 3.2 ms, and a dispersion measure, DM of 17 pc/cc. The pulsar was subsequently confirmed by the Fermi--TRAPUM collaboration via MeerKAT beamforming localisation and Parkes follow-up. Parkes/UWL observations allocated using green time detected this pulsar between 700--1500~MHz, and confirmed that it's in a binary system. Due to its low DM, we also detected strong interstellar scintillation. We request 35~hr of Murriyang time using the UWL receiver and APOLLO backend to obtain a phase-coherent timing solution and to characterise its spin, orbital, and propagation properties. Since the pulsar is also associated with a FERMI source, a precise radio ephemeris will also enable sensitive searches for gamma-ray pulsations in Fermi-LAT data and assess PSR J2147-3604's suitability for pulsar timing arrays (PTAs) and future gamma-ray timing applications.

records.title: Long-term project observations for project L126 semester 2026APRS_12
records.description: We propose a modest program to continue monitoring 4 of the 6 known radio magnetars in order to achieve three primary science goals. The first is to characterise magnetar outbursts over long timescales, for which tracking their rotational, flux density, and polarisation properties provide a clear view of the impulse response of their magnetic fields. Second, understanding the links between magnetars the mysterious fast radio burst phenomenon through the discovery of rare emission and propagation effects, shared spectro-temporal phenomenology, and connections to high-energy (X-ray/gamma-ray) phenomena. Lastly, our continued monitoring has enormous benefit to the wider magnetar community, providing rapid alerts to changes in activity, adding context to unusual behaviour detected by high-energy observations, and a host of supplementary science through the teams extensive collaborative networks. The project and its precursors have been running since 2007 and have contributed to 22 publications since then. This is the first submission since the project was converted to long-term status.

records.title: Parkes observations for project P1375 semester 2026APRS_05
records.description: Rotating radio transients (RRATs) are Galactic neutron stars that emit sporadic radio pulses, and the question of whether apparently one-off sources truly repeat remains unresolved. With the discovery of numerous fast radio bursts (FRBs), the paradigm of 'one detection defines an astrophysical source' has shifted. However, the distinction between truly non-repeating Galactic transients and insufficiently observed repeating sources remains critical. Recent high-sensitivity follow-up observations with FAST have revealed that multiple apparent one-off RRATs originally detected by Parkes are in fact repeating sources, with fainter pulses hundreds of times weaker than their initial bright detections. This discovery raises a fundamental question: are many one-off RRATs simply the result of insufficient observational sensitivity, or do they represent intrinsically catastrophic transient events. We propose deep follow-up monitoring of four apparent one-off RRATs using the Parkes Ultra-Wideband receiver system, which offers 1.7-3.4 times higher sensitivity than the Multibeam discovery data. These observations will constrain the pulse repetition rates and energy distributions of these sources, examine the extreme variability seen in some RRATs and pulsars that exhibit pulses differing by >500 times in brightness, and test whether hidden repeating emission explains the apparent one-off nature of these sources.

records.description: With this proposal, we aim to continue P1032, the rapid measurements of relativistic parameters of southern binary pulsar systems using data from the Parkes Ultra Wideband Low (UWL) receiver. As the MeerTime project at the MeerKAT radio telescope ended in early 2024, observations with the UWL receiver now form the backbone for extending the timing baselines of many pulsars that have been part of this project. Since the source selection in the previous semesters was tailored such that the UWL receiver is the most (versatile and) suited instrument to achieve the proposed scientific goals for the chosen pulsars, we propose to continue these observations. We will use the UWL data to obtain significant orbital coverage and timing baselines on these pulsars and obtain important constraints on orbital and temporal DM variations that will help in identifying the nature of the companion stars. Increasing the number of measured Neutron Star (NS) masses, as well as improving on current constraints has profound implications for NS internal structure and for stellar and binary evolution physics.

records.title: Parkes observations for project P1410 semester 2026APRS_09
records.description: Neutron stars are compact remnants formed in core-collapse supernovae of massive stars. A subset of these objects, known as pulsars, emit highly regular pulses of radiation that make them powerful tools for studying fundamental physics, stellar evolution, and the structure of our Galaxy. Despite decades of surveys, the known pulsar population remains incomplete: while about 4,800 pulsars are currently catalogued, population studies predict that roughly 10,000 or more radio-detectable pulsars should be observable with our current instrumentation. A significant fraction of the missing population is expected to consist of slowly rotating pulsars, which are difficult to detect with standard search pipelines. These pulsars often have very narrow pulse duty cycles and long spin periods, making them susceptible to reduced signal-to-noise ratios and contamination by low-frequency ("red") noise in Fourier-based searches. As a result, many such objects may remain hidden in archival survey data. Motivated by this, we reprocessed archival data from the Parkes Multibeam Pulsar Survey targeting narrow-duty-cycle signals and allowing to investigate lower signal to noise ratios for these candidates. This approach led to the identification of 12 highly credible new slow pulsar candidates that were missed in previous analyses. Several of these candidates show strong folded signal-to-noise ratios and physically plausible dispersion measures, indicating they are likely genuine pulsars. The primary goal of this proposal is to obtain targeted follow-up observations to confirm and time these newly identified pulsar candidates. Confirming them will help close the gap between predicted and observed pulsar populations and demonstrate the continued scientific value of archival radio survey data.

records.title: Parkes observations for project P1423 semester 2026APRS_14
records.description: Pulsars are rapidly rotating, highly magnetized neutron stars whose radio emission provides unique probes of extreme gravity, plasma physics, and magnetospheric processes. Millisecond pulsars(MSPs) exhibit exceptional rotational stability, making them fundamental components of Pulsar Timing Arrays used to detect nanohertz gravitational waves, while also enabling precision tests of general relativity, binary evolution, and studies of the interstellar medium(ISM). Normal pulsars(NPs), on the other hand, serve as powerful laboratories for investigating neutron-star interiors, supernova remnants, magnetospheric physics, pulsar winds, and glitch phenomena. Their polarization measurements are crucial, as they constrain emission geometry, magnetic-field configuration, and propagation effects such as Faraday rotation, while enabling robust determination of rotation measures(RM). For MSPs in particular, polarization studies improve timing-template fidelity and help correct frequency-dependent propagation effects that impact high-precision timing experiments. GMRT low-frequency surveys have significantly expanded the known pulsar population, yet many GMRT-discovered pulsars lack broadband polarization measurements, leaving their emission geometry and frequency-dependent profile evolution poorly constrained. We propose 21 hours of observations with the Parkes 64-m telescope using UWL receiver to conduct a spectro-polarimetric study of six GMRT-discovered pulsars: three MSPs(J1207-5050, J1227-4853, J1646-2142) and three NPs(J0514-4407, J0418-4154, J0702-4956) to conduct a spectro-polarimetric study. These targets exhibit unresolved or contradictory polarization behaviour, including profile evolution, eclipse-driven interaction signatures, incomplete detections, or absence of full-Stokes information. The proposed wideband, high-sensitivity observations will provide robust RM measurements, broadband polarization profiles, and frequency-dependent beam mapping, filling key observational gaps and enhancing the scientific value of GMRT-discovered pulsars for magnetospheric studies and pulsar timing science.

records.title: Parkes observations for project P1032 semester 2026APRS_10
records.description: With this proposal, we aim to continue P1032, the rapid measurements of relativistic parameters of southern binary pulsar systems using data from the Parkes Ultra Wideband Low (UWL) receiver. As the MeerTime project at the MeerKAT radio telescope ended in early 2024, observations with the UWL receiver now form the backbone for extending the timing baselines of many pulsars that have been part of this project. Since the source selection in the previous semesters was tailored such that the UWL receiver is the most (versatile and) suited instrument to achieve the proposed scientific goals for the chosen pulsars, we propose to continue these observations. We will use the UWL data to obtain significant orbital coverage and timing baselines on these pulsars and obtain important constraints on orbital and temporal DM variations that will help in identifying the nature of the companion stars. Increasing the number of measured Neutron Star (NS) masses, as well as improving on current constraints has profound implications for NS internal structure and for stellar and binary evolution physics.

records.title: Parkes observations for project P1416 semester 2026APRS_02
records.description: Radio pulsars in orbit around high-mass stellar companions offer a rich source of extreme physics for both observational astronomers and theorists alike. Despite being discovered 25 years ago, PSR J1638-4725 remains a veritable mystery compared to similar pulsar binary systems. Long-term monitoring has revealed extended `eclipses' where the pulsar is undetectable for months around periastron at GHz frequencies, along with intense variations in the observed pulsar dispersion measure, scatter broadening and flux density throughout the entire orbit. Preliminary spectroscopic characterisation of the companion star suggests it may be an O/B star, albiet one without a circumstellar disc of ejected material. This raises the unique opportunity to answer test the structure and origin of the near-wind regime of high-mass stars. In this proposal we will conduct an ambitious monitoring campaign of PSR J1638-4725 with both the ultra-wideband low and MARS recievers on Murriyang. We will track changes in the pulsar dispersion and scattering as it swings around the companion star, providing unique insights into the density and temperature distribution of the stellar wind from the companion star before and after the pulsar swings through periastron. These observations will also play a pivotal role in a broader multi-wavelength campaign to fully capture the upcoming 2026 periastron passage.

records.title: Parkes observations for project P1406 semester 2026APRS_03
records.description: NGC 362 is a post-core-collapse southern globular cluster (GC) where 12 pulsars have recently been discovered. The pulsar population is very diverse, containing extremely fast-spinning, mildly recycled and slow pulsars, the vast majority of which (11 out of 12) are part of binary systems with very different orbital periods and eccentricities. However, a full orbital characterization was possible only for three of these binaries. This is because the pulsars in NGC 362 are heavily affected by scintillation, and therefore are very elusive. Here, we propose to carry out a series of deep observations of NGC 362, taking advantage of the ultra-wide bandwidth of the UWL receiver, with the aim of determining the orbital parameters of the 8 binary pulsars that still lack characterization. This is of utmost importance, as it is the prerequisite for the derivation of their timing solutions. The latter would in turn allow a wealth of potential studies, such as probing the presence of a mass excess at the center of NGC 362, looking for optical and X-ray counterparts, studying the magnetic field at arcsecond scales, and more. These kinds of studies are only possible in clusters that host many pulsars. With its 12 pulsars, NGC 362 harbors a huge scientific potential, which we aim to unlock by characterizing its binaries. Moreover, we may discover additional pulsars thanks to fortuitous scintillation events.

records.title: Parkes observations for project P1411 semester 2026APRS_22
records.description: Conventional blind pulsar surveys that search for periodic signals in high-time-resolution data are increasingly limited by interstellar scattering at high dispersion measure (DM), orbital modulation in compact binaries, scintillation effects, and intensive computational demands. The Australian Square Kilometre Array Pathfinder (ASKAP) Evolutionary Map of the Universe (EMU) survey provides ultra-deep radio continuum maps enabling complementary image-domain pulsar searches that bypass these limitations. We have discovered seven new pulsars through three targeted strategies: (1) identifying compact sources embedded in supernova remnants (SNRs) and pulsar wind nebulae (PWNe), (2) detecting highly variable sources via variance imaging, and (3) selecting highly circularly polarised compact sources. Our sample includes three highly scattered pulsars (PSR J1638-4713 , PSR J1643-4511, and PSR J1631-4722 with DM > 800 pc/cm^3) including two pulsars associated with PWNe. Two millisecond pulsars (PSR J0927-7641 and PSR J1838-5949) are in potential wide binary systems with orbital periods of several tens of days, and two additional normal pulsars (PSR J1153-7106 and PSR 2223-0654). We propose follow-up timing observations of these pulsars with Murriyang's Ultra-Wideband Low (UWL) receiver to obtain phase-connected timing solutions, measure precise positions and spin parameters, and determine orbital characteristics for the binary systems,. These observations will enable studies of pulsar formation mechanisms, binary evolution pathways, PWN-SNR interactions, and validate image-based discovery techniques as powerful complements to traditional blind surveys for detecting elusive pulsars.

records.title: Parkes observations for project P1376 semester 2026APRS_01
records.description: Magnetars are highly magnetized neutron stars that exhibit diverse and often variable emission across the electromagnetic spectrum, including rare but exceptionally bright radio emission. However, their broadband radio spectra remain poorly characterized, with only a few sources studied in detail. Several radio magnetars show complex spectral structures, such as peaks at a few GHz and a few hundred GHz, and a dip around 20 to 50 GHz. These features are not yet fully accounted for in existing models of magnetar radio emission. We propose simultaneous observations of the radio magnetar 1E 1547.0-5408 using ATCA and Murriyang (Parkes). Our program will provide continuous frequency coverage from 0.7 to 96 GHz by combining Parkes' UWL receiver with ATCA's higher frequency bands. In addition, we plan to submit a complementary ALMA proposal to cover the 100 to 300 GHz range, enabling a complete view of the sub-millimeter component. This coordinated setup will allow us to accurately measure the broadband spectral shape, identify the locations of spectral peaks and dips, and probe the underlying magnetospheric emission mechanisms, providing strong constraints for theoretical modeling. Additionally, the Parkes observations will capture individual pulses from 1E 1547.0-5408, allowing us to compare their properties to those of SGR 1935+2154, a known Galactic FRB source, and explore potential links between other radio magnetars and FRBs. Following this initial campaign, we will propose a long-term wide-band monitoring program to track spectral evolution, as well as target-of-opportunity observations of other currently inactive radio magnetars, building toward a comprehensive understanding of the radio-emitting magnetar population.

records.title: Parkes observations for project P1375 semester 2026APRS_06
records.description: Rotating radio transients (RRATs) are Galactic neutron stars that emit sporadic radio pulses, and the question of whether apparently one-off sources truly repeat remains unresolved. With the discovery of numerous fast radio bursts (FRBs), the paradigm of 'one detection defines an astrophysical source' has shifted. However, the distinction between truly non-repeating Galactic transients and insufficiently observed repeating sources remains critical. Recent high-sensitivity follow-up observations with FAST have revealed that multiple apparent one-off RRATs originally detected by Parkes are in fact repeating sources, with fainter pulses hundreds of times weaker than their initial bright detections. This discovery raises a fundamental question: are many one-off RRATs simply the result of insufficient observational sensitivity, or do they represent intrinsically catastrophic transient events. We propose deep follow-up monitoring of four apparent one-off RRATs using the Parkes Ultra-Wideband receiver system, which offers 1.7-3.4 times higher sensitivity than the Multibeam discovery data. These observations will constrain the pulse repetition rates and energy distributions of these sources, examine the extreme variability seen in some RRATs and pulsars that exhibit pulses differing by >500 times in brightness, and test whether hidden repeating emission explains the apparent one-off nature of these sources.

records.title: GASKAP-HI Pilot Survey HI Absorption Spectra
records.description: A collection of neutral hydrogen (HI) absorption spectra produced from GASKAP-HI pilot phase I and II observations with the ASKAP telescope. The dataset contains 3219 sightlines across the Large (LMC) and Small Magellanic Clouds (SMC) and the Magellanic Bridge (MB) towards 1.4-GHz continuum sources. In addition, this dataset includes coverage of the Galactic foreground towards the Magellanic targets, covering the region of the Reticulum and Hydrus large-scale filaments. For each sightline we provide the HI absorption spectra in both native (0.24 km/s) and averaged (0.96 km/s) velocity resolution as well as matching HI emission spectra taken from the emission spectral line cubes produced from the same observations. We support these with plots of the spectra; index pages of all spectra, detections and low noise spectra; plus diagnostic plots showing source extents, pixel weight and moment 0 maps. The Magellanic and Galactic data sets are presented separately as they are based on different subsets of the total observations. For each of these data sets we provide a summary catalog for each of the native and averaged velocity resolution spectra. We also provide catalogues of the absorption features detected in the spectra. Lastly, we also provide more detailed analysis of the Magellanic Bridge spectra with a catalogue of MB spectra, spectra Gaussian fitting solutions, and catalogues of warm and cold neutral medium Gaussian components.

records.title: Parkes observations for project P1403 semester 2026APRS_01
records.description: PSR J1744-3922 is a mildly recycled pulsar in a compact binary system that exhibits properties distinct from those of typical millisecond pulsars (MSPs). With a relatively long spin period of 172 ms and a short orbital period of 4.6 h, this system is unusual compared to fully recycled MSPs and other mildly recycled pulsars. In addition to its atypical spin and orbital characteristics, PSR J1744-3922 displays variable radio emission coming from intra-binary propagation effects, although the physical mechanism responsible for this variability remains unclear. Classical eclipse signatures, such as strong dispersion measure variations or large time delays, are absent, raising the possibility of a more complex intra-binary propagation, absorption, or scattering environment. We propose a single continuous 10-h observation of PSR J1744-3922 using the Ultra-Wideband Low-frequency (UWL; 704-4032 MHz) receiver on the 64-m Murriyang (Parkes) radio telescope. The simultaneous, broad-band frequency coverage over more than two full orbital cycles will allow us to characterise the frequency- and phase-dependent behaviour of the radio emission, while polarimetric measurements will provide additional constraints on the nature of the intra-binary material.

records.title: Coupled Coastal Hazard Prediction System (CCHaPS) Climate Projections for Australia
records.description: CCHaPS, the Coupled Coastal Hazard Prediction System, is a 2D hydrodynamic and wave model (Semi-implicit Cross-scale Hydroscience Integrated System Model and Wind Wave Model III, SCHISM-WWMIII), configured around the Australian coastline including the Great Barrier Reef, and extending out to deep offshore waters or neighbouring landmasses. The model simulates water levels due to astronomical tides, weather, waves and aspects of wave-flow interaction over multiple decades, allowing for full consideration of the dynamics of extreme sea levels and waves in the Australian region, at high spatial resolution from ~7km off-shore down to ~250m at the coast, and ~100m in major river mouths. The model is run on an unstructured (triangular) grid comprising over 1.4 million nodes, which extends overland up to a 12m elevation contour, to enable modelling of inundation events and sea level rise. CCHaPS projections cover two 20-year periods: 1995 to 2014 (historical) and 2081 to 2100 (SSP3-7.0 emissions scenario). The projections are forced with two global GCMs (ACCESS-CM2 and EC-EARTH3) downscaled by two RCMs (BARPA and CCAM)* for winds and mean sea level pressure produced, water levels from Zhang et al's regional sea level projections, tides from TPXOv9.2, and spectral wave forcing from COWCLIP regional CMIP6 projections (see Lineage). The model used is SCHISM-WWMIII v5.9, using ST4 wave physics, run on NCI's Gadi supercomputer. The dataset comprises hourly netCDF data on an unstructured grid, compliant with CF, ACDD and UGRID metadata conventions. A notebook demonstrating how to interact with the data is attached under Supporting Documentation. Variables included are: depth (non-time varying), sea surface height, wet-dry node, currents, significant wave height, mean wave direction, peak wave direction, directional spreading, t01 and t02 mean wave period, peak wave period, peak directional spreading, peak direction (rad), and orbital velocity. The data is also stored on CSIRO infrastructure in the {ev-acs-wp3-cchaps} volume, and at NCI in /g/data/ia39/WP3/release/CCHaPS. Examples of how to work with the data in Python are provided in the accompanying notebook "CCHaPS_examples.ipynb" (see Supporting Documentation) A manuscript describing this dataset is in preparation and will be linked to this metadata record in due course. *due to an issue with CCAM's calendar implementation, EC-Earth3 downscaled by CCAM was not available to be run with SCHISM, so one RCM, BARPA, downscales both GCMs, while one GCM, ACCESS-CM2, has data downscaled by both RCMs. ERRATA: There are issues with dp_rad at 2091/06/26 14:00 and 2096/06/27 02:00

records.title: Soil thickness DSM data of the Flinders and Gilbert catchments Queensland 2026 Version 2, post the Flinders and Gilbert Agricultural Resource Assessment (FGARA)
records.description: Soil thickness is one of 18 attributes of soils chosen to underpin the Version 2 land suitability assessment of the Flinders and Gilbert catchments through the digital soil mapping process (DSM). This soil thickness raster data represents a modelled dataset of soil thickness presented as a positive number in meters eg a value of 1.12 shows the soil thickness is 1.12m deep and is derived from measured site data and environmental covariates. This data may underrepresent areas of soils deeper than 1.5m as the input data was mostly only recorded to a maximum of 1.5m where achievable being the extent of the hydraulic soil corer and the general agricultural soil depth. Soil thickness is a parameter used in land suitability assessment for plant edaphic requirements (root development and structural growth) and physical support and a component in other limitations including available water capacity (AWC). This raster data provides improved soil information used to underpin and identify opportunities and promote detailed investigation for a range of sustainable regional development options and was created within the ‘Land Suitability’ activity during the CSIRO SOGWRA. A companion dataset and statistics reflecting reliability of this data are also provided and can be found described in the lineage section of this metadata record. Processing information is supplied in ranger R scripts and attributes were modelled using a Random Forest approach. The DSM process is described in the CSIRO SOGWRA published report ‘Soils and land suitability for the Southern Gulf catchments’. A technical report from the CSIRO Southern Gulf Water Resource Assessment to the Government of Australia. The Assessment provides a comprehensive overview and integrated evaluation of the feasibility of aquaculture and agriculture development in the Southern Gulf catchments as well as the ecological, social and cultural (indigenous water values, rights and aspirations) impacts of development. Additional specific process notes are provided with the download data.

records.title: Contiguous suitable area data of the Flinders and Gilbert catchments Qld generated post the Flinders and Gilbert Agricultural Resource Assessment (FGARA)
records.description: These contiguous suitable area data are based on the version 2 land suitability data post the Flinders and Gilbert Agricultural Resource Assessment (FGARA). To address on-ground operational farming constraints imposed by parcels of suitable land being too small or oddly shaped according to natural variability of land, or physical limits on suitable farming land parcel sizes, contiguous suitable area data was generated. This contiguous suitable area data is based on crop-specific minimum areas and minimum length/width of contiguous suitable land and is produced as standalone data products for all crop groups. The rules are provided for download. The data was generated to remove the component of landscape complexity that natural distributions of soil and land variability and specific crop requirements produce. This data provides improved land evaluation information to identify opportunities and promote detailed investigation for a range of sustainable development options. The land suitability evaluation methods used to produce the underlying data are a modification of the Food and Agriculture Organisation (FAO) land evaluation approach. The land suitability analysis is described in full in the CSIRO SOGWRA published report ‘Soils and land suitability for the Southern Gulf catchments’. A technical report from the CSIRO Southern Gulf Water Resource Assessment to the Government of Australia. The naming convention for these data is; ‘crop group’ underscore ‘major crop’ underscore ‘season code’ underscore ‘irrigation type code’ underscore ‘catchment code’ underscore ‘data type’ eg ‘CG7_CottonGrains_D_Fw_G_ContigArea’ is Cotton and grain crops grown in the dry season with furrow irrigation in the Gilbert catchment contiguous suitable area data. The codes for season are; W – wet season; D – dry season; P – perennial. The codes for irrigation type are; S – overhead spray irrigation; T – trickle irrigation; Fd – flood irrigation; Fw – furrow irrigation; R – rainfed. It is important to emphasize that this is a regional-scale assessment: further data collection and detailed soil physical, chemical and nutrient analyses would be required to plan development at a scheme, enterprise or property scale. Several limitations that may have a bearing on land suitability were out of scope and not assessed as part of this activity (refer to the report), these limitations include biophysical and socio-cultural. For example these land suitability raster datasets do not include consideration of the licensing of water, flood risk, risk of irrigation induced secondary salinity, or land tenure and other legislative controls. Some of these may be addressed elsewhere in FGARA eg flooding was investigated by the Earth observation remote sensing group in the surface water activity. The Flinders and Gilbert Agricultural Resource Assessment provides a comprehensive overview and integrated evaluation of the feasibility of aquaculture and agriculture development in the Flinders and Gilbert catchments as well as the ecological, social and cultural (indigenous water values, rights and aspirations) impacts of development.

records.title: Versatile agricultural land spatial data of the Flinders and Gilbert catchments Qld generated post the Flinders and Gilbert Agricultural Resource Assessment (FGARA)
records.description: This versatile agricultural land data was prepared post FGARA 2013 and uses the Version 2 land suitability data 2024. The collection of five raster datasets (GeoTIFF format) is used to provide a synopsis of the land suitability data of the 21 crop groups and their specific irrigation management systems and seasons in the Flinders and Gilbert catchments Queensland. The definitive versatile agricultural land dataset (Ag_Versatility_14_Crops_S.tif) was determined by identifying where the largest number of 14 selected land management options were mapped as being suitable (i.e. suitability classes 1 to 3, refer to report cited with this metadata record). This analysis summarised the suitability of the selected land management options for each pixel, and highlights those pixels that are potentially more versatile for agricultural development because they are likely to suit a larger range of land management options and enterprises eg the score of zero represents the least versatile land, while the score of 14 represents the most versatile. The data values represent the number of land management options suitable for that pixel. The selected land management options were chosen to be relative to general potential agronomic experience and development aspirations of potential stakeholders in the catchments and were derived in consultation with the agricultural viability activity in the Southern Gulf Water Resource Assessment (SOGWRA) 2023. These selections are presented in Table 3-46 of the published report; ' Soils and land suitability for the Southern Gulf catchments’. A technical report from the CSIRO Southern Gulf Water Resource Assessment to the Government of Australia. Similarly, the selection of a different representative set from the land management options would result in a different versatility map outcome. In addition to the selected set of 14 land management options, versatile agricultural land is also presented using the subsets of each of the irrigation types (and rainfed cropping). In this case, the land management options were assigned to rainfed (8), furrow (17), spray (23) or trickle irrigation (10). The data values represent the number of land management options suitable for that pixel. Analytical products like these help to identify land where particular types of irrigation-related infrastructure investment may be best targeted. This data provides improved land evaluation information to identify opportunities and promote detailed investigation for a range of sustainable development options. It is important to emphasize that this is a regional-scale assessment: further data collection and detailed soil physical, chemical and nutrient analyses would be required to plan development at a scheme, enterprise or property scale. Several limitations that may have a bearing on land suitability were out of scope and not assessed as part of this activity (refer to the report), these limitations include biophysical and socio-cultural. For example these versatile agricultural land raster datasets do not include consideration of the licensing of water, flood risk, contiguous land, risk of irrigation induced secondary salinity, or land tenure and other legislative controls. Some of these may be addressed elsewhere in reports eg flooding was investigated by the Earth observation remote sensing group in the surface water activity. The Southern Gulf Water Resource Assessment and FGARA provides a comprehensive overview and integrated evaluation of the feasibility of aquaculture and agriculture development in the Flinders and Gilbert catchments Qld as well as the ecological, social and cultural (indigenous water values, rights and aspirations) impacts of development.

Data values are: 1 Very poorly drained, 2 Poorly drained, 3 Imperfectly drained, 4 Moderately well drained, 5 Well drained, 6 Rapidly drained. Soil drainage is a parameter used in land suitability assessments of soil wetness in combination with soil permeability indicating site and soil conditions that result in poor soil aeration for plant growth eg excess water on the soil surface or in the soil profile caused from inadequate site drainage reduces crop growth and quality and restricts machinery use. This raster data provides improved soil information used to underpin and identify opportunities and promote detailed investigation for a range of sustainable regional development options and was created within the ‘Land Suitability’ activity during the CSIRO SOGWRA. A companion dataset and statistics reflecting reliability of this data are also provided and can be found described in the lineage section of this metadata record. Processing information is supplied in ranger R scripts and attributes were modelled using a Random Forest approach. The DSM process is described in the CSIRO SOGWRA published report ‘Soils and land suitability for the Southern Gulf catchments’. records.title: Land suitability data of the Flinders and Gilbert catchments Queensland 2026 Version 2, post FGARA
records.description: These land suitability raster data (GeoTIFF format) indicates areas of potential suitability for 21 crop groups and their specific irrigation management systems and seasons in the Flinders and Gilbert catchments Queensland. This data provides improved land evaluation information to identify opportunities and promote detailed investigation for a range of sustainable development options and was created within the ‘Land suitability’ activity of the Northern Australia Water Resource Assessment projects. There are five land suitability classes coded 1-5. 1 – Highly suitable land with negligible limitations 2 – Suitable land with minor limitations 3 – Moderately suitable land with considerable limitations 4 – Currently unsuitable land with severe limitations and 5 – Unsuitable land with extreme limitations. The land suitability evaluation methods used to produce this data are a modification of the Food and Agriculture Organisation (FAO) land evaluation approach. The land suitability analysis is described in full in the CSIRO SOGWRA published report ‘Soils and land suitability for the Southern Gulf catchments’. A technical report from the CSIRO Southern Gulf Water Resource Assessment to the Government of Australia. Companion datasets showing the reliability of these suitability data (showing areas of the catchments where there is greater or lesser confidence in the accuracy of the suitability data) are also supplied. The naming convention for these data is; ‘crop group’ underscore ‘major crop’ underscore ‘season code’ underscore ‘irrigation type code’ underscore ‘catchments code’ underscore ‘data type’ eg ‘CG7_CottonGrains_D_Fw_S_Suit’ is Cotton and grain crops grown in the dry season with furrow irrigation in the Flinders and Gilbert catchments suitability data. The codes for season are; W – wet season; D – dry season; P – perennial. The codes for irrigation type are; S – overhead spray irrigation; T – trickle irrigation; Fd – flood irrigation; Fw – furrow irrigation; R – rainfed. The codes for data type are; suit – suitability data, CI – reliability data expressed as confusion index. It is important to emphasize that this is a regional-scale assessment: further data collection and detailed soil physical, chemical and nutrient analyses would be required to plan development at a scheme, enterprise or property scale. Several limitations that may have a bearing on land suitability were out of scope and not assessed as part of this activity (refer to the report), these limitations include biophysical and socio-cultural. For example these land suitability raster datasets do not include consideration of the licensing of water, flood risk, contiguous land, risk of irrigation induced secondary salinity, or land tenure and other legislative controls. Some of these may be addressed elsewhere in the NAWRA projects eg flooding was investigated by the Earth observation remote sensing group in the surface water activity. These Water Resource Assessments provide a comprehensive overview and integrated evaluation of the feasibility of aquaculture and agriculture development in the Flinders and Gilbert catchments Qld as well as the ecological, social and cultural (indigenous water values, rights and aspirations) impacts of development. These suitability raster datasets supersede the Version 1 FGARA land suitability data by using updated data and methods from recent Water Resource Assessments. Additional specific process notes are provided with the download data.

records.title: Parkes observations for project P1420 semester 2026APRS_06
records.description: We propose the pilot of a Murriyang CryoPAF Pulsar Survey of the Southern Galactic Plane (CPS-LowLat Pilot). The revolutionary CryoPAF receiver delivers the highest pulsar survey speed in the Southern Hemisphere, exceeding L-band capability of MeerKAT by ~2x, with a sufficiently low data rate to enable archiving and reprocessing essential to maximizing survey yields. Population synthesis predicts ~300 new pulsars in the full CPS-LowLat. Up to ~90 pulsars are predicted from this Pilot in a rich region of the Galactic Plane (-15deg < l < -10deg, |b| < 3deg), including 5-10 millisecond pulsars. 2.5-hr pointings are proposed to provide the requisite transformational pulsar detection rate, while maintaining sensitivity across a wide range of binary orbital periods, including ultra-compact systems. A frequency range of 1.3-1.85 GHz will mitigate dispersion smearing and scattering. Well-developed GPU-based searches for accelerated / binary systems and efficient coherent folding algorithms will be deployed. New discoveries from CPS-LowLat will enable strong-field tests of general relativity, equation-of-state constraints from massive neutron stars, more accurate modeling of the neutron star merger rate, and probes of exotic stellar-evolution pathways and of the ionised interstellar medium. Besides its impressive pulsar yield and the associated scientific possibilities, the proposed pilot will demonstrate the end-to-end performance of the CryoPAF for pulsar surveys prior to commencing the full CPS-LowLat, and validate pulsar population models.

records.title: Parkes observations for project P1402 semester 2026APRS_18
records.description: We propose a dedicated Parkes/Murriyang timing campaign of the newly confirmed narrow-duty cycle (~6 %) millisecond pulsar (MSP) PSR J2147-3604. This source was identified in a reprocessing of the Green Bank North Celestial Cap (GBNCC) survey as a high-confidence candidate with a spin period of 3.2 ms, and a dispersion measure, DM of 17 pc/cc. The pulsar was subsequently confirmed by the Fermi--TRAPUM collaboration via MeerKAT beamforming localisation and Parkes follow-up. Parkes/UWL observations allocated using green time detected this pulsar between 700--1500~MHz, and confirmed that it's in a binary system. Due to its low DM, we also detected strong interstellar scintillation. We request 35~hr of Murriyang time using the UWL receiver and APOLLO backend to obtain a phase-coherent timing solution and to characterise its spin, orbital, and propagation properties. Since the pulsar is also associated with a FERMI source, a precise radio ephemeris will also enable sensitive searches for gamma-ray pulsations in Fermi-LAT data and assess PSR J2147-3604's suitability for pulsar timing arrays (PTAs) and future gamma-ray timing applications.

records.title: Parkes observations for project P960 semester 2026APRS_07
records.description: We aim to carry out receiver pointing and characterisation tests of Parkes receivers. Typically, these tests are carried out after the receiver package is installed, but time does not always allow for proper characterisation. Receivers for consideration include UWL, MARS and 13MM packages. In addition to cross-referencing C007 for flux calibration via pointing, we aim to conduct gain-elevation and system temperature experiments using the Moon, to ensure users of the Parkes Observatory have the most accurate information available for calibration purposes.

records.title: Parkes observations for project P1317 semester 2026APRS_03
records.description: The existence of a population of millisecond pulsars (MSPs) in the Galactic bulge is supported, among others, by the Fermi GeV excess, a signal of gamma rays coming from the Galactic center (GC) direction and resembling the cumulative emission of known MSPs. In 2022, we were granted 20h of observations with the Green Bank Telescope to shed light onto the nature of 6 MSP candidates. We discovered two new MSPs, PSR J1740-28 and PSR J1740-2805, towards one of our targets, significantly increasing the number of highly-dispersed MSPs in the GC direction and probably unveiling the first direct evidence of a bulge MSP population. Data collected with the Murriyang telescope between 2023 and 2025 enabled us to obtain binary parameters for both pulsars and revealed that one of them is a black-widow candidate, associated with a circularly polarized source detected in MeerKAT data. Due to the faintness of the other pulsar, its position remains loosely constrained. We propose to continue regular timing observations of these pulsars with Murriyang, in order to constrain their parameter, study their long-term evolution, and rule out that they belong to a new globular cluster.

records.title: Parkes observations for project P595 semester 2026APRS_28
records.description: We propose to continue the PULSE@Parkes project in which high school students from Australia and around the World use the Parkes radio telescope in a remote observing model to observe and analyse pulsar data. The data from some PULSE@Parkes observations are used to support the space missions, other observations supplement the P456 Pulsar Timing Array project and the remainder were chosen in order to make a detailed analysis of pulsar timing irregularities and intermittency.

records.title: Parkes observations for project P1422 semester 2026APRS_15
records.description: Interplanetery Scintillation (IPS) is a powerful observing technique for measuring the size and structure of radio sources, as well as characterising solar wind turbulence. Murriyang was used for IPS in the 1960 and 1980s for IPS observations. However, with the the UWL's ultra-wide bandwidth, we believe that Murriyang IPS observations can once again provide a unique science opportunity. Recent observations with the Five-hundred-metre Aperture Spherical Telescope revealed an unexpected trend of scintillation timescale with frequency. Murriyang is the perfect instrument to corroborate this finding. Furthermore, we believe this effect is due to the inner scale of the turbulence, which can be uniquely probed with the high sensitivity and bandwidth of Murriyang in unprecedented detail, with a modest amount of observing time. As well as providing the most detailed study of the Heliosphere's inner scale yet, we can also determine if it can act as a new and direct probe of heliospheric density: an important complement to IPS and extremely useful for understanding the impact of the solar wind to pulsar DM variations. Finally, these observations will also provide useful insights for instrumental systematics on timescales rather longer than pulsar periods (1-10s) but similar to the timescales of the new class of Ultra-long period magnetars. Thus we can better understand whether Murriyang has a role to play in this important discovery space.

records.title: Metabolomics and lipidomics datasets for ontogenetic biochemical profiling of juvenile crown-of-thorns starfish
records.description: The datasets include polar metabolite and lipid profiles from juveniles aged 6 and 15 weeks, as well as 12, 15 and 27-30 months, supporting biochemical profiling from early post-settlement stages through to advanced herbivorous juvenile development. The collection supports investigation of age-related changes in juvenile physiology, biochemical pathways, sensory-associated molecules, lipid metabolism and the onset of toxicity-related processes, including saponin production. These data provide a resource for understanding crown-of-thorns starfish development and may support future applications in ecological monitoring, outbreak prediction and management of this coral predator.
