records.title: Long-term project observations for project L100 semester 2026APRS_08
records.description: We request time to observe 270 pulsars on a regular basis in order to achieve three main science goals. The first is to understand pulsars: how do they spin down and what disrupts this process, how and why their profiles vary with time, whether they precess or have planetary mass companions, in short all the things that make pulsar timing noisier than the perfect clock. Secondly we want to understand the interstellar medium of our Galaxy through repeated monitoring of dispersion measure, rotation measure and flux density variations in conjunction with scintillation parameters. Finally, we provide these data as a community service both to the high-energy community where we have strong collaborative links (particularly to Fermi) and to the radio pulsar astronomers generally through the CSIRO archive. The project is on-going since 2007, we are (co-)authors on 107 papers arising from the P574 data. The data have contributed to the PhD theses of students from Bordeaux, Manchester, Oxford, Stanford, and Swinburne. We are seeking long-term project status with a view to continuing the project into the SKA era.

records.title: Centroids with predictions: Anopheles farauti predicted abundance using hurdle model (Queensland, 5km grid)
records.description: This collection contains an fst file (centroids_5x5_qld_with_predictions_shiny-app.fst) used to reproduce the maps and analyses in manuscript "A hurdle modelling approach for estimating mosquito abundance: an Anopheles farauti case study", and to run the companion Shiny dashboard.

records.title: R code for hurdle modelling of Anopheles farauti abundance in Queensland, Australia
records.description: R code to reproduce the analyses in the manuscript "A hurdle modelling approach for estimating mosquito abundance: an Anopheles farauti case study". The software implements a two-stage (hurdle) framework that estimates the abundance of the malaria vector Anopheles farauti across Queensland, Australia. A boosted regression tree (BRT) species distribution model is fitted to presence-absence records and climate and landscape predictors to estimate habitat suitability. A random forest (RF) model then predicts longitudinal trap counts, conditional on suitability, using short-term (21-day) weather and landscape variables. Predicted counts are converted to abundance (using trap efficiency) and mapped across a 5 km grid for Queensland. The repository also includes zero-inflated count models for comparison and an interactive Shiny app for exploring the predicted suitability and abundance surfaces. The software was produced to provide spatially explicit, high-resolution abundance estimates for malaria risk assessment, vector surveillance planning and the design of targeted control, including as an input layer to gene drive release modelling for An. farauti. It is shared to make the analyses fully reproducible and to allow the framework to be applied to other vectors and regions.

records.title: Parkes observations for project P1419 semester 2026APRS_05
records.description: We propose a deep 100-hour Parkes radio pulsar survey of the Galactic plane region l = 240 ~ 260 deg, |b| < 2 deg, -a 80-square-degree zone currently unobserved by any major deep pulsar survey such as the Parkes Multibeam Pulsar Survey (PMPS) and The MPIfR-MeerKAT Galactic Plane Survey (MMGPS). This sightline probes the near side of the Perseus Arm (4~6 kpc), yet contains only 14 known pulsars, likely incomplete due to the shallow integrations and FFT-limited pipelines of prior work. Using the CryoPAF receiver (1100 ~ 1700 MHz, 600 MHz bandwidth) with 3000-second pointings and a Fast Folding Algorithm (FFA)-enhanced search, we will detect long-period (P=1~10s) and high-DM (< 350 pc cm ^-3) pulsars missed previously. We expect to discover 20 ~ 40 new pulsars, enabling precise mapping of the local electron density and testing Galactic ISM models. Critically, our field contains the unassociated Fermi sources , offering a prime opportunity for multiwavelength identification. The survey will also probe transient phenomena via single-pulse searches. This project addresses a well-defined observational gap with high discovery potential for both Galactic structure and high-energy astrophysics.

records.title: Parkes observations for project P1365 semester 2026APRS_11
records.description: Following the successful demonstration of a pilot first-pass (shallow) search of a small fraction of the sky, the second-pass processing has commenced for the SMART pulsar survey, which involves deep searches of 80-minute observations. Over the past year, this second-pass processing has led to the discovery of 16 new pulsars (including two millisecond pulsars), bringing the total number of SMART discoveries to 20 when combined with the first-pass results. These outcomes hint at the exciting promise of this first southern-sky pulsar survey in the frequency band of SKA-Low. All new pulsars require timing observations to determine their spin and astrometric parameters. Another important aspect of timing newly discovered pulsars is to identify specialised targets for further detailed follow-ups. Since the MWA no longer supports routine pulsar observations from 2025, timing follow-ups rely on other telescopes. The Parkes Murriyang telescope, with an identical sky coverage, sensitivity and the wide frequency coverage, offers the best option to time SMART discoveries. We have demonstrated Murriyang's suitability for this through previous semesters and are now extending the project to a sample of 11 pulsars, including six from the last semester. The data will also allow us to study pulse profiles, polarisation, and flux densities from ~100 MHz to 4 GHz. The analysis/results will be included in a publication in preparation that will detail the deep-search pipeline and report on initial pulsar discoveries.

records.title: Parkes observations for project P1413 semester 2026APRS_18
records.description: We request 75 hours of Parkes observing time for dedicated radio follow-up observations of PSR J1635-5134, a promising candidate pulsar-subdwarf B (sdB) star binary system. PSR J1635-5134 is a non-recycled 340 ms pulsar in a nearly circular 18-hour orbit with a minimum companion mass of 0.26 solar mass. It lies in a sparsely populated region of binary-pulsars parameter space and may represent a short-lived evolutionary stage immediately following inefficient spin-up, thereby providing a missing link between canonical binaries and the millisecond pulsar-WD population. The system exhibits peculiar, orbital-phase-dependent dispersion-measure (DM) variability, with DM variations exceeding 30 pc/cc, indicating substantial ionised material plausibly associated with an outflow from the companion. Moreover, during prior monitoring with Parkes, the DM variations shifted from being predominantly modest to being persistently large, implying an evolving plasma environment that cannot be characterised with sparse or irregular observations. Determining whether these high-DM variations are intermittent or long-lived, and mapping how the excess material varies with orbital phase and epoch, are essential for constraining the origin and geometry of the plasma and for testing the hypothesis that an sdB wind supplies the required electron column. Through this proposal, we aim to (i) extend the timing baseline to improve astrometric precision to sub-arcsecond accuracy, enabling secure identification of the optical counterpart in a crowded field, and (ii) perform phase-targeted observations during eclipse/DM variation phases to understand the temporal behavior of excess DM.

records.title: Parkes observations for project P1416 semester 2026APRS_03
records.description: Radio pulsars in orbit around high-mass stellar companions offer a rich source of extreme physics for both observational astronomers and theorists alike. Despite being discovered 25 years ago, PSR J1638-4725 remains a veritable mystery compared to similar pulsar binary systems. Long-term monitoring has revealed extended `eclipses' where the pulsar is undetectable for months around periastron at GHz frequencies, along with intense variations in the observed pulsar dispersion measure, scatter broadening and flux density throughout the entire orbit. Preliminary spectroscopic characterisation of the companion star suggests it may be an O/B star, albiet one without a circumstellar disc of ejected material. This raises the unique opportunity to answer test the structure and origin of the near-wind regime of high-mass stars. In this proposal we will conduct an ambitious monitoring campaign of PSR J1638-4725 with both the ultra-wideband low and MARS recievers on Murriyang. We will track changes in the pulsar dispersion and scattering as it swings around the companion star, providing unique insights into the density and temperature distribution of the stellar wind from the companion star before and after the pulsar swings through periastron. These observations will also play a pivotal role in a broader multi-wavelength campaign to fully capture the upcoming 2026 periastron passage.

records.title: Long-term project observations for project L133 semester 2026APRS_04
records.description: This project is to continue timing and profile studies of the first double-pulsar system, a unique laboratory for gravitational physics. Important results published in our 53-page Phys. Rev. X paper (2021) include the first measurements of higher-order light-propagation effects and of the relativistic deformation of the orbit and highlight the importance of a long term observational campaign, including VLBI observations, for this remarkable system. The main aims of this proposal are to provide the strongest tests to date for general relativity and to measure for the first time the moment-of-inertia of a neutron star. Additionally, we will determine the system geometry, map the pulsar beams via geodetic precession, and search for the reappearance of Pulsar B. We exploit the high sensitivity and broad bandwidth of the UWL receiver. We are collaborating with the MeerKAT Double Pulsar Timing team to optimise combination of MeerKAT and UWL data.

records.title: Parkes observations for project P1054 semester 2026APRS_24
records.description: With this proposal we ask time to continue our timing follow-up campaign of pulsars discovered with the MeerKAT telescope. Fiftythree sources have been discovered in targeted observations of Fermi unidentified point sources, two towards Supernova Remnants, 27 in the Magellanic Clouds, 109 in Globular Clusters and 96 in a survey of the Galactic plane. A large fraction of the new discoveries are recycled pulsars (including a few relativistic systems, a pulsar with a planetary companion and several 'spider' binaries), or young pulsars. Timing observations have an essential role in exploiting the full potential of any pulsar discovery, allowing for the precise measurement of rotational, astrometric and orbital parameters which, in turn, give us powerful tools to improve our understanding of the physics in extreme environments as well as of the population of neutron stars as a whole. The UWL receiver of the Parkes telescope is a sensitive, versatile instrument that is allowing us to successfully time these new sources, in the bright-end of TRAPUM discoveries.

records.title: Parkes observations for project P1183 semester 2026APRS_08
records.description: After nearly four years of monitoring with both the Parkes and FAST telescopes, FRB 20220529 has been established as an extremely active repeater. It exhibits one of the longest known activity durations and shows evidence for a potential periodicity. Owing to the frequent observations carried out with Parkes and FAST, two abrupt rotation-measure (RM) flares have been detected in this source. These constitute the first RM flares ever observed in a fast radio burst (FRB), indicating that a dense, magnetised plasma clump passed across the line of sight. The second RM flare in particular makes a binary-origin scenario for FRB 20220529 especially compelling. If confirmed, the periodicity and RM flares would mutually reinforce one another, serving as a smoking gun for a binary origin. Previous analyses have shown that observations from both Parkes and FAST are essential. FAST's exceptional sensitivity enables the detection of many bursts, whereas the Parkes UWL receiver provides a stable burst-detection rate even during low-activity phases. To further investigate FRB 20220529, we have scheduled regular FAST observations every fortnight. We therefore propose to continue monitoring FRB 20220529 with the Parkes UWL receiver as well. The FAST and Parkes sessions are expected to be separated by a few days, ideally about one week. A cadence of approximately one week offers an excellent opportunity to capture detailed structure during the onset of RM decreases, as demonstrated by previous monitoring.

records.title: Parkes observations for project P1411 semester 2026APRS_24
records.description: Conventional blind pulsar surveys that search for periodic signals in high-time-resolution data are increasingly limited by interstellar scattering at high dispersion measure (DM), orbital modulation in compact binaries, scintillation effects, and intensive computational demands. The Australian Square Kilometre Array Pathfinder (ASKAP) Evolutionary Map of the Universe (EMU) survey provides ultra-deep radio continuum maps enabling complementary image-domain pulsar searches that bypass these limitations. We have discovered seven new pulsars through three targeted strategies: (1) identifying compact sources embedded in supernova remnants (SNRs) and pulsar wind nebulae (PWNe), (2) detecting highly variable sources via variance imaging, and (3) selecting highly circularly polarised compact sources. Our sample includes three highly scattered pulsars (PSR J1638-4713 , PSR J1643-4511, and PSR J1631-4722 with DM > 800 pc/cm^3) including two pulsars associated with PWNe. Two millisecond pulsars (PSR J0927-7641 and PSR J1838-5949) are in potential wide binary systems with orbital periods of several tens of days, and two additional normal pulsars (PSR J1153-7106 and PSR 2223-0654). We propose follow-up timing observations of these pulsars with Murriyang's Ultra-Wideband Low (UWL) receiver to obtain phase-connected timing solutions, measure precise positions and spin parameters, and determine orbital characteristics for the binary systems,. These observations will enable studies of pulsar formation mechanisms, binary evolution pathways, PWN-SNR interactions, and validate image-based discovery techniques as powerful complements to traditional blind surveys for detecting elusive pulsars.

records.title: Long-term project observations for project L126 semester 2026APRS_14
records.description: We propose a modest program to continue monitoring 4 of the 6 known radio magnetars in order to achieve three primary science goals. The first is to characterise magnetar outbursts over long timescales, for which tracking their rotational, flux density, and polarisation properties provide a clear view of the impulse response of their magnetic fields. Second, understanding the links between magnetars the mysterious fast radio burst phenomenon through the discovery of rare emission and propagation effects, shared spectro-temporal phenomenology, and connections to high-energy (X-ray/gamma-ray) phenomena. Lastly, our continued monitoring has enormous benefit to the wider magnetar community, providing rapid alerts to changes in activity, adding context to unusual behaviour detected by high-energy observations, and a host of supplementary science through the teams extensive collaborative networks. The project and its precursors have been running since 2007 and have contributed to 22 publications since then. This is the first submission since the project was converted to long-term status.

records.title: Parkes observations for project P960 semester 2026APRS_08
records.description: We aim to carry out receiver pointing and characterisation tests of Parkes receivers. Typically, these tests are carried out after the receiver package is installed, but time does not always allow for proper characterisation. Receivers for consideration include UWL, MARS and 13MM packages. In addition to cross-referencing C007 for flux calibration via pointing, we aim to conduct gain-elevation and system temperature experiments using the Moon, to ensure users of the Parkes Observatory have the most accurate information available for calibration purposes.

records.title: Parkes observations for project P1411 semester 2026APRS_23
records.description: Conventional blind pulsar surveys that search for periodic signals in high-time-resolution data are increasingly limited by interstellar scattering at high dispersion measure (DM), orbital modulation in compact binaries, scintillation effects, and intensive computational demands. records.title: Parkes observations for project P1398 semester 2026APRS_08
records.description: Low-frequency (< ~1 GHz) Galactic-plane pulsar surveys are strongly limited by sky background noise, interstellar scattering, and dispersion smearing, leading to an incomplete census of the pulsar population. High-frequency (> 2 GHz) observations mitigate these effects and have recently enabled the discovery of pulsars that remain undetectable at low-frequency. We analyzed archival data from the 2008 Parkes 6.5-GHz pulsar survey using modern search techniques. This reprocessing has revealed four previously unknown millisecond pulsar candidates with spin periods of 3-11 ms and dispersion measures of 20-170 pc/cc. Two candidates exhibit significant line-of-sight acceleration, indicating likely membership in compact binary systems. We request a total of 8.4 hours of follow-up observations with the Parkes (Murriyang) Ultra-Wideband Low (UWL) receiver to confirm these candidates and characterize their emission across 704-4032 MHz. Confirming these sources would expand the population of high-frequency selected pulsars and demonstrate the continued importance of high-frequency searches for uncovering exotic systems obscured in conventional low-frequency surveys.

records.title: Data Assessment Framework - Template (v1.2)
records.description: MS Excel tool for undertaking a data assessment according to the Data Assessment Framework (https://doi.org/10.25919/bp0y-av75)

records.title: Methane Emissions in Melbourne, Australia: Prior Estimates using Global and National Data
records.description: This collection contains the datasets developed and used in: Shahrokhi et al. (2026a), Methane Emissions in Melbourne, Australia; Part 1: Prior Estimates Using Global and National Data. Shahrokhi et al. (2026b), Methane Emissions in Melbourne, Australia; Part 2: Improving Prior Estimates Using Synthesis Inversion. The collection includes the following datasets. Emission Data: "Sectoral Methane Emissions Victoria and Melbourne.nc" contains gridded annual methane emissions for the state of Victoria with greater detail for Melbourne from 19 emission sectors, together with total methane emissions, across the modelling domain. Emissions are provided in units of kt/year on 3 km × 3 km grids. The modelling domain covers the state of Victoria and northern Tasmania, Australia (see the Location Details map). "Agriculture Emissions Australia.nc" contains gridded annual methane emissions from the agricultural sector across Australia. Emissions are provided in units of kg/s on approximately 1 km × 1 km grids. This dataset was derived using the Australian livestock distribution dataset developed by Navarro and Marcos Martinez (2021; subsequently updated by the authors in 2025), together with sector-specific methane emission factors. Further details on the methodology are provided in Shahrokhi et al. (2026a). Grid Information: "GRIDCRO2D_0" and "GRIDDOT2D_0" provide the spatial grid information for the modelling domain, including grid row and column indices, latitude, and longitude coordinates corresponding to the 3 km x 3 km modelling grid. Modelled Data: "Modelled Data – Meteorology and Mole Fractions.csv" contains hourly averaged output from the offline WRF–CMAQ forward model for January–June 2023. The data were extracted for the Melbourne observation sites (Aspendale, Bangholme, Clayton and Parkville) and the regional background site at Kennaook/Cape Grim, Tasmania. The file includes meteorological variables and methane mole fractions attributed to each of the 19 emission sectors presented in the emission files. Wind speed is reported in m/s, wind direction in degrees, planetary boundary layer (PBL) height in metres, and methane mole fractions for each sector in parts per billion (ppb).

records.title: Global Petrophysical Database
records.description: The Global Petrophysical Database (GPD) is a global compilation of petrophysical properties for a wide range of rock types, obtained using a variety of in-situ and laboratory measurement techniques. Properties include porosity, density, permeability/hydraulic conductivity, diffusion coefficients, tortuosity, thermal conductivity, specific heat capacity and radiogenic heat production. Mechanical properties are not currently included. The GPD incorporates data from several pre-existing databases (covering more than 500 publications) and more than 50 individual publications. The data can be used and analysed in many ways, such as identifying depth trends or correlations between parameters. The data may be useful for a wide range of geoscientific applications, including hydrogeology, mineral exploration, geothermal studies, petroleum geology, CO2 geosequestration, H2 storage, waste disposal and contaminant dispersal studies. The dataset is provided in the form of a spreadsheet and CSV files corresponding to each worksheet.

records.title: Sea Change Australia: Climate Report Cards
records.description: Sea Change Australia Climate report cards for multiple jurisdictions: WA, NT, QLD, NSW, SA, and TAS/VIC. Two versions are provided: reports for 2025 and reports for 2026.

records.title: Parkes observations for project P1344 semester 2026APRS
records.description: Fast radio bursts (FRBs) are millisecond-duration radio bursts of extragalactic origin. Since the discovery of the first FRB in the archival Parkes/Murriyang multibeam data, a broad dichotomy in population has emerged. Some FRBs have been seen to be repeating, while others are not, despite a significant amount of follow-up using different radio telescopes. The commissioning of new dedicated FRB detection systems has led to an exponential increase in the detected FRBs over the last decade. Despite >700 FRBs published to date, there is still a lack of understanding about the physical mechanisms through which FRB emission is produced. Due to the possibility of detecting multiple bursts from the same source in a repeating FRB, it forms an ideal sample set to uncover the physics of the source (e.g., emission mechanism, progenitor surrounding media), and test possible progenitor models. The coherent upgrade to the FRB detection system to ASKAP is expected to detect ~1 FRB/week. However, due to the limited fractional bandwidth available with ASKAP and survey nature of the telescope, probing the spectro-polarimetric characteristics of repeating sources is non-optimal. Hence, the large bandwidth offered by the ultra wideband-low (UWL) on Parkes/Murriyang is an ideal instrument to follow-up repeating FRB sources discovered through CRACO. We propose using the unallocated time/Green Time on UWL to follow up repeater-like sources to study their wideband spectro-polarimetric characteristics.

records.title: Parkes observations for project P595 semester 2026APRS_29
records.description: We propose to continue the PULSE@Parkes project in which high school students from Australia and around the World use the Parkes radio telescope in a remote observing model to observe and analyse pulsar data. The data from some PULSE@Parkes observations are used to support the space missions, other observations supplement the P456 Pulsar Timing Array project and the remainder were chosen in order to make a detailed analysis of pulsar timing irregularities and intermittency.

records.title: Parkes observations for project P1419 semester 2026APRS_06
records.description: We propose a deep 100-hour Parkes radio pulsar survey of the Galactic plane region l = 240 ~ 260 deg, |b| < 2 deg, -a 80-square-degree zone currently unobserved by any major deep pulsar survey such as the Parkes Multibeam Pulsar Survey (PMPS) and The MPIfR-MeerKAT Galactic Plane Survey (MMGPS). This sightline probes the near side of the Perseus Arm (4~6 kpc), yet contains only 14 known pulsars, likely incomplete due to the shallow integrations and FFT-limited pipelines of prior work. Using the CryoPAF receiver (1100 ~ 1700 MHz, 600 MHz bandwidth) with 3000-second pointings and a Fast Folding Algorithm (FFA)-enhanced search, we will detect long-period (P=1~10s) and high-DM (< 350 pc cm ^-3) pulsars missed previously. We expect to discover 20 ~ 40 new pulsars, enabling precise mapping of the local electron density and testing Galactic ISM models. Critically, our field contains the unassociated Fermi sources , offering a prime opportunity for multiwavelength identification. The survey will also probe transient phenomena via single-pulse searches. This project addresses a well-defined observational gap with high discovery potential for both Galactic structure and high-energy astrophysics.

records.title: Long-term project observations for project L147 semester 2026APRS_05
records.description: We propose to carry out a deep Galactic Bulge pulsar survey (GBps), covering the core of the Bulge region using the new cryoPAF system on Murriyang, the Parkes radio telescope. Such a deep survey is expected to discover a population of millisecond pulsars in the Galactic Bulge and reveal their distribution and gamma-ray emissions. With these, we will lead pioneering studies on the origin of gamma-ray emission in the Galactic Bulge, a longstanding mystery in modern astronomy. The outcome of this project will significantly advance our knowledge of the formation and evolution of millisecond pulsars in the Galactic Bulge, the origin and properties of high-energy emissions, and the nature of dark matter annihilation in the Galactic Centre. A total of 200 observations with the cryoPAF is required to cover a 400 square degree region (|gl|<10 deg, |gb|<10 deg). The survey is expected to be carried out over four semesters, from April 2026 to October 2027.

records.title: Parkes observations for project P1365 semester 2026APRS_12
records.description: Following the successful demonstration of a pilot first-pass (shallow) search of a small fraction of the sky, the second-pass processing has commenced for the SMART pulsar survey, which involves deep searches of 80-minute observations. Over the past year, this second-pass processing has led to the discovery of 16 new pulsars (including two millisecond pulsars), bringing the total number of SMART discoveries to 20 when combined with the first-pass results. These outcomes hint at the exciting promise of this first southern-sky pulsar survey in the frequency band of SKA-Low. All new pulsars require timing observations to determine their spin and astrometric parameters. Another important aspect of timing newly discovered pulsars is to identify specialised targets for further detailed follow-ups. Since the MWA no longer supports routine pulsar observations from 2025, timing follow-ups rely on other telescopes. The Parkes Murriyang telescope, with an identical sky coverage, sensitivity and the wide frequency coverage, offers the best option to time SMART discoveries. We have demonstrated Murriyang's suitability for this through previous semesters and are now extending the project to a sample of 11 pulsars, including six from the last semester. The data will also allow us to study pulse profiles, polarisation, and flux densities from ~100 MHz to 4 GHz. The analysis/results will be included in a publication in preparation that will detail the deep-search pipeline and report on initial pulsar discoveries.

records.title: Long-term project observations for project L124 semester 2026APRS_08
records.description: We propose a long-term project to monitor a very active repeater, FRB 20190520B, with Murriyang's UWL system. Our previous observations show that FRB 20190520B is not only among the most active FRBs that can be observed with Murriyang, but also shows extreme rotation measure (RM) and dispersion measure (DM) evolution, along with distinctive behavior at 3GHz frequency. This makes the UWL receiver uniquely suited for detailed studies and long-term monitoring of this repeating FRB. Through this program, we anticipate detecting a large sample of bursts from this FRB. In collaboration with FAST, we aim to investigate the time evolution of various properties of FRB 20190520B, enhance our understanding of polarisation across an extremely wide bandwidth with high sensitivity, and gain deeper insights into the local environment and emission mechanisms of FRBs.

records.title: Parkes observations for project P1402 semester 2026APRS_19
records.description: We propose a dedicated Parkes/Murriyang timing campaign of the newly confirmed narrow-duty cycle (~6 %) millisecond pulsar (MSP) PSR J2147-3604. This source was identified in a reprocessing of the Green Bank North Celestial Cap (GBNCC) survey as a high-confidence candidate with a spin period of 3.2 ms, and a dispersion measure, DM of 17 pc/cc. The pulsar was subsequently confirmed by the Fermi--TRAPUM collaboration via MeerKAT beamforming localisation and Parkes follow-up. Parkes/UWL observations allocated using green time detected this pulsar between 700--1500~MHz, and confirmed that it's in a binary system. Due to its low DM, we also detected strong interstellar scintillation. We request 35~hr of Murriyang time using the UWL receiver and APOLLO backend to obtain a phase-coherent timing solution and to characterise its spin, orbital, and propagation properties. Since the pulsar is also associated with a FERMI source, a precise radio ephemeris will also enable sensitive searches for gamma-ray pulsations in Fermi-LAT data and assess PSR J2147-3604's suitability for pulsar timing arrays (PTAs) and future gamma-ray timing applications.

records.title: Long-term project observations for project L100 semester 2026APRS_09
records.description: We request time to observe 270 pulsars on a regular basis in order to achieve three main science goals. The first is to understand pulsars: how do they spin down and what disrupts this process, how and why their profiles vary with time, whether they precess or have planetary mass companions, in short all the things that make pulsar timing noisier than the perfect clock. Secondly we want to understand the interstellar medium of our Galaxy through repeated monitoring of dispersion measure, rotation measure and flux density variations in conjunction with scintillation parameters. Finally, we provide these data as a community service both to the high-energy community where we have strong collaborative links (particularly to Fermi) and to the radio pulsar astronomers generally through the CSIRO archive. The project is on-going since 2007, we are (co-)authors on 107 papers arising from the P574 data. The data have contributed to the PhD theses of students from Bordeaux, Manchester, Oxford, Stanford, and Swinburne. We are seeking long-term project status with a view to continuing the project into the SKA era.

records.title: Parkes observations for project P1032 semester 2026APRS_11
records.description: With this proposal, we aim to continue P1032, the rapid measurements of relativistic parameters of southern binary pulsar systems using data from the Parkes Ultra Wideband Low (UWL) receiver. As the MeerTime project at the MeerKAT radio telescope ended in early 2024, observations with the UWL receiver now form the backbone for extending the timing baselines of many pulsars that have been part of this project. Since the source selection in the previous semesters was tailored such that the UWL receiver is the most (versatile and) suited instrument to achieve the proposed scientific goals for the chosen pulsars, we propose to continue these observations. We will use the UWL data to obtain significant orbital coverage and timing baselines on these pulsars and obtain important constraints on orbital and temporal DM variations that will help in identifying the nature of the companion stars. Increasing the number of measured Neutron Star (NS) masses, as well as improving on current constraints has profound implications for NS internal structure and for stellar and binary evolution physics.

records.title: Long-term project observations for project L101 semester 2026APRS_05
records.description: The Parkes Pulsar Timing Array (PPTA) project has three primary goals: (a) detection of gravitational waves from astronomical sources, (b) establishment of a pulsar timescale, and (c) improvement of our understanding of Solar-system dynamics. We are now in an exciting regime where a signal detected in our (and other data sets) has the form expected for a gravitational wave background. We, along with the international community, are now working hard to either confirm or deny this result, and to determine the astrophysical origin of this signal. With this proposal, we aim to maintain our pre-eminent position in the field. This is a continuing proposal for which observations of millisecond pulsars (MSPs) will continue to improve bounds on ultra-low-frequency gravitational waves until they are detected with confidence. Continued Parkes observations will remain valuable at least until the first stage of the SKA is able to improve on our sensitivity and observing cadence. Even after the gravitational wave background is detected, continued observations will resolve the background origin and individual sources will be identified; advancing the nascent field of gravitational wave astronomy.

records.title: Parkes observations for project P1416 semester 2026APRS_04
records.description: Radio pulsars in orbit around high-mass stellar companions offer a rich source of extreme physics for both observational astronomers and theorists alike. Despite being discovered 25 years ago, PSR J1638-4725 remains a veritable mystery compared to similar pulsar binary systems. Long-term monitoring has revealed extended `eclipses' where the pulsar is undetectable for months around periastron at GHz frequencies, along with intense variations in the observed pulsar dispersion measure, scatter broadening and flux density throughout the entire orbit. Preliminary spectroscopic characterisation of the companion star suggests it may be an O/B star, albiet one without a circumstellar disc of ejected material. This raises the unique opportunity to answer test the structure and origin of the near-wind regime of high-mass stars. In this proposal we will conduct an ambitious monitoring campaign of PSR J1638-4725 with both the ultra-wideband low and MARS recievers on Murriyang. We will track changes in the pulsar dispersion and scattering as it swings around the companion star, providing unique insights into the density and temperature distribution of the stellar wind from the companion star before and after the pulsar swings through periastron. These observations will also play a pivotal role in a broader multi-wavelength campaign to fully capture the upcoming 2026 periastron passage.

records.title: Long-term project observations for project L125 semester 2026APRS_21
records.description: The atomic interstellar medium shows tiny-scale optical depth fluctuations on the scale of 0.1~10,000 AU, whose origin and nature are poorly understood. The existence of this Tiny-Scale Atomic Structure (TSAS) has significant implications, potentially calling into question our fundamental understanding of heating, cooling and dynamical processes in the interstellar medium. Yet observations remain sparse. This long-term project plans to search for temporal variations in HI absorption spectra seen against background pulsars to characterise TSAS in the Milky Way interstellar medium (ISM). These observations constitute the largest number of sightlines and densest temporal sampling ever performed in a single experiment, and will test predictions that TSAS is the tail end of a turbulent cascade, constrain its minimum size scale (down to resolutions of ~0.05 AU) and potentially provide the first direct measurements of pressures in "large" TSAS features of > 1000 AU. We make use of the phase-resolved spectral line mode that we have recently implemented on Parkes, which has cut data rates and processing times by factors of ~1000 compared to past studies. This is an expansion of our pilot P1321 to a long term study.

records.title: Integrated Exposure, Health and Nest Environment Data for Nesting Green Turtles from the Southern Gulf of Carpentaria
records.description: This collection brings together multi‑disciplinary datasets generated to assess environmental exposure, physiological condition, maternal transfer, and nest environments of nesting green turtles (Chelonia mydas) from two remote island rookeries in the southern Gulf of Carpentaria, Australia. Data were collected across two consecutive nesting seasons and include chemical exposure measurements, functional omics profiles, and nest microbiome characterisation. Collectively, these datasets establish an integrated baseline for ecosurveillance in a minimally disturbed tropical marine system and support future assessments of cumulative stressors, environmental change and wildlife health. The collection is organised into sub-folders covering (1) metabolomic, lipidomic and proteomic profiles, (2) per‑ and polyfluoroalkyl substances and trace metal concentrations, and (3) bacterial and fungal community composition of turtle nest sands.

records.title: Synthetic Tropical Cyclone SCHISM-WWMIII Simulations for Queensland
records.description: Numerical model simulations of 1500 synthetic tropical cyclones, carried out with the coupled hydrodynamic-waves SCHISM-WWMIII model for the Queensland region. This dataset contains the full SCHISM-WWMIII output from each TC simulation in a single netCDF file (outputs/schout_1.nc), with the tide-only elevation counterpart ( outputs/schout_1_tide_only.nc). Storm surge is calculated as the elevation difference between these, and stored in storm_surge.nc files. Additionally, time-maximum fields of storm surge and significiant wave height are stored in and max_storm_surge.nc and max_hs.nc respectively. The dataset does not contain config or sflux files, but the unstructured model grid .gr3 file is included. There is an example in the notebook found under "Supporting Documentation" of which contains the code necessary to reproduce the wind and pressure fields used to drive each TC simulation. There are sister datasets to this publication for WA and Northern Australia.

records.description: Numerical model simulations of 2000 synthetic tropical cyclones (TCs), carried out with the coupled hydrodynamic-waves SCHISM-WWMIII model for the Western Australia region. This dataset contains the full SCHISM-WWMIII output from each TC simulation in a single netCDF file (outputs/schout_1.nc), with the tide-only elevation counterpart ( outputs/schout_1_tide_only.nc). Storm surge is calculated as the elevation difference between these, and stored in storm_surge.nc files. Additionally, time-maximum fields of storm surge and significiant wave height are stored in and max_storm_surge.nc and max_hs.nc respectively. The dataset does not contain config or sflux files, but the unstructured model grid .gr3 file is included. records.title: Multi-omics Datasets from Freshwater Turtle Organs for PFAS Exposure Assessment
records.description: This collection contains metabolomics, lipidomics and proteomics datasets generated from organs of freshwater turtles sampled to investigate the biological effects of per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS). The datasets comprise untargeted metabolite, lipid and protein profiles from multiple turtle organs, providing a comprehensive multi-omics resource for assessing PFAS exposure, bioaccumulation and associated biological responses. The collection supports investigation of molecular pathways affected by PFAS contamination, including energy metabolism, lipid regulation, protein expression, oxidative stress and other physiological processes relevant to environmental health. These datasets provide a valuable resource for understanding contaminant impacts in freshwater turtles and support environmental risk assessment, ecotoxicology research and wildlife conservation efforts.

records.title: GenCost project data
records.description: This repository provides data from the GenCost project. The GenCost project is a collaboration between CSIRO and AEMO, together with stakeholder input, to deliver an annual process of updating electricity generation and storage costs. Each report incorporates updated current and future cost estimates and global electricity scenarios.

records.title: PI-CFM dataset for generated soft gripper
records.description: PI-CFM Soft Gripper-Design Dataset — A collection of soft-gripper designs and their simulated grasp performance, produced by the PI-CFM (physics-informed conditional flow-matching) model. Each design is a standalone design_{idx:07d}.npz holding the geometry mask, the latent genome that regenerates it, and 11 simulation metrics (pull-off force, contact arc/wrap, displacement, buckling bounds, etc.), plus source provenance.

records.title: Simple Electricity Model
records.description: Simple Electricity Model (SEM) was designed to be the simplest electricity model that could be used to reliably project the future National Electricity Market (NEM) generation mix and average cost of generation, calculating results within no more than 1 hour. In making this model available the objective is to provide more transparency around how estimates of the future cost of generation are calculated. The collection includes model data and software files. The software files themselves are not capable of running the model. Users must obtain licences to the underlying software environment which is available from external parties. See the user guide provided for more details.

records.title: Long-term project observations for project L101 semester 2026APRS_06
records.description: The Parkes Pulsar Timing Array (PPTA) project has three primary goals: (a) detection of gravitational waves from astronomical sources, (b) establishment of a pulsar timescale, and (c) improvement of our understanding of Solar-system dynamics. We are now in an exciting regime where a signal detected in our (and other data sets) has the form expected for a gravitational wave background. We, along with the international community, are now working hard to either confirm or deny this result, and to determine the astrophysical origin of this signal. With this proposal, we aim to maintain our pre-eminent position in the field. This is a continuing proposal for which observations of millisecond pulsars (MSPs) will continue to improve bounds on ultra-low-frequency gravitational waves until they are detected with confidence. Continued Parkes observations will remain valuable at least until the first stage of the SKA is able to improve on our sensitivity and observing cadence. Even after the gravitational wave background is detected, continued observations will resolve the background origin and individual sources will be identified; advancing the nascent field of gravitational wave astronomy.

records.title: Long-term project observations for project L125 semester 2026APRS_22
records.description: The atomic interstellar medium shows tiny-scale optical depth fluctuations on the scale of 0.1~10,000 AU, whose origin and nature are poorly understood. The existence of this Tiny-Scale Atomic Structure (TSAS) has significant implications, potentially calling into question our fundamental understanding of heating, cooling and dynamical processes in the interstellar medium. Yet observations remain sparse. This long-term project plans to search for temporal variations in HI absorption spectra seen against background pulsars to characterise TSAS in the Milky Way interstellar medium (ISM). These observations constitute the largest number of sightlines and densest temporal sampling ever performed in a single experiment, and will test predictions that TSAS is the tail end of a turbulent cascade, constrain its minimum size scale (down to resolutions of ~0.05 AU) and potentially provide the first direct measurements of pressures in "large" TSAS features of > 1000 AU. We make use of the phase-resolved spectral line mode that we have recently implemented on Parkes, which has cut data rates and processing times by factors of ~1000 compared to past studies. This is an expansion of our pilot P1321 to a long term study.

records.title: Australian subnational material flows and metrics
records.description: This collection contains material flow data for Australian states and territories from 2010 to 2024. The dataset provides annual estimates of domestic extraction, imports, exports, domestic material consumption, material footprint, and emissions, including air emissions, solid and liquid waste, and seed and fertiliser flows. It also includes four headline circular economy and resource-use indicators: material footprint per capita, recycling rate, circularity rate, and material productivity. These indicators align with the metrics reported in the Australian Treasury’s Measuring What Matters framework. The data were produced to support analysis of material use, resource productivity, circular economy performance, and environmental pressures across Australian jurisdictions over time. The collection is intended to assist researchers, policymakers, analysts, and other users interested in tracking material flows and evaluating progress toward more sustainable patterns of consumption.

records.title: Parkes observations for project P1418 semester 2026APRS_04
records.description: Pulsars exhibit diverse radio-emission phenomena that remain poorly understoon. Among the most extreme are giant pulses (GPs): short-duration radio bursts whose energies exceed the average pulse by at least 10 times. Only 16 pulsars are known to emit GPs, including just five millisecond pulsars. This rises the question of whether this reflects intrinsic population differences or observational bias. We propose high time-resolution observations with Murriyang Ultra Wide-bandwidth Low-frequency (UWL) receiver to search for and characterise GPs from two prominent millisecond pulsar candidates, PSR J0030+0451 and PSR J1902-5105. Both share key properties with established GP emitters including large magnetic fields at the light-cylinder and high energy emission in X and gamma ray. These observations will provide essential clues to understanding how GPs are generated and what is their relation to average radio and high energy emissions in terms of their production mechanisms and locations within the pulsars magnetosphere.

records.title: Parkes observations for project P1054 semester 2026APRS_26
records.description: With this proposal we ask time to continue our timing follow-up campaign of pulsars discovered with the MeerKAT telescope. Fiftythree sources have been discovered in targeted observations of Fermi unidentified point sources, two towards Supernova Remnants, 27 in the Magellanic Clouds, 109 in Globular Clusters and 96 in a survey of the Galactic plane. A large fraction of the new discoveries are recycled pulsars (including a few relativistic systems, a pulsar with a planetary companion and several 'spider' binaries), or young pulsars. Timing observations have an essential role in exploiting the full potential of any pulsar discovery, allowing for the precise measurement of rotational, astrometric and orbital parameters which, in turn, give us powerful tools to improve our understanding of the physics in extreme environments as well as of the population of neutron stars as a whole. The UWL receiver of the Parkes telescope is a sensitive, versatile instrument that is allowing us to successfully time these new sources, in the bright-end of TRAPUM discoveries.

records.title: Parkes observations for project P1398 semester 2026APRS_09
records.description: Low-frequency (< ~1 GHz) Galactic-plane pulsar surveys are strongly limited by sky background noise, interstellar scattering, and dispersion smearing, leading to an incomplete census of the pulsar population. High-frequency (> 2 GHz) observations mitigate these effects and have recently enabled the discovery of pulsars that remain undetectable at low-frequency. We analyzed archival data from the 2008 Parkes 6.5-GHz pulsar survey using modern search techniques. This reprocessing has revealed four previously unknown millisecond pulsar candidates with spin periods of 3-11 ms and dispersion measures of 20-170 pc/cc. Two candidates exhibit significant line-of-sight acceleration, indicating likely membership in compact binary systems. We request a total of 8.4 hours of follow-up observations with the Parkes (Murriyang) Ultra-Wideband Low (UWL) receiver to confirm these candidates and characterize their emission across 704-4032 MHz. Confirming these sources would expand the population of high-frequency selected pulsars and demonstrate the continued importance of high-frequency searches for uncovering exotic systems obscured in conventional low-frequency surveys.

records.title: Parkes observations for project P595 semester 2026APRS_30
records.description: We propose to continue the PULSE@Parkes project in which high school students from Australia and around the World use the Parkes radio telescope in a remote observing model to observe and analyse pulsar data. The data from some PULSE@Parkes observations are used to support the space missions, other observations supplement the P456 Pulsar Timing Array project and the remainder were chosen in order to make a detailed analysis of pulsar timing irregularities and intermittency.

records.title: Parkes observations for project P1409 semester 2026APRS_06
records.description: To investigate the physical origin and local environment of the repeating fast radio burst FRB 20230607A, which exhibits an exceptionally high rotation measure, we propose to observe this repeater with 24-hour observations using the Ultra-Wideband Low-frequency (UWL) receiver of the Parkes radio telescope (Murriyang). This proposal aims to monitor the secular evolution of the Faraday Rotation Measure, studying the cause of its low linear polarization, and resolve the specro-polarimetric structure of repeat bursts. The possible findings are critical to unveiling the extreme magnetized environment of the source, understanding emission mechanisms and propagation effects, and thereby shedding light on the physics origin(s) of repeating fast radio bursts.

records.title: Parkes observations for project P1402 semester 2026APRS_20
records.description: We propose a dedicated Parkes/Murriyang timing campaign of the newly confirmed narrow-duty cycle (~6 %) millisecond pulsar (MSP) PSR J2147-3604. This source was identified in a reprocessing of the Green Bank North Celestial Cap (GBNCC) survey as a high-confidence candidate with a spin period of 3.2 ms, and a dispersion measure, DM of 17 pc/cc. The pulsar was subsequently confirmed by the Fermi--TRAPUM collaboration via MeerKAT beamforming localisation and Parkes follow-up. Parkes/UWL observations allocated using green time detected this pulsar between 700--1500~MHz, and confirmed that it's in a binary system. Due to its low DM, we also detected strong interstellar scintillation. We request 35~hr of Murriyang time using the UWL receiver and APOLLO backend to obtain a phase-coherent timing solution and to characterise its spin, orbital, and propagation properties. Since the pulsar is also associated with a FERMI source, a precise radio ephemeris will also enable sensitive searches for gamma-ray pulsations in Fermi-LAT data and assess PSR J2147-3604's suitability for pulsar timing arrays (PTAs) and future gamma-ray timing applications.

records.title: Long-term project observations for project L134 semester 2026APRS_07
records.description: Omega Cen is the largest globular cluster in the Milky Way. It contains at least 18 known MSPs, and there are solid hints for the presence of an even larger pulsar population. We propose a regular monthly follow-up to refine the timing solutions of the five Parkes discoveries from 2020, and to find timing solutions for the 13 MeerKAT discoveries from 2023, in combination with six MeerKAT observations between 2021 and 2023, and future MeerKAT observations. These timing solutions should enable the detection of derivatives of the spin periods of these pulsars, allowing us to probe the dynamics of Omega Cen and the presence of a possible IMBH at its centre. Timing solutions will also enable the search for X-ray and gamma-ray pulsations in the multiple sources detected in this cluster. This study will allow us to better understand the populations of this globular cluster and its formation history. We request observations until 2030, when we expect to have measurements of the second period derivative of the five brighter discoveries, and first period derivative measurements for the later discoveries. These observations will also contribute to the study of eclipsing binaries, and may include future discoveries from pending searches in MeerKAT data.

records.title: Parkes observations for project P1411 semester 2026APRS_25
records.description: Conventional blind pulsar surveys that search for periodic signals in high-time-resolution data are increasingly limited by interstellar scattering at high dispersion measure (DM), orbital modulation in compact binaries, scintillation effects, and intensive computational demands. The Australian Square Kilometre Array Pathfinder (ASKAP) Evolutionary Map of the Universe (EMU) survey provides ultra-deep radio continuum maps enabling complementary image-domain pulsar searches that bypass these limitations. We have discovered seven new pulsars through three targeted strategies: (1) identifying compact sources embedded in supernova remnants (SNRs) and pulsar wind nebulae (PWNe), (2) detecting highly variable sources via variance imaging, and (3) selecting highly circularly polarised compact sources. Our sample includes three highly scattered pulsars (PSR J1638-4713 , PSR J1643-4511, and PSR J1631-4722 with DM > 800 pc/cm^3) including two pulsars associated with PWNe. Two millisecond pulsars (PSR J0927-7641 and PSR J1838-5949) are in potential wide binary systems with orbital periods of several tens of days, and two additional normal pulsars (PSR J1153-7106 and PSR 2223-0654). We propose follow-up timing observations of these pulsars with Murriyang's Ultra-Wideband Low (UWL) receiver to obtain phase-connected timing solutions, measure precise positions and spin parameters, and determine orbital characteristics for the binary systems,. These observations will enable studies of pulsar formation mechanisms, binary evolution pathways, PWN-SNR interactions, and validate image-based discovery techniques as powerful complements to traditional blind surveys for detecting elusive pulsars.

records.title: Spectra and Polarisation In Cutouts of Extragalactic sources from RACS Second Data Release (SPICE-RACS-DR2)
records.description: Spectra and Polarisation In Cutouts of Extragalactic sources from RACS (SPICE-RACS) is a project to derive an all-Southern-sky, linear polarisation map from the Rapid ASKAP Continuum Survey (RACS). Through this project, we will derive the following products: • Cutout image cubes in Stokes I, Q, and U around every source detected in total intensity as a function of frequency • Polarisation spectra as a function of frequency and Faraday depth for every component detected in total intensity • A catalogue summarising the polarisation properties, including rotation measure (RM), for every component. • Catalogues that provide the source and component positions in total intensity. Note that the total intensity catalogues should be treated as a reference for source positions in the images, and approximate source properties. These are not processed to the same quality standard as the forthcoming RACS-low3 catalogue (Galvin et al. in prep). This collection is laid out as follows: / ├── catalogues/ │ └── ... ├── cubelets/ │ ├── {FIELD_NAME}{SBID}_cubelets.tar.gz │ └── ... ├── skymaps/ │ ├── spice-racs.dr2.{column name}{interpolation}.fits │ └── ... └── spectra/ ├── {FIELD_NAME}_{SBID}_spectra.tar.gz └── ... Catalogues: - RACS-low3_INITIAL_components.fits - RACS-low3_INITIAL_sources.fits - spice-racs.dr2.fits.gz Key identifier columns: The following columns can be used to match across the catalogues, and are also used to structure the data below. • Scheduling Block: 'sbid' in the spice-racs catalogue, and 'SBID' in the source and component catalogues. • Field or Tile: 'tile_id' in the spice-racs catalogue, and 'Field_ID' in the source and component catalogues. • PyBDSF Gaussian component: 'cat_id' in the spice-racs catalogue, and 'Gaussian_ID' component catalogue. • PyBDSF Source: 'source_id' in the spice-racs catalogue, and 'Source_ID' in the source and component catalogues. Basic subsets: From the SPICE-RACS DR2 paper, S4.1: "Our catalogue contains a row for every source detected in total intensity. We must therefore stress that not every reported row will correspond to a component with a reliable detection of polarised flux. Rather, we have retained all possible values so that users in the community can make their own cuts on the catalogue to satisfy their own needs and balance of completeness vs. correctness. To assist users of the catalogue, we have again defined some basic subsets that should be reasonable, although conservative, for most science cases. These are as follows: • goodI: Where the stokesI_fit_flag and channel_flag columns are False. • goodRM: goodI, and where leakage_flag and snr_flag are False." Cubelets: {tile_id}_{sbid}/ ├── {source_id stem} │ ├── {source_id}.SB{sbid}.cutout.{image type}.restored.{Stokes}.{tile_id}.contcube.linmos.{ion type}.fits │ └── ... └── ... • 'image type' can be 'image' or 'weight' • 'Stokes' can be 'i', 'q', or 'u' • ion type can be 'ion' or left out of the file name Spectra: {tile_id}_{sbid}/ ├── {cat_id stem}/ │ ├── {cat_id}.SB{sbid}.{spectra type}.fits │ └── ... └── ... • 'spectra type' can be 'freq', 'fdf', or 'rmsf' Note that a 'stem' for cat_id or source_id e.g. "XYZ_123" will be "XYZ" Sky maps: These are catalogue data interpolated onto sky using either nearest-neighbour (nn) or inverse-distance weighting (idw). All files are HEALPix images with Nside=512. All files are named following: spice-racs.dr2.{column name}_{interpolation}.fits Where 'column name' is the column from the catalogue being interpolated, and interpolation is either 'nn' or 'idw' as above.

records.title: Long-term project observations for project L152 semester 2026APRS_02
records.description: PSR J1757-1854 is the most relativistic galactic double neutron star system. Its eccentricity makes it an ideal playground for gravity experiments with pulsar timing. Via observations of its profile evolution, we can constraint its rate of geodetic precession. Currently, there are four possible geometric configurations that explain the time evolution of the polarisation swing. The geodetic precession and the Lense-Thirring effect will eventually manifest themselves in the post-Keplerian parameters within the next decade, allowing for two further tests of gravity. We propose a regular monitoring of this source to extend the timing baseline and contribute towards the tests of gravity. We will inspect the polarisation properties of this observation, and we will add the ToAs to a global timing campaign. These observations will be added to joint GBT and MeerKAT observations, and they will be part of a long-term, global observational program of this pulsar.

records.title: SCOPFProxy.jl
records.description: SCOPFProxy.jl is a Julia-based research software tool developed by CSIRO Energy to support learning-assisted security-constrained power system optimisation. It provides utilities for parsing MATPOWER-format network cases, reading contingency and metadata files, validating selected non-islanding contingencies, and preparing reproducible demonstration workflows for security-constrained optimal power flow studies. The bundled example uses the synthetic national electricity market (SNEM) case to demonstrate the input-processing and contingency-validation workflow. It is intended as a lightweight reproducible example and does not execute a full SCOPF optimisation by default.

records.title: MultiStageSCTNEP.jl
records.description: MultiStageSCTNEP.jl is a Julia-based research software tool developed to support CSIRO Energy research on multi-stage security-constrained transmission expansion planning. It provides utilities for staged planning studies, candidate transmission investment tracking across planning horizons, reinforcement-candidate refinement using system-stress indicators, and reproducible planning-output generation. The workflow supports non-confidential benchmark and synthetic power-system cases, including IEEE test systems and larger SNEM-style studies.

records.title: Long-term project observations for project L132 semester 2026APRS_03
records.description: PSR J1227-6208 is a recycled pulsar in a binary with a massive white dwarf companion. A recent timing measurement from combined MeerKAT and Parkes observations shows the companion mass to be between 1.2 and 1.5 solar masses, very close to the Chandrasekhar limit, resulting in potentially profound physical implications. However, the timing precision is limited by the DM timing noise. We propose regular monitoring of this pulsar with the Parkes UWL receiver in conjunction with MeerKAT observations during the following four years. The joint monitoring will significantly improve the constraints on the Post-Keplerian parameters, with Parkes observations contributing to constrain the DM noise due to its large frequency bandwidth. These observations will be added to the already existing 11-year-long timing baseline, of which the later 5 years already include high-precision MeerKAT data and Parkes UWL data. After four years of further timing with the inclusion of UWL observations, we predict an uncertainty on the masses smaller than 0.01 solar masses based on simulations. If UWL is not included, the mass uncertainties may not improve beyond their current values.

records.title: Parkes observations for project P1413 semester 2026APRS_19
records.description: We request 75 hours of Parkes observing time for dedicated radio follow-up observations of PSR J1635-5134, a promising candidate pulsar-subdwarf B (sdB) star binary system. PSR J1635-5134 is a non-recycled 340 ms pulsar in a nearly circular 18-hour orbit with a minimum companion mass of 0.26 solar mass. It lies in a sparsely populated region of binary-pulsars parameter space and may represent a short-lived evolutionary stage immediately following inefficient spin-up, thereby providing a missing link between canonical binaries and the millisecond pulsar-WD population. The system exhibits peculiar, orbital-phase-dependent dispersion-measure (DM) variability, with DM variations exceeding 30 pc/cc, indicating substantial ionised material plausibly associated with an outflow from the companion. Moreover, during prior monitoring with Parkes, the DM variations shifted from being predominantly modest to being persistently large, implying an evolving plasma environment that cannot be characterised with sparse or irregular observations. Determining whether these high-DM variations are intermittent or long-lived, and mapping how the excess material varies with orbital phase and epoch, are essential for constraining the origin and geometry of the plasma and for testing the hypothesis that an sdB wind supplies the required electron column. Through this proposal, we aim to (i) extend the timing baseline to improve astrometric precision to sub-arcsecond accuracy, enabling secure identification of the optical counterpart in a crowded field, and (ii) perform phase-targeted observations during eclipse/DM variation phases to understand the temporal behavior of excess DM.

records.title: Long-term project observations for project L126 semester 2026APRS_15
records.description: We propose a modest program to continue monitoring 4 of the 6 known radio magnetars in order to achieve three primary science goals. The first is to characterise magnetar outbursts over long timescales, for which tracking their rotational, flux density, and polarisation properties provide a clear view of the impulse response of their magnetic fields. Second, understanding the links between magnetars the mysterious fast radio burst phenomenon through the discovery of rare emission and propagation effects, shared spectro-temporal phenomenology, and connections to high-energy (X-ray/gamma-ray) phenomena. Lastly, our continued monitoring has enormous benefit to the wider magnetar community, providing rapid alerts to changes in activity, adding context to unusual behaviour detected by high-energy observations, and a host of supplementary science through the teams extensive collaborative networks. The project and its precursors have been running since 2007 and have contributed to 22 publications since then. This is the first submission since the project was converted to long-term status.

records.title: Parkes observations for project P1410 semester 2026APRS_10
records.description: Neutron stars are compact remnants formed in core-collapse supernovae of massive stars. A subset of these objects, known as pulsars, emit highly regular pulses of radiation that make them powerful tools for studying fundamental physics, stellar evolution, and the structure of our Galaxy. Despite decades of surveys, the known pulsar population remains incomplete: while about 4,800 pulsars are currently catalogued, population studies predict that roughly 10,000 or more radio-detectable pulsars should be observable with our current instrumentation. A significant fraction of the missing population is expected to consist of slowly rotating pulsars, which are difficult to detect with standard search pipelines. These pulsars often have very narrow pulse duty cycles and long spin periods, making them susceptible to reduced signal-to-noise ratios and contamination by low-frequency ("red") noise in Fourier-based searches. As a result, many such objects may remain hidden in archival survey data. Motivated by this, we reprocessed archival data from the Parkes Multibeam Pulsar Survey targeting narrow-duty-cycle signals and allowing to investigate lower signal to noise ratios for these candidates. This approach led to the identification of 12 highly credible new slow pulsar candidates that were missed in previous analyses. Several of these candidates show strong folded signal-to-noise ratios and physically plausible dispersion measures, indicating they are likely genuine pulsars. The primary goal of this proposal is to obtain targeted follow-up observations to confirm and time these newly identified pulsar candidates. Confirming them will help close the gap between predicted and observed pulsar populations and demonstrate the continued scientific value of archival radio survey data.

records.title: Parkes observations for project P1423 semester 2026APRS_15
records.description: Pulsars are rapidly rotating, highly magnetized neutron stars whose radio emission provides unique probes of extreme gravity, plasma physics, and magnetospheric processes. Millisecond pulsars(MSPs) exhibit exceptional rotational stability, making them fundamental components of Pulsar Timing Arrays used to detect nanohertz gravitational waves, while also enabling precision tests of general relativity, binary evolution, and studies of the interstellar medium(ISM). Normal pulsars(NPs), on the other hand, serve as powerful laboratories for investigating neutron-star interiors, supernova remnants, magnetospheric physics, pulsar winds, and glitch phenomena. Their polarization measurements are crucial, as they constrain emission geometry, magnetic-field configuration, and propagation effects such as Faraday rotation, while enabling robust determination of rotation measures(RM). For MSPs in particular, polarization studies improve timing-template fidelity and help correct frequency-dependent propagation effects that impact high-precision timing experiments. GMRT low-frequency surveys have significantly expanded the known pulsar population, yet many GMRT-discovered pulsars lack broadband polarization measurements, leaving their emission geometry and frequency-dependent profile evolution poorly constrained. We propose 21 hours of observations with the Parkes 64-m telescope using UWL receiver to conduct a spectro-polarimetric study of six GMRT-discovered pulsars: three MSPs(J1207-5050, J1227-4853, J1646-2142) and three NPs(J0514-4407, J0418-4154, J0702-4956) to conduct a spectro-polarimetric study. These targets exhibit unresolved or contradictory polarization behaviour, including profile evolution, eclipse-driven interaction signatures, incomplete detections, or absence of full-Stokes information. The proposed wideband, high-sensitivity observations will provide robust RM measurements, broadband polarization profiles, and frequency-dependent beam mapping, filling key observational gaps and enhancing the scientific value of GMRT-discovered pulsars for magnetospheric studies and pulsar timing science.

records.title: Parkes observations for project P1165 semester 2026APRS_06

records.title: Long-term project observations for project L125 semester 2026APRS_23
records.description: The atomic interstellar medium shows tiny-scale optical depth fluctuations on the scale of 0.1~10,000 AU, whose origin and nature are poorly understood. The existence of this Tiny-Scale Atomic Structure (TSAS) has significant implications, potentially calling into question our fundamental understanding of heating, cooling and dynamical processes in the interstellar medium. Yet observations remain sparse. This long-term project plans to search for temporal variations in HI absorption spectra seen against background pulsars to characterise TSAS in the Milky Way interstellar medium (ISM). These observations constitute the largest number of sightlines and densest temporal sampling ever performed in a single experiment, and will test predictions that TSAS is the tail end of a turbulent cascade, constrain its minimum size scale (down to resolutions of ~0.05 AU) and potentially provide the first direct measurements of pressures in "large" TSAS features of > 1000 AU. We make use of the phase-resolved spectral line mode that we have recently implemented on Parkes, which has cut data rates and processing times by factors of ~1000 compared to past studies. This is an expansion of our pilot P1321 to a long term study.

records.title: Parkes observations for project P1304 semester 2026APRS_01
records.description: Fast radio bursts (FRBs) are immensely energetic radio transients whose origin remains unclear. With fewer than 10% of nearly 1,000 known FRBs exhibiting repeating behaviour, nearby events are crucial for understanding their mechanisms. The discovery of FRB 20200120E in a globular cluster within M81 (3.63 Mpc) and FRB 20200428 from the Galactic magnetar SGR 1935+2154 suggests that FRBs originate from compact objects in diverse stellar environments. However, current blind surveys like CHIME have detected only one repeating FRB within 100 Mpc, indicating the need for targeted searches. We propose a pilot survey using the Parkes CryoPAF receiver to systematically search for FRBs in nearby globular cluster systems. With its large field of view (~1 degree) and improved cryogenic system (SEFD = 27.21 Jy), Parkes cryoPAF offers a complementary approach to high-sensitivity single-dish telescopes. Our survey strategy targets multiple pointings covering >7,000 globular clusters across nearby galaxies, with optimization accounting for continuum radio background and telescope sensitivity. We request 24 hours of observations targeting three recommended pointings (TP0, TP1, TP2), expected to yield approximately two new FRB detections based on current models. This pilot experiment, combined with complementary FAST observations, will establish an efficient multi-telescope survey framework to discover nearby FRBs and investigate the physical conditions and environments that produce such sources.

records.title: Parkes observations for project P1183 semester 2026APRS_09
records.description: After nearly four years of monitoring with both the Parkes and FAST telescopes, FRB 20220529 has been established as an extremely active repeater. It exhibits one of the longest known activity durations and shows evidence for a potential periodicity. Owing to the frequent observations carried out with Parkes and FAST, two abrupt rotation-measure (RM) flares have been detected in this source. These constitute the first RM flares ever observed in a fast radio burst (FRB), indicating that a dense, magnetised plasma clump passed across the line of sight. The second RM flare in particular makes a binary-origin scenario for FRB 20220529 especially compelling. If confirmed, the periodicity and RM flares would mutually reinforce one another, serving as a smoking gun for a binary origin. Previous analyses have shown that observations from both Parkes and FAST are essential. FAST's exceptional sensitivity enables the detection of many bursts, whereas the Parkes UWL receiver provides a stable burst-detection rate even during low-activity phases. To further investigate FRB 20220529, we have scheduled regular FAST observations every fortnight. We therefore propose to continue monitoring FRB 20220529 with the Parkes UWL receiver as well. The FAST and Parkes sessions are expected to be separated by a few days, ideally about one week. A cadence of approximately one week offers an excellent opportunity to capture detailed structure during the onset of RM decreases, as demonstrated by previous monitoring.

records.title: Parkes observations for project P1375 semester 2026APRS_07
records.description: Rotating radio transients (RRATs) are Galactic neutron stars that emit sporadic radio pulses, and the question of whether apparently one-off sources truly repeat remains unresolved. With the discovery of numerous fast radio bursts (FRBs), the paradigm of 'one detection defines an astrophysical source' has shifted. However, the distinction between truly non-repeating Galactic transients and insufficiently observed repeating sources remains critical. Recent high-sensitivity follow-up observations with FAST have revealed that multiple apparent one-off RRATs originally detected by Parkes are in fact repeating sources, with fainter pulses hundreds of times weaker than their initial bright detections. This discovery raises a fundamental question: are many one-off RRATs simply the result of insufficient observational sensitivity, or do they represent intrinsically catastrophic transient events. We propose deep follow-up monitoring of four apparent one-off RRATs using the Parkes Ultra-Wideband receiver system, which offers 1.7-3.4 times higher sensitivity than the Multibeam discovery data. These observations will constrain the pulse repetition rates and energy distributions of these sources, examine the extreme variability seen in some RRATs and pulsars that exhibit pulses differing by >500 times in brightness, and test whether hidden repeating emission explains the apparent one-off nature of these sources.

records.title: Stochastic climate data for central-north Victoria (Maryborough area)
records.description: This collection provides stochastic data for rainfall, evaporation, and maximum temperature. It contains two folders (historical stochastic data and stochastic data adjusted by climate change). The historical data contains three sub-datasets, each parameterised to a different subset of the historical period: full-period (1889–2022), post-75 (1975–2022), and post-93 (1993–2022). Each sub-dataset includes 1,000 replicates for eight sites — four for rainfall, three for evaporation, and one for maximum temperature. The duration of each dataset spans from 1889 to 2021, with the final year offset due to stochastic data generation. The climate change-adjusted data contains 12 datasets covering the period from 2022 to 2091, each with different transient trends applied to rainfall, evaporation, and temperature. The baseline used for the climate change-adjusted data is the post-1975 stochastic dataset.
