records.title: Habitat Condition Assessment Tool (HCAT) v3.0: Expert-derived ecosystem condition assessments for Australia (data collected July 2025-April 2026)
records.description: This collection comprises site-level ecosystem condition assessments collected through the Habitat Condition Assessment Tool (HCAT) between July 2025 and April 2026, applying the version 3.0 methodology (Munroe et al. 2025). The HCAT is a web-based platform hosted by the Atlas of Living Australia’s BioCollect information system that enables experts with deep ecological knowledge and field experience to contribute site-level ecosystem condition assessments (https://biocollect.ala.org.au/hcat/home/index, see Related Links). Specifically, the data collection comprises: • Site condition assessments (GeoPackage): A spatial data file Site_Condition_Assessments.gpkg containing polygon features representing individual site assessments, with associated attribute data including overall ecosystem condition scores, ecosystem characteristic scores, and assessment dates • Site photographs (where provided): A collection of photographs associated with the site assessments, contributed optionally by experts. Not all sites have photos available • Photo–site linking metadata: A metadata file (site_photos_attribute_data.csv) linking each site photo to its corresponding site and attribution information. This collection contains 1,063 site condition assessments assessed between 2010 and 2025 and 735 associated site photographs. A data dictionary has also been provided, describing the contents and file structure of the collection (see Supporting files). It also provides a brief description of the methodology used to create this collection. This data collection has been designed to provide expert-derived reference and modified ecosystem sites to support development, calibration and validation of model-based ecosystem condition assessments, such as the Habitat Condition Assessment System (HCAS; Valavi et al. 2026; Harwood et al. 2016, see Related Links), which integrates site-based observations with satellite remote sensing across entire continents, and ecosystem state-and-transition modelling based on the Australian Ecosystem Models Framework (Richards et al. 2020, see Related Links). The HCAT captures ecosystem condition across a continuum of intact to highly modified states, supporting a wide range of biodiversity research, natural resource planning, and environmental monitoring and reporting uses. The HCAT data collection is ongoing – the tool remains open for contributions, and coverage of Australia’s ecosystems is expected to expand through future expert elicitation campaigns. Updates will be periodically published with recalibrated ecosystem condition scores including revised scaling factors, and new contributors and site assessments. The HCAT v3.0 instructions guide provides a complete description of data elicitation methods, and can be cited as: Munroe S, Giljohann K, Brenton P, Williams KJ, Hosack G, Richards A, Brinkman J, Checksfield S, Salomon J, Raisbeck-Brown N, Warnick A, Dickson F, Pirzl R, Sinclair S and White M (2025) The Habitat Condition Assessment Tool: Instructions for participants, version 3.0. Publication EP2025-2633. CSIRO, Townsville, Australia. DOI: https://doi.org/10.25919/gkr9-cx03.

records.description: We propose a deep 100-hour Parkes radio pulsar survey of the Galactic plane region l = 240 ~ 260 deg, |b| < 2 deg, -a 80-square-degree zone currently unobserved by any major deep pulsar survey such as the Parkes Multibeam Pulsar Survey (PMPS) and The MPIfR-MeerKAT Galactic Plane Survey (MMGPS). This sightline probes the near side of the Perseus Arm (4~6 kpc), yet contains only 14 known pulsars, likely incomplete due to the shallow integrations and FFT-limited pipelines of prior work. Using the CryoPAF receiver (1100 ~ 1700 MHz, 600 MHz bandwidth) with 3000-second pointings and a Fast Folding Algorithm (FFA)-enhanced search, we will detect long-period (P=1~10s) and high-DM (< 350 pc cm ^-3) pulsars missed previously. We expect to discover 20 ~ 40 new pulsars, enabling precise mapping of the local electron density and testing Galactic ISM models. Critically, our field contains the unassociated Fermi sources , offering a prime opportunity for multiwavelength identification. The survey will also probe transient phenomena via single-pulse searches. This project addresses a well-defined observational gap with high discovery potential for both Galactic structure and high-energy astrophysics.

records.title: Long-term project observations for project L126 semester 2026APRS_18
records.description: We propose a modest program to continue monitoring 4 of the 6 known radio magnetars in order to achieve three primary science goals. The first is to characterise magnetar outbursts over long timescales, for which tracking their rotational, flux density, and polarisation properties provide a clear view of the impulse response of their magnetic fields. Second, understanding the links between magnetars the mysterious fast radio burst phenomenon through the discovery of rare emission and propagation effects, shared spectro-temporal phenomenology, and connections to high-energy (X-ray/gamma-ray) phenomena. Lastly, our continued monitoring has enormous benefit to the wider magnetar community, providing rapid alerts to changes in activity, adding context to unusual behaviour detected by high-energy observations, and a host of supplementary science through the teams extensive collaborative networks. The project and its precursors have been running since 2007 and have contributed to 22 publications since then. This is the first submission since the project was converted to long-term status.

records.title: Long-term project observations for project L124 semester 2026APRS_10
records.description: We propose a long-term project to monitor a very active repeater, FRB 20190520B, with Murriyang's UWL system. Our previous observations show that FRB 20190520B is not only among the most active FRBs that can be observed with Murriyang, but also shows extreme rotation measure (RM) and dispersion measure (DM) evolution, along with distinctive behavior at 3GHz frequency. This makes the UWL receiver uniquely suited for detailed studies and long-term monitoring of this repeating FRB. Through this program, we anticipate detecting a large sample of bursts from this FRB. In collaboration with FAST, we aim to investigate the time evolution of various properties of FRB 20190520B, enhance our understanding of polarisation across an extremely wide bandwidth with high sensitivity, and gain deeper insights into the local environment and emission mechanisms of FRBs.

records.title: Long-term project observations for project L132 semester 2026APRS_04
records.description: PSR J1227-6208 is a recycled pulsar in a binary with a massive white dwarf companion. A recent timing measurement from combined MeerKAT and Parkes observations shows the companion mass to be between 1.2 and 1.5 solar masses, very close to the Chandrasekhar limit, resulting in potentially profound physical implications. However, the timing precision is limited by the DM timing noise. We propose regular monitoring of this pulsar with the Parkes UWL receiver in conjunction with MeerKAT observations during the following four years. The joint monitoring will significantly improve the constraints on the Post-Keplerian parameters, with Parkes observations contributing to constrain the DM noise due to its large frequency bandwidth. These observations will be added to the already existing 11-year-long timing baseline, of which the later 5 years already include high-precision MeerKAT data and Parkes UWL data. After four years of further timing with the inclusion of UWL observations, we predict an uncertainty on the masses smaller than 0.01 solar masses based on simulations. If UWL is not included, the mass uncertainties may not improve beyond their current values.

records.title: Parkes observations for project P737 semester 2026APRS_06
records.description: Instrumental Commissioning

records.title: Parkes observations for project P1421 semester 2026APRS_02
records.description: Fast radio bursts (FRBs) are brief, ultra-bright transients, most likely associated with neutron stars. Although their luminosity makes them powerful probes of cosmological environments, their extragalactic distances and sporadic occurrence hinder direct investigation of their emission physics. The Crab pulsar has been considered a potential Galactic analogue to FRBs through its giant pulses (GPs). At nanosecond resolution, Crab GPs resolve into narrowband, nearly 100% polarised nanoshots with randomly distributed polarisation angles (PAs), motivating models in which burst envelopes arise from the superposition of many independently polarised shots. However, this behaviour contrasts with most FRBs, which frequently exhibit coherent PA evolution across microsecond-millisecond timescales. Consequently, Crab GPs have generally been regarded as poor FRB analogues. Recent high-time-resolution observations from the CRAFT survey revealed FRBs with rapid, highly structured PA variability that is naturally interpreted as the superposition of partially correlated polarised shots rather than smooth PA swings. Also, a rare and largely unexplored sub-class of Crab single pulses has been identified that exhibits coherent or partially ordered PA evolution on nanosecond-microsecond timescales, implying correlated shot properties or organised plasma and magnetic-field structure within the emission region. We aim to systematically identify and characterise these Crab pulses and assess their relevance as FRB analogues. Using the Fast, Intense Radio Emission Simulator (FIRES), we model these events within a polarised shot noise framework and directly compare their inferred shot properties to the high-time-resolution CRAFT FRB sample.

records.title: Parkes observations for project P1409 semester 2026APRS_08
records.description: To investigate the physical origin and local environment of the repeating fast radio burst FRB 20230607A, which exhibits an exceptionally high rotation measure, we propose to observe this repeater with 24-hour observations using the Ultra-Wideband Low-frequency (UWL) receiver of the Parkes radio telescope (Murriyang). This proposal aims to monitor the secular evolution of the Faraday Rotation Measure, studying the cause of its low linear polarization, and resolve the specro-polarimetric structure of repeat bursts. The possible findings are critical to unveiling the extreme magnetized environment of the source, understanding emission mechanisms and propagation effects, and thereby shedding light on the physics origin(s) of repeating fast radio bursts.

records.title: Parkes observations for project P1054 semester 2026APRS_32
records.description: With this proposal we ask time to continue our timing follow-up campaign of pulsars discovered with the MeerKAT telescope. Fiftythree sources have been discovered in targeted observations of Fermi unidentified point sources, two towards Supernova Remnants, 27 in the Magellanic Clouds, 109 in Globular Clusters and 96 in a survey of the Galactic plane. A large fraction of the new discoveries are recycled pulsars (including a few relativistic systems, a pulsar with a planetary companion and several 'spider' binaries), or young pulsars. Timing observations have an essential role in exploiting the full potential of any pulsar discovery, allowing for the precise measurement of rotational, astrometric and orbital parameters which, in turn, give us powerful tools to improve our understanding of the physics in extreme environments as well as of the population of neutron stars as a whole. The UWL receiver of the Parkes telescope is a sensitive, versatile instrument that is allowing us to successfully time these new sources, in the bright-end of TRAPUM discoveries.

records.title: Long-term project observations for project L100 semester 2026APRS_11
records.description: We request time to observe 270 pulsars on a regular basis in order to achieve three main science goals. The first is to understand pulsars: how do they spin down and what disrupts this process, how and why their profiles vary with time, whether they precess or have planetary mass companions, in short all the things that make pulsar timing noisier than the perfect clock. Secondly we want to understand the interstellar medium of our Galaxy through repeated monitoring of dispersion measure, rotation measure and flux density variations in conjunction with scintillation parameters. Finally, we provide these data as a community service both to the high-energy community where we have strong collaborative links (particularly to Fermi) and to the radio pulsar astronomers generally through the CSIRO archive. The project is on-going since 2007, we are (co-)authors on 107 papers arising from the P574 data. The data have contributed to the PhD theses of students from Bordeaux, Manchester, Oxford, Stanford, and Swinburne. We are seeking long-term project status with a view to continuing the project into the SKA era.

records.title: Parkes observations for project P1416 semester 2026APRS_08
records.description: Radio pulsars in orbit around high-mass stellar companions offer a rich source of extreme physics for both observational astronomers and theorists alike. Despite being discovered 25 years ago, PSR J1638-4725 remains a veritable mystery compared to similar pulsar binary systems. Long-term monitoring has revealed extended `eclipses' where the pulsar is undetectable for months around periastron at GHz frequencies, along with intense variations in the observed pulsar dispersion measure, scatter broadening and flux density throughout the entire orbit. Preliminary spectroscopic characterisation of the companion star suggests it may be an O/B star, albiet one without a circumstellar disc of ejected material. This raises the unique opportunity to answer test the structure and origin of the near-wind regime of high-mass stars. In this proposal we will conduct an ambitious monitoring campaign of PSR J1638-4725 with both the ultra-wideband low and MARS recievers on Murriyang. We will track changes in the pulsar dispersion and scattering as it swings around the companion star, providing unique insights into the density and temperature distribution of the stellar wind from the companion star before and after the pulsar swings through periastron. These observations will also play a pivotal role in a broader multi-wavelength campaign to fully capture the upcoming 2026 periastron passage.

records.title: Parkes observations for project P1032 semester 2026APRS_13
records.description: With this proposal, we aim to continue P1032, the rapid measurements of relativistic parameters of southern binary pulsar systems using data from the Parkes Ultra Wideband Low (UWL) receiver. As the MeerTime project at the MeerKAT radio telescope ended in early 2024, observations with the UWL receiver now form the backbone for extending the timing baselines of many pulsars that have been part of this project. Since the source selection in the previous semesters was tailored such that the UWL receiver is the most (versatile and) suited instrument to achieve the proposed scientific goals for the chosen pulsars, we propose to continue these observations. We will use the UWL data to obtain significant orbital coverage and timing baselines on these pulsars and obtain important constraints on orbital and temporal DM variations that will help in identifying the nature of the companion stars. Increasing the number of measured Neutron Star (NS) masses, as well as improving on current constraints has profound implications for NS internal structure and for stellar and binary evolution physics.

records.title: Parkes observations for project P1413 semester 2026APRS_23
records.description: We request 75 hours of Parkes observing time for dedicated radio follow-up observations of PSR J1635-5134, a promising candidate pulsar-subdwarf B (sdB) star binary system. PSR J1635-5134 is a non-recycled 340 ms pulsar in a nearly circular 18-hour orbit with a minimum companion mass of 0.26 solar mass. It lies in a sparsely populated region of binary-pulsars parameter space and may represent a short-lived evolutionary stage immediately following inefficient spin-up, thereby providing a missing link between canonical binaries and the millisecond pulsar-WD population. The system exhibits peculiar, orbital-phase-dependent dispersion-measure (DM) variability, with DM variations exceeding 30 pc/cc, indicating substantial ionised material plausibly associated with an outflow from the companion. Moreover, during prior monitoring with Parkes, the DM variations shifted from being predominantly modest to being persistently large, implying an evolving plasma environment that cannot be characterised with sparse or irregular observations. Determining whether these high-DM variations are intermittent or long-lived, and mapping how the excess material varies with orbital phase and epoch, are essential for constraining the origin and geometry of the plasma and for testing the hypothesis that an sdB wind supplies the required electron column. Through this proposal, we aim to (i) extend the timing baseline to improve astrometric precision to sub-arcsecond accuracy, enabling secure identification of the optical counterpart in a crowded field, and (ii) perform phase-targeted observations during eclipse/DM variation phases to understand the temporal behavior of excess DM.

records.title: Parkes observations for project P1394 semester 2026APRS_03
records.description: We propose to observe the radio-loud magnetar 1E 1547.0-5408 to support an upcoming campaign with NASA's Imaging X-ray Polarimetry Explorer (IXPE) to confirm the first ever direct detection of vacuum birefringence. This strong-field quantum effect was first predicted by Heisenberg back in the 1930s, but has eluded direct detection in Earth-based laboratories due to our inability to replicate the magnetic field strengths required to induce vacuum birefreingence. 1E 1547.0-5408 displays a high X-ray polarisation fraction with a strong energy and rotation-phase dependence, along with evidence of mode-locking in the polarisation position angle. Both effects are strong indicators that vacuum birefringence is occurring in the magnetised atmosphere of this extreme object. Our observations with Murriyang will not only provide a phase-coherent timing solution for folding the IXPE photons during the upcoming 2026 campaign, but provides a critical, independent measure of the magnetar viewing and magnetic geometry. Combined, these measurements will confirm this long sought direct of vacuum birefrinegnce, thereby opening a new window into studying quantum electrodynamics in one of the most extreme environments in the Universe.

records.title: Long-term project observations for project L147 semester 2026APRS_08
records.description: We propose to carry out a deep Galactic Bulge pulsar survey (GBps), covering the core of the Bulge region using the new cryoPAF system on Murriyang, the Parkes radio telescope. Such a deep survey is expected to discover a population of millisecond pulsars in the Galactic Bulge and reveal their distribution and gamma-ray emissions. With these, we will lead pioneering studies on the origin of gamma-ray emission in the Galactic Bulge, a longstanding mystery in modern astronomy. The outcome of this project will significantly advance our knowledge of the formation and evolution of millisecond pulsars in the Galactic Bulge, the origin and properties of high-energy emissions, and the nature of dark matter annihilation in the Galactic Centre. A total of 200 observations with the cryoPAF is required to cover a 400 square degree region (|gl|<10 deg, |gb|<10 deg). The survey is expected to be carried out over four semesters, from April 2026 to October 2027.

records.description: Australian oat production is limited by crown rust disease caused by Puccinia coronata f. sp. avenae (Pca). This project seeks to generate resources and knowledge to advance our understanding of the disease and develop strategies to minimise yield losses to Pca.

records.title: Parkes observations for project P1420 semester 2026APRS_08
records.description: We propose the pilot of a Murriyang CryoPAF Pulsar Survey of the Southern Galactic Plane (CPS-LowLat Pilot). The revolutionary CryoPAF receiver delivers the highest pulsar survey speed in the Southern Hemisphere, exceeding L-band capability of MeerKAT by ~2x, with a sufficiently low data rate to enable archiving and reprocessing essential to maximizing survey yields. Population synthesis predicts ~300 new pulsars in the full CPS-LowLat. Up to ~90 pulsars are predicted from this Pilot in a rich region of the Galactic Plane (-15deg < l < -10deg, |b| < 3deg), including 5-10 millisecond pulsars. 2.5-hr pointings are proposed to provide the requisite transformational pulsar detection rate, while maintaining sensitivity across a wide range of binary orbital periods, including ultra-compact systems. A frequency range of 1.3-1.85 GHz will mitigate dispersion smearing and scattering. Well-developed GPU-based searches for accelerated / binary systems and efficient coherent folding algorithms will be deployed. New discoveries from CPS-LowLat will enable strong-field tests of general relativity, equation-of-state constraints from massive neutron stars, more accurate modeling of the neutron star merger rate, and probes of exotic stellar-evolution pathways and of the ionised interstellar medium. Besides its impressive pulsar yield and the associated scientific possibilities, the proposed pilot will demonstrate the end-to-end performance of the CryoPAF for pulsar surveys prior to commencing the full CPS-LowLat, and validate pulsar population models.

records.description: We propose a simultaneous joint observation campaign using the Parkes radio telescope and the EP satellite to observation three magnetars with known radio emission. Under simultaneous observations, we aim to investigate the correlation between their radio and X-ray emissions, including pulse profiles, flux intensity, polarization evolution, correlated multi-wavelength behavior and timing behavior.

records.title: Parkes observations for project P1365 semester 2026APRS_16
records.description: Following the successful demonstration of a pilot first-pass (shallow) search of a small fraction of the sky, the second-pass processing has commenced for the SMART pulsar survey, which involves deep searches of 80-minute observations. Over the past year, this second-pass processing has led to the discovery of 16 new pulsars (including two millisecond pulsars), bringing the total number of SMART discoveries to 20 when combined with the first-pass results. These outcomes hint at the exciting promise of this first southern-sky pulsar survey in the frequency band of SKA-Low. All new pulsars require timing observations to determine their spin and astrometric parameters. Another important aspect of timing newly discovered pulsars is to identify specialised targets for further detailed follow-ups. Since the MWA no longer supports routine pulsar observations from 2025, timing follow-ups rely on other telescopes. The Parkes Murriyang telescope, with an identical sky coverage, sensitivity and the wide frequency coverage, offers the best option to time SMART discoveries. We have demonstrated Murriyang's suitability for this through previous semesters and are now extending the project to a sample of 11 pulsars, including six from the last semester. The data will also allow us to study pulse profiles, polarisation, and flux densities from ~100 MHz to 4 GHz. The analysis/results will be included in a publication in preparation that will detail the deep-search pipeline and report on initial pulsar discoveries.

records.title: DNA methylation sequencing data from known-age Eucalyptus camaldulensis trees for epigenetic clock development
records.description: This collection contains raw RRBS sequence data and associated metadata from known-age Eucalyptus camaldulensis (river red gum) individuals. The data were generated to characterise age-associated DNA methylation patterns and develop an epigenetic clock for estimating the age of this long-lived hardwood species.

records.title: Annotated reference genome for Heteronotia binoei (prickly gecko)
records.description: This collection contains a chromosome-level genome assembly (FASTA format) and corresponding annotation file (General Feature Format) for the CA6 sexual lineage of Heteronotia binoei. This high-quality assembly will help unlock novel aspects of this Australian gecko's reproductive biology and evolutionary history. The isolate (CCM8108) was collected from Hamelin Station Homestead, WA in May 2022. The assembly consists of 198 scaffolds - 21 of which represent autosomes and an unidentified sex chromosome - with a BUSCO completeness of 94.2%, a contig N50 of 33137610, and a total length of 2.7Gb. The genome annotation features 7250 complete BUSCOs (96.9% completeness).

records.title: Sandy Soils II project
records.description: SS-II Output 1 NDVI Viewer', is a R Shiny app (see link in services tab) that allows the user to explore satellite-based crop growth (NDVI) across amelioration trial sites on sandy soils in low and medium rainfall areas of the Southern Region. The app visualises Sentinel-2 satellite imagery and derived crop growth curves from GRDC CSP2403-017RTX – Sandy Soils II project, Output 1 sites, which builds on the earlier GRDC CSP00203 amelioration trials. Output 1 is focused on where, when and how to ameliorate sands, using whole-of-paddock experimentation techniques, with optimised deep tillage treatments and amendments compared against no-tillage to test which parts of the landscape best respond to amelioration. The NDVI viewer draws on eight of these Output 1 trial sites in the Southern Cropping Region of Australia (South Australia and Victoria). Sites are affected by one or a combination of soil constraints, high soil strength, water repellence and/or poor soil fertility. Treatments include a deep ripping, spading and/or inclusion ripping treatments, with/without additional soil amendments. This app monitors the seasonal impact of amelioration treatments on crop growth using Sentinel-2 satellite NDVI imagery, providing a non-destructive, whole-of-season view of canopy development by treatment. To help visualise which parts of the landscape respond best to amelioration. Imagery was sourced via the Digital Earth Australia STAC catalog using the PAT_Sentinel QGIS plugin (CSIRO), filtered to exclude images where more than 30% of paddock pixels exceeded the cloud probability threshold, and processed to NDVI at 10 m resolution. The app presents data analysis outputs at the site level, consolidated by treatment and, soil zone. Outputs are descriptive rather than inferential: mean NDVI growth curves, cumulative NDVI, and area-under-the-curve (AUC) summaries are calculated per treatment for each site and season. No formal statistical testing is applied to the NDVI results presented in this app.

records.title: Tooth-billed bowerbirds videos - Barnes Pikle Nature Refuge 2018-2020
records.description: Tooth-billed bowerbird videos – During the display season months of October – December 2018-2020, motion-triggered automatic cameras were placed adjacent to Tooth-billed bowerbird (TBBB) courts at Barnes Pikle Nature Refuge (17°26’S by 145°32’E) near Tarzali in Wet Tropics upland rainforest between 860-960 m asl. There were nine TBBB courts, dispersed along a ridge, and were the only TBBB courts known to occur on Barnes Pikle’s southernmost ridge.

records.title: Parkes observations for project P1420 semester 2026APRS_10
records.description: We propose the pilot of a Murriyang CryoPAF Pulsar Survey of the Southern Galactic Plane (CPS-LowLat Pilot). The revolutionary CryoPAF receiver delivers the highest pulsar survey speed in the Southern Hemisphere, exceeding L-band capability of MeerKAT by ~2x, with a sufficiently low data rate to enable archiving and reprocessing essential to maximizing survey yields. Population synthesis predicts ~300 new pulsars in the full CPS-LowLat. Up to ~90 pulsars are predicted from this Pilot in a rich region of the Galactic Plane (-15deg < l < -10deg, |b| < 3deg), including 5-10 millisecond pulsars. 2.5-hr pointings are proposed to provide the requisite transformational pulsar detection rate, while maintaining sensitivity across a wide range of binary orbital periods, including ultra-compact systems. A frequency range of 1.3-1.85 GHz will mitigate dispersion smearing and scattering. Well-developed GPU-based searches for accelerated / binary systems and efficient coherent folding algorithms will be deployed. New discoveries from CPS-LowLat will enable strong-field tests of general relativity, equation-of-state constraints from massive neutron stars, more accurate modeling of the neutron star merger rate, and probes of exotic stellar-evolution pathways and of the ionised interstellar medium. Besides its impressive pulsar yield and the associated scientific possibilities, the proposed pilot will demonstrate the end-to-end performance of the CryoPAF for pulsar surveys prior to commencing the full CPS-LowLat, and validate pulsar population models.

records.title: Long-term project observations for project L147 semester 2026APRS_11
records.description: We propose to carry out a deep Galactic Bulge pulsar survey (GBps), covering the core of the Bulge region using the new cryoPAF system on Murriyang, the Parkes radio telescope. Such a deep survey is expected to discover a population of millisecond pulsars in the Galactic Bulge and reveal their distribution and gamma-ray emissions. With these, we will lead pioneering studies on the origin of gamma-ray emission in the Galactic Bulge, a longstanding mystery in modern astronomy. The outcome of this project will significantly advance our knowledge of the formation and evolution of millisecond pulsars in the Galactic Bulge, the origin and properties of high-energy emissions, and the nature of dark matter annihilation in the Galactic Centre. A total of 200 observations with the cryoPAF is required to cover a 400 square degree region (|gl|<10 deg, |gb|<10 deg). The survey is expected to be carried out over four semesters, from April 2026 to October 2027.

records.title: National Bushfire Intelligence Capability (NBIC) Terrain release 2.0
records.description: Existing national-scale elevation datasets often contain inconsistencies in spatial resolution, acquisition date, and vertical accuracy, and may include terrain artefacts in densely forested areas where radar-based methods can misrepresent vegetation canopy as ground surface [1]. These limitations can affect applications requiring accurate terrain representation, including bushfire behaviour modelling, hydrological analysis, and environmental assessment. This dataset provides a seamless, continental-scale bare-earth Digital Elevation Model (DEM) of Australia generated through the integration of multiple elevation datasets of varying resolution, date and source. A total of 1,549 open-access lidar-derived DEM datasets (513,620 individual files) were obtained through Geoscience Australia's Elevation Information System (ELVIS) and merged with the Shuttle Radar Topography Mission (SRTM) DEM [1]. All source datasets were standardised to a common coordinate reference system (EPSG:3577) and vertical datum (Australian Vertical Working Surface, AVWS). The final product provides national coverage of Australia at 90 m spatial resolution, matching the grid specification used for the National Bushfire Intelligence Capability (NBIC) Bushfire Fuels Classification 90 m dataset [2]. Processing included metadata extraction, quality ranking of source DEMs, vertical datum transformation, reprojection, DEM mosaicking and application of the DEM blending and smoothing method described in Gallant (2019) [3]. This continental implementation extends previous large-area DEM integration workflows [4] and includes additional procedures for standardised gridding and metadata harmonisation. Dataset quality was assessed using high-precision Permanent Survey Marks (PSM) acquired and cleaned from all redactions. Comparison with 100,463 independent PSM control points showed that the blended DEM achieved a statistically significant improvement in vertical accuracy relative to SRTM, reducing Root Mean Square Error (RMSE) from 3.32% (5.05 m to 4.88 m) and Mean Absolute Error (MAE) by 4.2% (3.32 m to 3.17 m), despite replacement datasets covering only 17% of the DEM extent. Most improvements were seen in high slope and elevation areas. The resulting dataset provides a nationally consistent, gap-free elevation surface suitable for bushfire behaviour modelling, vegetation mapping, hydrological studies, flood risk assessment and other environmental applications.

records.title: Conservation genomics of the Swan galaxias (Galaxias fontanus)
records.description: The Swan galaxias (Galaxias fontanus) is an endangered Tasmanian freshwater fish. We carried out a genome assembly and population genomic analysis to help with the conservation of the species. This genetic data has been used to inform conservation translocations and corresponds to data in a published paper. This includes a 612 Mb contig-level genome assembly generated using PacBio HiFi long-read sequencing and RNA-seq. We used ddRAD sequencing to characterise genetic diversity across the seven core G. fontanus populations (three natural and four translocated), measuring SNP variation against the genome assembly. In this collection we provide data (or links to datasets in other repositories - e.g. GenBank)

records.title: Sydney Science Park CSIRO Urban Living Lab datasets
records.description: The Sydney Science Park CSIRO Urban Living Lab (SSP-ULL) was established in 2019 and is an initiative of CSIRO and Celestino to undertake experimentation in a real-world setting to deal with the multiple and inter-related urban challenges Australia faces. Datasets have been collected to inform planning and design decisions at Sydney Science Park and are shared to encourage ongoing research leading to liveability, sustainability and resilience outcomes for Australian cities and suburbs.

records.title: HCAS 3.3 (1988-2024) base model estimate of habitat condition (90m grid), National Connectivity Index 2.0 (NCI) and annual time series for continental Australia
records.description: Citation: Valavi R, Levick SR, Lehmann EA, Liu N, Giljohann KM, Williams KJ, Collings S, Johnson S, Botha EJ, Munroe SEM, Van Niel TG, Newnham G, Paget M, Malley C, Carlile P, Gunawardana D, Lyon P, Richards AE, Tetreault Campbell S and Ferrier S (2025) HCAS 3.3 (1988-2024) base model estimate of habitat condition (90m grid), National Connectivity Index 2.0 (NCI) and annual time series for continental Australia. Data collection 65549. CSIRO, Canberra, Australia. DOI: https://data.csiro.au/collection/csiro:65549. The HCAS v3.3 data collection spans 37 years from (1988–2024), representing relative habitat condition for predominantly terrestrial biodiversity, and includes: • a 90 m gridded 37-year long-term epoch (base model) of Habitat Condition • 35 annual short-term 3-year rolling epochs of Habitat Condition from 1990 to 2024 • 33 annual short-term 5-year rolling epochs of Habitat Condition from 1992 to 2024 • 28 annual short-term 10-year rolling epochs of Habitat Condition from 1997 to 2024 • two additional long-term custom epochs (1988–2023 and 2001–2024) • model-based uncertainty estimates of habitat condition for the long-term epoch and selected 3-year epochs, expressed as 95% confidence interval limit derived using the bootstrap method of Lehmann et al. (2025) • ordinal classification of all habitat condition and derived condition products into six modification levels aligned with Vegetation Assets, States and Transitions (VAST) narrative framework (Thackway and Lesslie, 2006, 2008) • National Connectivity Index (NCI) v2.0 for long- and short-term and custom epochs (Giljohann et al., 2022) • Connectivity-adjusted Condition (NCIC) derived from the geometric mean of NCI and Habitat Condition for all epochs, and associated Landscape Context Effect (LCE) • Ecosystem Site Condition (ESC) derived from the geometric mean of Inferred Local Pressures (ILP) and Habitat Condition for all epochs, and associated Local Pressures Effect (LPE) • supporting datasets to aid interpretation and use, including reference sites and the 14 remotely sensed ecosystem characteristics (ecosystem condition variables) used as inputs; and • example summary tables and charts by IBRA bioregions for continental Australia, for the long-term and 3-year epochs of NCI and Habitat Condition, trends, and VAST-classified habitat condition. HCAS v3.3 (production version 3) derived using 'ClassicHCAS' software version 0.2.0 and 'HCAS-workflow' software version 1.2.1. The NCI and NCIC are developed by DCCEEW and included in the data collection along with other derivative products, for end user convenience. The NCI has been updated using HCAS v3.3 epochs. Raster datasets (*.tif) are Cloud Optimised GeoTIFFs at 90 m grid resolution, GDA 1994 (Australian Albers, EPSG:3577). Data extent is defined by any data pixel intersecting a coastline polygon as defined by the land fraction dataset (Liu 2024). HCAS v3.3 Habitat Condition indices vary continuously from a theoretical minimum of 0.0 (ecosystem integrity removed) to a maximum of 1.0 (ecosystem integrity in reference condition). NCI also ranges continuously from 0.0 (unconnected removed habitat) to a maximum of 1.0 (fully connected intact habitat), as does the NCIC: from 0.0 (landscape ecosystem integrity functionally extinguished) to a maximum of 1.0 (landscape ecosystem integrity functionally intact and in reference condition). Both the HCAS and NCIC represent the contribution that a given site (grid cell) makes to effective area of ecosystem integrity remaining within a spatial reporting unit, as a proportion of the contribution made by a site in reference condition. Data are described in "Habitat Condition Assessment System (HCAS) version 3.3: A guide to the 90-metre data collection. Technical report EP2025-2979. https://doi.org/10.25919/jz55-5d44" (available from CSIRO's publication repository, see related links). Narrative metadata is provided for selected data series (supporting documentation).

records.title: Archival chromatin short-read data for Heteronotia binoei (Prickly gecko)
records.description: The data consist of 150-bp paired-end Illumina sequencing reads from a chromatin conformation assay of 17 archival and 7 modern Heteronotia binoei specimens. Archival specimens, collected between 1960 and 1995, were formalin-fixed prior to long-term storage in ethanol. The archival specimens were collected, with approval, from the Australian National Wildlife Collection (ANWC) and the Western Australian Museum (WAM). Liver samples were taken from all specimens and treated with MNase to enrich for closed chromatin. The modern specimens were collected from Western Australia in April 2024 in accordance with the Australian National University Animal Ethics permit A2022/07. Flash-frozen liver tissue was sampled from these specimens immediately following euthanasia and 30mg was briefly fixed with formalin before being treated with MNase. The enriched DNA for both archival and modern samples was prepared for sequencing using the IDT xGen cfDNA & FFPE DNA library prep kit and sequenced across two Illumina NovaSeqX 10B flow cells. DNA was also extracted from ethanol-preserved tail tissue of one of the modern samples for use as an input control in the chromatin conformation assay. This sample was prepared using a Illumina DNA Prep M library prep kit and sequences across two lanes of a NovaSeqX 10B flow cell. These sequencing data are included in this collection.

records.title: Illumina short-read RNAseq reads for Heteronotia binoei parthenogens
records.description: This collection contains raw 150bp paired-end RNAseq reads in gzipped FASTQ format. A total of 22 Heteronotia binoei parthenogens are represented by these data, with ~40-50GB of reads available per sample.

records.title: Reference images, mitogenomes and COX1 DNA barcodes for Australian mosquitoes
records.description: Mosquitoes (Diptera: Culicidae) pose a biosecurity risk for Australia by affecting the health of humans, livestock and native animals. There are over 300 species of Australian mosquitoes, and several species are known vectors for serious human and animal arboviral pathogens (including Ross River virus, Barmah Forest virus, Murray Valley encephalitis virus, Japanese encephalitis virus, Kunjin virus and Dengue virus). Accurate, timely identification of each species underpins effective surveillance and response strategies but can be limited by lack of taxonomic knowledge and reliable reference datasets. This collection contains a database of images for 657 specimens representing 165 species of endemic Australian mosquitoes linked to DNA barcodes. A total of 1343 COX1 gene DNA barcode sequences (also available in GenBank) are included for 182 mosquito species, with 186 barcoded specimens (103 species) vouchered in the Australian National Insect Collection (ANIC). Complete mitogenome sequences (available fully annotated in GenBank) are also provided for 302 mosquito specimens (137 mosquito species). This resource will assist the identification of specimens with damage to key morphological characters or ambiguously identifiable specimens that are regularly encountered in surveillance programs. It will also facilitate identification of cryptic species or life stages lacking in morphological information such as early instar larvae. Wherever possible, high-resolution images of live, undamaged and reliably identified mosquitoes that display key diagnostic features are provided to assist morphological key-based identification in the absence of DNA sequence information.

records.title: Long-term ecological monitoring guides spatial prioritisation of coral reef restoration following an extreme marine heatwave - data and code
records.description: Climate-driven ecosystem degradation occurs at spatial scales far exceeding the capacity of direct restoration, creating an urgent need for frameworks that identify where intervention can maximise ecological benefit. We developed a restoration prioritisation framework integrating long-term ecological monitoring, habitat-specific reference conditions, and hierarchical Bayesian modelling to quantify historical resilience and post-disturbance need. We applied the framework following the extreme 2025 marine heatwave at northern Ningaloo Reef, Western Australia. We analysed 18 years of monitoring data (2007–2025), comprising 579 transects across 148 sites, four reef regions and four geomorphic habitats. Historical coral-cover trajectories at 83 sites were used to quantify resistance and recovery, integrated into a Historical Resilience Index (HRI). HRI was combined with post-heatwave restoration need, measured as the departure of 2025 coral cover from habitat-specific historical reference conditions, to identify restoration priorities. Historical resilience varied markedly among sites and habitats, while heatwave-driven coral mortality resulted in 52 of 83 sites (63%) being classified as the highest priority, “Restore Now”. Despite high historical resilience, 37 of 41 reef-slope sites were classified as Restore Now because of severe coral loss. In contrast, shallow reef flats exhibited lower and more variable historical resilience but were less frequently prioritised for restoration. This revealed a mismatch between ecological priority and operational feasibility, with many high-priority sites occurring in deeper, high-energy reef-slope habitats that are challenging and costly to restore. The HRI framework provides a transferable approach for targeting restoration using long-term monitoring data and adaptively updating priorities as disturbance regimes change.

records.title: CSIRO Discovery and Resources Characterisation (DaRC) Sample Collection Management System (CMR-Specify)
records.description: Preserving geo- samples for long-term reuse is essential for verification, reanalysis, and future research. The CSIRO Discovery and Resources Characterisation (DaRC) program maintains a diverse collection of geo-samples generated through mineral exploration and research since the 1970s. Historically, these collections have been managed independently by projects and researchers, resulting in fragmented practices that limit discoverability, accessibility, traceability, and reuse. This collection presents CMR-Specify, a digital collection management system built on the open-source Specify platform and configured for geo-sample management. CMR-Specify provides a centralised repository linking samples and sub-samples with projects, collections, collecting events, hierarchical storage locations, associated resources, contributor roles, and collection-management activities including reporting, querying, labelling, loans, and disposals. CMR-Specify supports key sample management functions, including sample search and discovery, metadata management, sample loading and relocation, and label and report generation. It integrates with research and field services, including Fieldmark for field data capture and the CSIRO Spectroscopy Reflectance Database for contextual and analytical data, and uses International Generic Sample Number (IGSN) DOI services for persistent identification and discovery. Together, these capabilities transform fragmented project-based sample holdings into a connected, traceable, and reusable research collection, supporting the long-term preservation, accessibility, citation, and reuse of samples in the program.

records.title: Parkes observations for project P1416 semester 2026APRS_09
records.description: Radio pulsars in orbit around high-mass stellar companions offer a rich source of extreme physics for both observational astronomers and theorists alike. Despite being discovered 25 years ago, PSR J1638-4725 remains a veritable mystery compared to similar pulsar binary systems. Long-term monitoring has revealed extended `eclipses' where the pulsar is undetectable for months around periastron at GHz frequencies, along with intense variations in the observed pulsar dispersion measure, scatter broadening and flux density throughout the entire orbit. Preliminary spectroscopic characterisation of the companion star suggests it may be an O/B star, albiet one without a circumstellar disc of ejected material. This raises the unique opportunity to answer test the structure and origin of the near-wind regime of high-mass stars. In this proposal we will conduct an ambitious monitoring campaign of PSR J1638-4725 with both the ultra-wideband low and MARS recievers on Murriyang. We will track changes in the pulsar dispersion and scattering as it swings around the companion star, providing unique insights into the density and temperature distribution of the stellar wind from the companion star before and after the pulsar swings through periastron. These observations will also play a pivotal role in a broader multi-wavelength campaign to fully capture the upcoming 2026 periastron passage.

records.title: Parkes observations for project P1392 semester 2026APRS_01
records.description: Since their discovery in 1968, pulsars have served as laboratories to study extreme physics. Pulsars are born out of core-collapse supernovae, however their early life and subsequent evolution are still poorly understood. SN 1987A was a core-collapse supernova from a blue supergiant star in the Large Magellanic Cloud (LMC), which was discovered in 1987. The discovery of this source was associated with neutrino detection, which strongly suggested the birth of a young pulsar. There have been multiple radio campaigns spanning ~3 decades to find dispersed radio pulsations from the source. However, no dispersed signal has been found to date. The lack of detection has mainly been attributed to the dense surrounding nebula, which could obscure radio emission, though the nebula is expected to become less dense over time as it expands. Recently, James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) observations revealed Argon emission lines near the centre of the source, which suggests the presence of a central neutron star. Hence, coupled with evidence of the possibility of a central neutron star and the advances in the software and hardware instrumentation since the last search for a pulsar using Murriyang in 2018 (e.g., wide bandwidth instruments such as the UWL, high-frequency MARS receiver, robust subbanded search algorithms), we plan to conduct a fresh search for a pulsar at the center of SN 1987A. A detection of any radio pulses in the proposed search will provide crucial insights into the birth and evolution of a pulsar from such early stages.

Compiled from high-throughput screening and optimisation experiments performed at the Collaborative Crystallisation Centre (C3)

records.title: Resradar
records.description: This repository contains the code and data-processing pipelines for the paper "How similar are protein crystallisation conditions? A Data-Driven Deep Learning Approach to Quantifying Similarity". It learns a similarity metric for protein crystallisation reservoir conditions. The pipeline preprocesses screening data, calculates baseline chemical distances, and trains a transformer model to embed reservoir conditions. The model positions chemically and experimentally similar conditions closer together in the embedding space.

Such a deep survey is expected to discover a population of millisecond pulsars in the Galactic Bulge and reveal their distribution and gamma-ray emissions. With these, we will lead pioneering studies on the origin of gamma-ray emission in the Galactic Bulge, a longstanding mystery in modern astronomy. The outcome of this project will significantly advance our knowledge of the formation and evolution of millisecond pulsars in the Galactic Bulge, the origin and properties of high-energy emissions, and the nature of dark matter annihilation in the Galactic Centre. A total of 200 observations with the cryoPAF is required to cover a 400 square degree region (|gl|<10 deg, |gb|<10 deg). The survey is expected to be carried out over four semesters, from April 2026 to October 2027.

records.title: Beaufort River AEM Project Data
records.description: A compilation of airborne electromagnetic (AEM) survey data for the area surrounding Beaufort River, Western Australia. The AEM data was collected using the SkyTEM 312 system. Data have been processed and inverted using stitched 1D layered earth models including induced polarisation effects using Cole-Cole parameters for chargeability, time-constant, and exponent factor. Included are the processed data and inverted models. Cross sections of the modeled electrical conductivity

records.title: Parkes observations for project P1416 semester 2026APRS_13
records.description: Radio pulsars in orbit around high-mass stellar companions offer a rich source of extreme physics for both observational astronomers and theorists alike. Despite being discovered 25 years ago, PSR J1638-4725 remains a veritable mystery compared to similar pulsar binary systems. Long-term monitoring has revealed extended `eclipses' where the pulsar is undetectable for months around periastron at GHz frequencies, along with intense variations in the observed pulsar dispersion measure, scatter broadening and flux density throughout the entire orbit. Preliminary spectroscopic characterisation of the companion star suggests it may be an O/B star, albiet one without a circumstellar disc of ejected material. This raises the unique opportunity to answer test the structure and origin of the near-wind regime of high-mass stars. In this proposal we will conduct an ambitious monitoring campaign of PSR J1638-4725 with both the ultra-wideband low and MARS recievers on Murriyang. We will track changes in the pulsar dispersion and scattering as it swings around the companion star, providing unique insights into the density and temperature distribution of the stellar wind from the companion star before and after the pulsar swings through periastron. These observations will also play a pivotal role in a broader multi-wavelength campaign to fully capture the upcoming 2026 periastron passage.

records.title: Parkes observations for project P960 semester 2026APRS_16
records.description: We aim to carry out receiver pointing and characterisation tests of Parkes receivers. Typically, these tests are carried out after the receiver package is installed, but time does not always allow for proper characterisation. Receivers for consideration include UWL, MARS and 13MM packages. In addition to cross-referencing C007 for flux calibration via pointing, we aim to conduct gain-elevation and system temperature experiments using the Moon, to ensure users of the Parkes Observatory have the most accurate information available for calibration purposes.

records.title: Dissolved inorganic carbon in surface waters, the water column and sediment porewaters of the East Australian Current and Tasman Sea, RV Investigator voyage IN2016_V04
records.description: This collection contains dissolved inorganic carbon (DIC) measurements collected aboard RV Investigator during voyage IN2016_V04 in waters of the East Australian Current and Tasman Sea off eastern Australia. DIC was measured using an Apollo SciTech AS-C3 dissolved inorganic carbon analyser configured for semi-continuous underway measurements and analysis of discrete seawater samples. The current dataset contains semi-continuous underway DIC measurements from the vessel's continuous surface seawater supply. Seawater was filtered through a 5 µm cartridge filter prior to DIC analysis. Temperature and salinity measured by the ship's underway CTD were used to calculate seawater density and express DIC concentrations in µmol kg⁻¹. A variable time offset between the DIC analyser and underway CTD records was manually estimated at approximately six-hour intervals and interpolated across the dataset before matching temperature and salinity to individual DIC measurements. The DIC system was calibrated approximately every 12 hours using Certified Reference Material supplied by A. G. Dickson, Scripps Institution of Oceanography, with DIC calculation and calibration following the AS-C3 operating procedures. The collection is intended to include three components: semi-continuous underway surface-water measurements, discrete water-column measurements from CTD/Niskin samples, and sediment porewater measurements. Only the underway dataset is currently included. The discrete water-column and sediment porewater DIC data are undergoing quality-control review and will be added to the collection when that review is complete. Data access is currently restricted while the collection is being prepared for release.

records.title: Eddy covariance air-sea CO2 and CH4 fluxes and ancillary measurements at the Lucinda Jetty Coastal Observatory (LJCO), Great Barrier Reef, 2021-2024.
records.description: This collection contains eddy covariance measurements of air–sea carbon dioxide (CO2) and methane (CH4) fluxes, together with supporting meteorological and radiation measurements, made at the Lucinda Jetty Coastal Observatory (LJCO) in the Great Barrier Reef lagoon, north Queensland, Australia, between 2021 and 2024. The measurements were made as a test deployment to evaluate the performance of a commercial eddy covariance system for direct air–sea greenhouse gas flux measurement in a tropical coastal setting. LJCO was selected as the test site because it is co-located with an established IMOS observing facility, providing existing infrastructure, power, communications and routine site access alongside complementary long-term oceanographic and atmospheric observations, and because the jetty provides an extended open-water footprint suitable for eddy covariance measurement. The system comprises a LI-COR LI-7200RS enclosed-path CO2/H2O analyser, a LI-COR LI-7700 open-path CH4 analyser and a Gill WindMaster Pro sonic anemometer, logged through a LI-COR data acquisition and Biomet system. Ancillary measurements include net radiation (Kipp & Zonen CNR4, ventilated), air temperature and relative humidity (Vaisala HMP155), photosynthetically active radiation, rainfall (tipping-bucket rain gauge) and time-lapse site imagery. Data status: the data currently in this collection are raw, unprocessed measurements that have not been quality controlled. Quality-controlled flux data and relavent reporting will be added to the collection as they become available.

records.title: SEMO error-mitigated and standard quantum annealing and classical computing solutions of weighted Max-Cut on cubic lattice
records.description: The weighted Max-Cut is a NP hard problem with application implications. This collection includes Python script and numerical results solving the Max-Cut problem on a cubic lattice with 11x11x11 nodes and random edge weights with mixed signs. Solution time with a novel SEMO (spin-error mitigation for optimisation) error-mitigated quantum annealing for the problem is compared with the standard D-Wave quantum annealing and BQM hybrid solvers, and various classical solvers including simulated annealing, Tabu search, Goemans-Williamson and Goemans-Williamson-inspired algorithms. It has been quantitatively demonstrated that the SEMO error-mitigated quantum annealing is outperforming other approaches. The error-mitigated quantum annealing approach presented in this article would be applicable in solving other discrete optimisation problems efficiently, which is particularly impactful for certain time-critical applications.

records.title: Parkes observations for project P1406 semester 2026APRS_07
records.description: NGC 362 is a post-core-collapse southern globular cluster (GC) where 12 pulsars have recently been discovered. The pulsar population is very diverse, containing extremely fast-spinning, mildly recycled and slow pulsars, the vast majority of which (11 out of 12) are part of binary systems with very different orbital periods and eccentricities. However, a full orbital characterization was possible only for three of these binaries. This is because the pulsars in NGC 362 are heavily affected by scintillation, and therefore are very elusive. Here, we propose to carry out a series of deep observations of NGC 362, taking advantage of the ultra-wide bandwidth of the UWL receiver, with the aim of determining the orbital parameters of the 8 binary pulsars that still lack characterization. This is of utmost importance, as it is the prerequisite for the derivation of their timing solutions. The latter would in turn allow a wealth of potential studies, such as probing the presence of a mass excess at the center of NGC 362, looking for optical and X-ray counterparts, studying the magnetic field at arcsecond scales, and more. These kinds of studies are only possible in clusters that host many pulsars. With its 12 pulsars, NGC 362 harbors a huge scientific potential, which we aim to unlock by characterizing its binaries. Moreover, we may discover additional pulsars thanks to fortuitous scintillation events.

records.title: Long-term project observations for project L101 semester 2026APRS_08
records.description: The Parkes Pulsar Timing Array (PPTA) project has three primary goals: (a) detection of gravitational waves from astronomical sources, (b) establishment of a pulsar timescale, and (c) improvement of our understanding of Solar-system dynamics. We are now in an exciting regime where a signal detected in our (and other data sets) has the form expected for a gravitational wave background. We, along with the international community, are now working hard to either confirm or deny this result, and to determine the astrophysical origin of this signal. With this proposal, we aim to maintain our pre-eminent position in the field. This is a continuing proposal for which observations of millisecond pulsars (MSPs) will continue to improve bounds on ultra-low-frequency gravitational waves until they are detected with confidence. Continued Parkes observations will remain valuable at least until the first stage of the SKA is able to improve on our sensitivity and observing cadence. Even after the gravitational wave background is detected, continued observations will resolve the background origin and individual sources will be identified; advancing the nascent field of gravitational wave astronomy.

records.title: Long-term project observations for project L126 semester 2026APRS_19
records.description: We propose a modest program to continue monitoring 4 of the 6 known radio magnetars in order to achieve three primary science goals. The first is to characterise magnetar outbursts over long timescales, for which tracking their rotational, flux density, and polarisation properties provide a clear view of the impulse response of their magnetic fields. Second, understanding the links between magnetars the mysterious fast radio burst phenomenon through the discovery of rare emission and propagation effects, shared spectro-temporal phenomenology, and connections to high-energy (X-ray/gamma-ray) phenomena. Lastly, our continued monitoring has enormous benefit to the wider magnetar community, providing rapid alerts to changes in activity, adding context to unusual behaviour detected by high-energy observations, and a host of supplementary science through the teams extensive collaborative networks. The project and its precursors have been running since 2007 and have contributed to 22 publications since then. This is the first submission since the project was converted to long-term status.

records.title: Parkes observations for project P1032 semester 2026APRS_14
records.description: With this proposal, we aim to continue P1032, the rapid measurements of relativistic parameters of southern binary pulsar systems using data from the Parkes Ultra Wideband Low (UWL) receiver. As the MeerTime project at the MeerKAT radio telescope ended in early 2024, observations with the UWL receiver now form the backbone for extending the timing baselines of many pulsars that have been part of this project. Since the source selection in the previous semesters was tailored such that the UWL receiver is the most (versatile and) suited instrument to achieve the proposed scientific goals for the chosen pulsars, we propose to continue these observations. We will use the UWL data to obtain significant orbital coverage and timing baselines on these pulsars and obtain important constraints on orbital and temporal DM variations that will help in identifying the nature of the companion stars. Increasing the number of measured Neutron Star (NS) masses, as well as improving on current constraints has profound implications for NS internal structure and for stellar and binary evolution physics.

records.title: Long-term project observations for project L100 semester 2026APRS_13
records.description: We request time to observe 270 pulsars on a regular basis in order to achieve three main science goals. The first is to understand pulsars: how do they spin down and what disrupts this process, how and why their profiles vary with time, whether they precess or have planetary mass companions, in short all the things that make pulsar timing noisier than the perfect clock. Secondly we want to understand the interstellar medium of our Galaxy through repeated monitoring of dispersion measure, rotation measure and flux density variations in conjunction with scintillation parameters. Finally, we provide these data as a community service both to the high-energy community where we have strong collaborative links (particularly to Fermi) and to the radio pulsar astronomers generally through the CSIRO archive. The project is on-going since 2007, we are (co-)authors on 107 papers arising from the P574 data. The data have contributed to the PhD theses of students from Bordeaux, Manchester, Oxford, Stanford, and Swinburne. We are seeking long-term project status with a view to continuing the project into the SKA era.

records.title: CDR survey dashboard
records.description: This service connects to an online dashboard where users can interactively explore data from a national survey investigating Australian public views on novel carbon dioxide removal (CDR). Conducted in June 2025, the survey included 2,488 respondents and examined awareness and support for CDR, perceived risks and benefits, views on ocean alkalinity enhancement and mineral carbonation, and preferences for responsible development, governance and deployment. The dashboard is designed to complement the project reports and related publications available from the project website (https://research.csiro.au/cdr-perceptions) and provides an opportunity to explore the survey findings beyond what is possible in a static report.

records.title: From Buoys to CCHaPS: Tracking 40 Years of Extreme Waves along Australia's East Coast
records.description: This collection documents a reproducible analysis of long-term extreme significant wave heights (Hs) along Australia’s east coast, prepared for the 4th Wind Wave Symposium in Perth in 2025. Annual maximum Hs observations from 14 offshore wave buoys between Cairns and Eden are compared with co-located data from two Australian Climate Service wave hindcasts: WHACS and CCHaPS. The analysis estimates empirical return intervals and 100-year wave-height return levels; compares stationary Gumbel, Generalised Extreme Value (GEV) and mixed-climate two-Gumbel models; and investigates long-term changes using non-stationary Gumbel models. The collection includes derived annual-maximum datasets, buoy locations, reproducible R Markdown code, figures, tables and the rendered HTML workflow. It supports evaluation of how well wave hindcasts reproduce observed extreme-wave behaviour, including regional differences associated with tropical-cyclone and non-tropical-cyclone wave climates and evidence for changes through time.

records.title: Consumption based emissions intensity of the NEM
records.description: State level consumption based carbon emissions intensity factors calculated using a power flow-tracing model of the National Electricity Market.

records.title: Kautilya_PhD_Chapter_1
records.description: Chapter 1 of Kautilya's PhD characterises bacterial communities across two Western Australian estuarine systems: the Swan-Canning Estuary, the Leschenault Estuary, and the Ashfield Flats wetland. This dataset provides 16S rRNA (V3-V4 region) raw sequences for Ashfield Flats wetland only. The goal was to examine existing microbial communities and assess their potential plastic-degradation capabilities within the Ashfield Flats wetland. Sampling for the Ashfield data was carried out in 2020. The samples collected were sediments.

records.title: Kautilya_PhD_Chapter 3
records.description: Chapter 3 presents a manipulative field experiment at Herdsman Lake, an urban wetland in metropolitan Perth, examining the microbial communities that colonise plastic buried in sediment and whether they carry the genetic capacity to degrade it. Low-density polyethylene (LDPE) films were deployed as the test substrate alongside polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) as an inert negative control, buried for 90 days and retrieved across a time series together with paired bulk sediment samples. Genomic DNA was extracted from plastic-associated biofilms and sediment and sequenced by shotgun metagenomics. The microbes and genes associated with LDPE degradation were looked at, along with physicochemical changes of plastics

records.title: Kautilya_PhD_Chapter_2
records.description: Chapter 2 presents a multi-ecosystem survey of plastic and the associated plastisphere across the aquatic ecosystems of metropolitan Western Australia, profiling both bacterial (16S rRNA) and fungal (ITS) communities. The sequencing data were obtained via full-length PacBio CCS amplicon sequencing. Eleven sites were sampled across four ecosystem types: estuarine (Claremont Jetty, Matilda Bay Foreshore, South Perth Boatramp), wetland (Eric Singleton Wetland, Berringa Park Wetland, Salter Point Lagoon), beach (Scarborough Beach, South Beach, Mangles Bay) and island (Rottnest Island, Penguin Island). The design allows substrate effects (plastic versus sediment) to be separated from environmental context, which is the central question of the chapter. Sampling was conducted 2024. The samples collected comprised of plastic and sediments.

records.title: Parkes observations for project P1418 semester 2026APRS_07
records.description: Pulsars exhibit diverse radio-emission phenomena that remain poorly understoon. Among the most extreme are giant pulses (GPs): short-duration radio bursts whose energies exceed the average pulse by at least 10 times. Only 16 pulsars are known to emit GPs, including just five millisecond pulsars. This rises the question of whether this reflects intrinsic population differences or observational bias. We propose high time-resolution observations with Murriyang Ultra Wide-bandwidth Low-frequency (UWL) receiver to search for and characterise GPs from two prominent millisecond pulsar candidates, PSR J0030+0451 and PSR J1902-5105. Both share key properties with established GP emitters including large magnetic fields at the light-cylinder and high energy emission in X and gamma ray. These observations will provide essential clues to understanding how GPs are generated and what is their relation to average radio and high energy emissions in terms of their production mechanisms and locations within the pulsars magnetosphere.

records.title: Parkes observations for project P1402 semester 2026APRS_25
records.description: We propose a dedicated Parkes/Murriyang timing campaign of the newly confirmed narrow-duty cycle (~6 %) millisecond pulsar (MSP) PSR J2147-3604. This source was identified in a reprocessing of the Green Bank North Celestial Cap (GBNCC) survey as a high-confidence candidate with a spin period of 3.2 ms, and a dispersion measure, DM of 17 pc/cc. The pulsar was subsequently confirmed by the Fermi--TRAPUM collaboration via MeerKAT beamforming localisation and Parkes follow-up. Parkes/UWL observations allocated using green time detected this pulsar between 700--1500~MHz, and confirmed that it's in a binary system. Due to its low DM, we also detected strong interstellar scintillation. We request 35~hr of Murriyang time using the UWL receiver and APOLLO backend to obtain a phase-coherent timing solution and to characterise its spin, orbital, and propagation properties. Since the pulsar is also associated with a FERMI source, a precise radio ephemeris will also enable sensitive searches for gamma-ray pulsations in Fermi-LAT data and assess PSR J2147-3604's suitability for pulsar timing arrays (PTAs) and future gamma-ray timing applications.

records.title: A Standard Metadata Template For Representing Water Samples
records.description: This dataset provides a standardized template for representing metadata associated with water specimens (including groundwater and surface water) within the CSIRO Mineral Resources Discovery program. It captures core sample properties such as name, identifier, type, and location, along with related contextual metadata including project details, sampling information, and key water measurements (e.g. pH and Eh). Developed iteratively with input from researchers and laboratory technicians, the template supports the systematic curation and management of both legacy and newly collected mineral exploration samples through the CMR Specify collection management system. This standardization reduces duplicate data entry and metadata redundancy, while improving sample curation, management, and discoverability.

records.title: The red algal genus Callithamniella (Rhodophyta, Ceramiaceae) in Australia, including two new species C. cygnora and C. carolyniae
records.description: This collection contains data supporting the associated publication 'The red algal genus Callithamniella (Rhodophyta, Ceramiaceae) in Australia, including two new species C. cygnora and C. carolyniae' by Huisman et al., published in Nuytsia [link to be confirmed]. The study investigated phylogenetic relationships of the red algae genus Callithamniella, and the description of two new species. The study was based on plastid data derived from genome skimming data generated by the National Biodiversity DNA Library as part of the Marine Parks Australia Ocean Discovery and Restoration grant campaign on Marine Invertebrates, macroalgae, and seagrass, supported by Bioplatforms Australia, NCRIS, and Illumina.

records.title: Long-term project observations for project L124 semester 2026APRS_11
records.description: We propose a long-term project to monitor a very active repeater, FRB 20190520B, with Murriyang's UWL system. Our previous observations show that FRB 20190520B is not only among the most active FRBs that can be observed with Murriyang, but also shows extreme rotation measure (RM) and dispersion measure (DM) evolution, along with distinctive behavior at 3GHz frequency. This makes the UWL receiver uniquely suited for detailed studies and long-term monitoring of this repeating FRB. Through this program, we anticipate detecting a large sample of bursts from this FRB. In collaboration with FAST, we aim to investigate the time evolution of various properties of FRB 20190520B, enhance our understanding of polarisation across an extremely wide bandwidth with high sensitivity, and gain deeper insights into the local environment and emission mechanisms of FRBs.
