In addition to cross-referencing C007 for flux calibration via pointing, we aim to conduct gain-elevation and system temperature experiments using the Moon, to ensure users of the Parkes Observatory have the most accurate information available for calibration purposes.

records.title: Parkes observations for project P1390 semester 2026APRS_05
records.description: We propose 18.9 hours of Parkes Ultra-Wideband (UWL) observations to investigate PSR J1606-0854, a remarkable nearby Galactic pulsar discovered via the ASKAP CRACO backend. This source exhibits unprecedented emission properties that challenge conventional classification boundaries: it produces ultra-bright bursts (up to 900 Jy ms) with broad durations (~ 20 ms), extremely faint RRAT-like emission (0.02-0.5 Jy ms), but notably lacks intermediate-fluence pulses (1-10 Jy ms). The fluence distribution spans five orders of magnitude, with a surface magnetic field strength of B_surf ~ 1.3e14 G comparable to magnetars, and is the highest among known RRATs. High-sensitivity FAST observations conducted since July 2025 have detected over 100 pulses. With Parkes complementary sensitivity and wideband spectral coverage (0.7-4 GHz), we will search for the missing intermediate-fluence pulses and characterize the source's broadband spectrum. This study provides a unique laboratory for understanding neutron-star emission mechanisms across an unprecedented dynamic range, probing the faint end of the neutron-star emission continuum, and investigating the evolutionary connections between classical pulsars, rotating radio transients, and magnetars.

records.title: Parkes observations for project P1200 semester 2026APRS_04
records.description: We propose to use a single CryoPAF beam for high precision pulsar timing experiments to determine whether pulsar timing projects, such as P456, should continue with the UWL or transition to the CryoPAF, which has a lower system temperature in the overlapping bands and no requirement for extra calibration observations. We will observe three of the best timed pulsars and compare the resulting observations with those from P456. These pulsars are J1909-3744, J1744-1134, and J1713+0747. records.title: Parkes observations for project P1032 semester 2026APRS_17
records.description: With this proposal, we aim to continue P1032, the rapid measurements of relativistic parameters of southern binary pulsar systems using data from the Parkes Ultra Wideband Low (UWL) receiver. As the MeerTime project at the MeerKAT radio telescope ended in early 2024, observations with the UWL receiver now form the backbone for extending the timing baselines of many pulsars that have been part of this project. Since the source selection in the previous semesters was tailored such that the UWL receiver is the most (versatile and) suited instrument to achieve the proposed scientific goals for the chosen pulsars, we propose to continue these observations. We will use the UWL data to obtain significant orbital coverage and timing baselines on these pulsars and obtain important constraints on orbital and temporal DM variations that will help in identifying the nature of the companion stars. Increasing the number of measured Neutron Star (NS) masses, as well as improving on current constraints has profound implications for NS internal structure and for stellar and binary evolution physics.

records.title: Parkes observations for project P1054 semester 2026APRS_41
records.description: With this proposal we ask time to continue our timing follow-up campaign of pulsars discovered with the MeerKAT telescope. Fiftythree sources have been discovered in targeted observations of Fermi unidentified point sources, two towards Supernova Remnants, 27 in the Magellanic Clouds, 109 in Globular Clusters and 96 in a survey of the Galactic plane. A large fraction of the new discoveries are recycled pulsars (including a few relativistic systems, a pulsar with a planetary companion and several 'spider' binaries), or young pulsars. Timing observations have an essential role in exploiting the full potential of any pulsar discovery, allowing for the precise measurement of rotational, astrometric and orbital parameters which, in turn, give us powerful tools to improve our understanding of the physics in extreme environments as well as of the population of neutron stars as a whole. The UWL receiver of the Parkes telescope is a sensitive, versatile instrument that is allowing us to successfully time these new sources, in the bright-end of TRAPUM discoveries.

records.title: Parkes observations for project P1413 semester 2026APRS_29
records.description: We request 75 hours of Parkes observing time for dedicated radio follow-up observations of PSR J1635-5134, a promising candidate pulsar-subdwarf B (sdB) star binary system. PSR J1635-5134 is a non-recycled 340 ms pulsar in a nearly circular 18-hour orbit with a minimum companion mass of 0.26 solar mass. It lies in a sparsely populated region of binary-pulsars parameter space and may represent a short-lived evolutionary stage immediately following inefficient spin-up, thereby providing a missing link between canonical binaries and the millisecond pulsar-WD population. The system exhibits peculiar, orbital-phase-dependent dispersion-measure (DM) variability, with DM variations exceeding 30 pc/cc, indicating substantial ionised material plausibly associated with an outflow from the companion. Moreover, during prior monitoring with Parkes, the DM variations shifted from being predominantly modest to being persistently large, implying an evolving plasma environment that cannot be characterised with sparse or irregular observations. Determining whether these high-DM variations are intermittent or long-lived, and mapping how the excess material varies with orbital phase and epoch, are essential for constraining the origin and geometry of the plasma and for testing the hypothesis that an sdB wind supplies the required electron column. Through this proposal, we aim to (i) extend the timing baseline to improve astrometric precision to sub-arcsecond accuracy, enabling secure identification of the optical counterpart in a crowded field, and (ii) perform phase-targeted observations during eclipse/DM variation phases to understand the temporal behavior of excess DM.

records.title: Australian Phytoplankton Microscopy Machine Learning Dataset
records.description: The Australian Phytoplankton Microscopy Machine Learning Dataset is an annotated collection of laboratory microscopy imagery developed to support the training and evaluation of deep learning object detection models for microalgae identification. The collection comprises ten datasets derived from the CSIRO Australian Phytoplankton Microscopy Dataset (CAPMD) source imagery. The collection spans three optical contrast modes (bright field, differential interference contrast, phase contrast), four objective magnifications (200X, 400X, 630X, 1000X) and two microscope platforms (Zeiss Axio Observer, Zeiss Axio Plan). The principal dataset is a multi-species training set covering ten species, most of them harmful algal bloom (HAB) taxa of monitoring interest, imaged at 630X under bright field microscopy on the Zeiss Axio Observer. Nine additional single-species datasets document Heterosigma akashiwo (strain CS1197) under controlled variation of optical contrast mode, objective magnification, and microscope platform, enabling quantification of cross-condition model transferability. Five datasets are provided with train, validation, and test partitions for direct model training. The remaining five serve as held-out cross-condition evaluation targets. All datasets are shipped in YOLO detection format, accompanied by the source segmentation polygons in COCO format, with an additional MMDetection-format copy of the multi-species dataset provided to support reproduction of the Faster R-CNN and Deformable DETR results reported in the companion paper.

records.title: Legume Termination Timing, Nitrogen Contribution and Legacy Effects in Companion Cropping Systems Field Trial Data, Goomalling Trial 1, Goomalling, Western Australia, 2025-2026
records.description: This collection contains observational data and metadata from a two-year field experiment conducted at Goomalling, Western Australia, from 2025 to 2026. The experiment was established to evaluate legume-based nitrogen management strategies and mixed cropping systems as pathways to reduce reliance on synthetic nitrogen fertiliser in Western Australian grain production systems. The experiment investigated the productivity, nitrogen contribution and residual nitrogen legacy effects of wheat grown in association with contrasting grain legume species. Treatments included wheat monocultures with and without nitrogen fertiliser, monoculture grain crops of Coyote lupin and Morava vetch, monoculture brown manure crops terminated at contrasting timings, and wheat-legume companion cropping and intercrop systems. The subsequent year assessed residual impacts on soil fertility and wheat performance under contrasting nitrogen fertiliser treatments. Key research questions relating to: Productivity and performance of lupin- and vetch-based mixed cropping systems. Nitrogen contribution from grain and brown manure legume systems. Effects of early (first-flower) versus late (first-flower plus one month) termination of companion and brown manure legumes on biomass production, nitrogen accumulation and residual benefits to subsequent crops. Residual nitrogen benefits to subsequent wheat crops. Trade-offs between grain harvest, biomass production and nitrogen retention. Effects of legume species and management strategies on system productivity and nitrogen cycling. The dataset includes plot-level, crop-component and subsample observations collected throughout the experiment. Measurements include crop establishment, plant height, biomass production, nodulation status, soil mineral nitrogen, yield components, grain yield and grain quality traits. Associated metadata describe trial design, treatment structure, crop species, nitrogen fertiliser treatments, sampling stages and experimental layout. The current release may not include all datasets generated by the experiment. Additional datasets undergoing processing and quality assurance may be included in future releases as they become available. Goomalling Trial 1 forms part of a broader research program evaluating legume-based nitrogen management strategies across multiple locations and environments in Western Australia. Related experiments were conducted at Beverley (Avondale Trial 1, Avondale Trial 2 and Avondale Trial 3), Goomalling (Goomalling Trial 2) and Perillup, with varying treatment structures and research objectives. Users interested in cross-site comparisons should consult the associated datasets and metadata for each trial.

records.title: Inter-Row Wheat-Lupin Management, Termination Timing and Nitrogen Legacy Effects Field Trial Data, Goomalling Trial 2, Goomalling, Western Australia, 2025-2026
records.description: This collection contains observational data and metadata from a two-year field experiment conducted at Goomalling, Western Australia, from 2025 to 2026. Legume rows were terminated either by herbicide sprayout, leaving biomass on the soil surface, or by mechanical cultivation, incorporating legume biomass into the soil. Both management approaches were applied at contrasting termination timings, enabling comparison of early (first-flower) and late (first-flower plus one month) legume termination. The subsequent year assessed residual impacts on soil fertility and wheat performance under contrasting nitrogen fertiliser treatments. Effects of herbicide sprayout versus cultivation and incorporation of legume biomass on nitrogen cycling and residual fertility. -Nitrogen contribution from lupin-based systems. -Residual nitrogen benefits to subsequent wheat crops. -Trade-offs between grain production, biomass retention, incorporation of organic matter and nitrogen availability. The dataset includes plot-level, crop-component and subsample observations collected throughout the experiment. records.title: Long-term project observations for project L125 semester 2026APRS_29
records.description: The atomic interstellar medium shows tiny-scale optical depth fluctuations on the scale of 0.1~10,000 AU, whose origin and nature are poorly understood. The existence of this Tiny-Scale Atomic Structure (TSAS) has significant implications, potentially calling into question our fundamental understanding of heating, cooling and dynamical processes in the interstellar medium. Yet observations remain sparse. This long-term project plans to search for temporal variations in HI absorption spectra seen against background pulsars to characterise TSAS in the Milky Way interstellar medium (ISM). These observations constitute the largest number of sightlines and densest temporal sampling ever performed in a single experiment, and will test predictions that TSAS is the tail end of a turbulent cascade, constrain its minimum size scale (down to resolutions of ~0.05 AU) and potentially provide the first direct measurements of pressures in "large" TSAS features of > 1000 AU. We make use of the phase-resolved spectral line mode that we have recently implemented on Parkes, which has cut data rates and processing times by factors of ~1000 compared to past studies. This is an expansion of our pilot P1321 to a long term study.

records.title: Long-term project observations for project L147 semester 2026APRS_25
records.description: We propose to carry out a deep Galactic Bulge pulsar survey (GBps), covering the core of the Bulge region using the new cryoPAF system on Murriyang, the Parkes radio telescope. Such a deep survey is expected to discover a population of millisecond pulsars in the Galactic Bulge and reveal their distribution and gamma-ray emissions. With these, we will lead pioneering studies on the origin of gamma-ray emission in the Galactic Bulge, a longstanding mystery in modern astronomy. The outcome of this project will significantly advance our knowledge of the formation and evolution of millisecond pulsars in the Galactic Bulge, the origin and properties of high-energy emissions, and the nature of dark matter annihilation in the Galactic Centre. A total of 200 observations with the cryoPAF is required to cover a 400 square degree region (|gl|<10 deg, |gb|<10 deg). The survey is expected to be carried out over four semesters, from April 2026 to October 2027.

records.description: We propose to use a single CryoPAF beam for high precision pulsar timing experiments to determine whether pulsar timing projects, such as P456, should continue with the UWL or transition to the CryoPAF, which has a lower system temperature in the overlapping bands and no requirement for extra calibration observations. We will observe three of the best timed pulsars and compare the resulting observations with those from P456. These pulsars are J1909-3744, J1744-1134, and J1713+0747. In addition, we will also observe J0613-0200, J1017-7156, J1902-5105, J2129-5721, which show diminished signal-to-noise above 2 GHz, but are still important to the P456 observing programme. The results will be used to demonstrate pulsar timing techniques using the CryoPAF; demonstrate that the CryoPAF can be polarization and flux calibrated to a level required for high precision timing; provide high-precision timing data sets with the CryoPAF in order to ensure there are no timing offsets within the system; compare the UWL and CryoPAF results to determine which type of pulsars are best observed with the CryoPAF and which with the UWL.

records.title: Long-term project observations for project L125 semester 2026APRS_30
records.description: The atomic interstellar medium shows tiny-scale optical depth fluctuations on the scale of 0.1~10,000 AU, whose origin and nature are poorly understood. The existence of this Tiny-Scale Atomic Structure (TSAS) has significant implications, potentially calling into question our fundamental understanding of heating, cooling and dynamical processes in the interstellar medium. Yet observations remain sparse. This long-term project plans to search for temporal variations in HI absorption spectra seen against background pulsars to characterise TSAS in the Milky Way interstellar medium (ISM). These observations constitute the largest number of sightlines and densest temporal sampling ever performed in a single experiment, and will test predictions that TSAS is the tail end of a turbulent cascade, constrain its minimum size scale (down to resolutions of ~0.05 AU) and potentially provide the first direct measurements of pressures in "large" TSAS features of > 1000 AU. We make use of the phase-resolved spectral line mode that we have recently implemented on Parkes, which has cut data rates and processing times by factors of ~1000 compared to past studies. This is an expansion of our pilot P1321 to a long term study.

records.title: Parkes observations for project P1183 semester 2026APRS_14
records.description: After nearly four years of monitoring with both the Parkes and FAST telescopes, FRB 20220529 has been established as an extremely active repeater. It exhibits one of the longest known activity durations and shows evidence for a potential periodicity. Owing to the frequent observations carried out with Parkes and FAST, two abrupt rotation-measure (RM) flares have been detected in this source. These constitute the first RM flares ever observed in a fast radio burst (FRB), indicating that a dense, magnetised plasma clump passed across the line of sight. The second RM flare in particular makes a binary-origin scenario for FRB 20220529 especially compelling. If confirmed, the periodicity and RM flares would mutually reinforce one another, serving as a smoking gun for a binary origin. Previous analyses have shown that observations from both Parkes and FAST are essential. FAST's exceptional sensitivity enables the detection of many bursts, whereas the Parkes UWL receiver provides a stable burst-detection rate even during low-activity phases. To further investigate FRB 20220529, we have scheduled regular FAST observations every fortnight. We therefore propose to continue monitoring FRB 20220529 with the Parkes UWL receiver as well. The FAST and Parkes sessions are expected to be separated by a few days, ideally about one week. A cadence of approximately one week offers an excellent opportunity to capture detailed structure during the onset of RM decreases, as demonstrated by previous monitoring.

records.title: Parkes observations for project P1365 semester 2026APRS_21
records.description: Following the successful demonstration of a pilot first-pass (shallow) search of a small fraction of the sky, the second-pass processing has commenced for the SMART pulsar survey, which involves deep searches of 80-minute observations. Over the past year, this second-pass processing has led to the discovery of 16 new pulsars (including two millisecond pulsars), bringing the total number of SMART discoveries to 20 when combined with the first-pass results. These outcomes hint at the exciting promise of this first southern-sky pulsar survey in the frequency band of SKA-Low. All new pulsars require timing observations to determine their spin and astrometric parameters. Another important aspect of timing newly discovered pulsars is to identify specialised targets for further detailed follow-ups. Since the MWA no longer supports routine pulsar observations from 2025, timing follow-ups rely on other telescopes. The Parkes Murriyang telescope, with an identical sky coverage, sensitivity and the wide frequency coverage, offers the best option to time SMART discoveries. We have demonstrated Murriyang's suitability for this through previous semesters and are now extending the project to a sample of 11 pulsars, including six from the last semester. The data will also allow us to study pulse profiles, polarisation, and flux densities from ~100 MHz to 4 GHz. The analysis/results will be included in a publication in preparation that will detail the deep-search pipeline and report on initial pulsar discoveries.

records.title: Parkes observations for project P1054 semester 2026APRS_43
records.description: With this proposal we ask time to continue our timing follow-up campaign of pulsars discovered with the MeerKAT telescope. Fiftythree sources have been discovered in targeted observations of Fermi unidentified point sources, two towards Supernova Remnants, 27 in the Magellanic Clouds, 109 in Globular Clusters and 96 in a survey of the Galactic plane. A large fraction of the new discoveries are recycled pulsars (including a few relativistic systems, a pulsar with a planetary companion and several 'spider' binaries), or young pulsars. Timing observations have an essential role in exploiting the full potential of any pulsar discovery, allowing for the precise measurement of rotational, astrometric and orbital parameters which, in turn, give us powerful tools to improve our understanding of the physics in extreme environments as well as of the population of neutron stars as a whole. The UWL receiver of the Parkes telescope is a sensitive, versatile instrument that is allowing us to successfully time these new sources, in the bright-end of TRAPUM discoveries.

records.title: Long-term project observations for project L147 semester 2026APRS_26
records.description: We propose to carry out a deep Galactic Bulge pulsar survey (GBps), covering the core of the Bulge region using the new cryoPAF system on Murriyang, the Parkes radio telescope. Such a deep survey is expected to discover a population of millisecond pulsars in the Galactic Bulge and reveal their distribution and gamma-ray emissions. With these, we will lead pioneering studies on the origin of gamma-ray emission in the Galactic Bulge, a longstanding mystery in modern astronomy. The outcome of this project will significantly advance our knowledge of the formation and evolution of millisecond pulsars in the Galactic Bulge, the origin and properties of high-energy emissions, and the nature of dark matter annihilation in the Galactic Centre. A total of 200 observations with the cryoPAF is required to cover a 400 square degree region (|gl|<10 deg, |gb|<10 deg). The survey is expected to be carried out over four semesters, from April 2026 to October 2027.

records.title: Parkes observations for project P1402 semester 2026APRS_30
records.description: We propose a dedicated Parkes/Murriyang timing campaign of the newly confirmed narrow-duty cycle (~6 %) millisecond pulsar (MSP) PSR J2147-3604. This source was identified in a reprocessing of the Green Bank North Celestial Cap (GBNCC) survey as a high-confidence candidate with a spin period of 3.2 ms, and a dispersion measure, DM of 17 pc/cc. The pulsar was subsequently confirmed by the Fermi--TRAPUM collaboration via MeerKAT beamforming localisation and Parkes follow-up. Parkes/UWL observations allocated using green time detected this pulsar between 700--1500~MHz, and confirmed that it's in a binary system. Due to its low DM, we also detected strong interstellar scintillation. We request 35~hr of Murriyang time using the UWL receiver and APOLLO backend to obtain a phase-coherent timing solution and to characterise its spin, orbital, and propagation properties. Since the pulsar is also associated with a FERMI source, a precise radio ephemeris will also enable sensitive searches for gamma-ray pulsations in Fermi-LAT data and assess PSR J2147-3604's suitability for pulsar timing arrays (PTAs) and future gamma-ray timing applications.

records.title: Parkes observations for project P1411 semester 2026APRS_44
records.description: Conventional blind pulsar surveys that search for periodic signals in high-time-resolution data are increasingly limited by interstellar scattering at high dispersion measure (DM), orbital modulation in compact binaries, scintillation effects, and intensive computational demands. The Australian Square Kilometre Array Pathfinder (ASKAP) Evolutionary Map of the Universe (EMU) survey provides ultra-deep radio continuum maps enabling complementary image-domain pulsar searches that bypass these limitations. We have discovered seven new pulsars through three targeted strategies: (1) identifying compact sources embedded in supernova remnants (SNRs) and pulsar wind nebulae (PWNe), (2) detecting highly variable sources via variance imaging, and (3) selecting highly circularly polarised compact sources. Our sample includes three highly scattered pulsars (PSR J1638-4713 , PSR J1643-4511, and PSR J1631-4722 with DM > 800 pc/cm^3) including two pulsars associated with PWNe. Two millisecond pulsars (PSR J0927-7641 and PSR J1838-5949) are in potential wide binary systems with orbital periods of several tens of days, and two additional normal pulsars (PSR J1153-7106 and PSR 2223-0654). We propose follow-up timing observations of these pulsars with Murriyang's Ultra-Wideband Low (UWL) receiver to obtain phase-connected timing solutions, measure precise positions and spin parameters, and determine orbital characteristics for the binary systems,. These observations will enable studies of pulsar formation mechanisms, binary evolution pathways, PWN-SNR interactions, and validate image-based discovery techniques as powerful complements to traditional blind surveys for detecting elusive pulsars.

records.title: Parkes observations for project P1032 semester 2026APRS_18
records.description: With this proposal, we aim to continue P1032, the rapid measurements of relativistic parameters of southern binary pulsar systems using data from the Parkes Ultra Wideband Low (UWL) receiver. As the MeerTime project at the MeerKAT radio telescope ended in early 2024, observations with the UWL receiver now form the backbone for extending the timing baselines of many pulsars that have been part of this project. Since the source selection in the previous semesters was tailored such that the UWL receiver is the most (versatile and) suited instrument to achieve the proposed scientific goals for the chosen pulsars, we propose to continue these observations. We will use the UWL data to obtain significant orbital coverage and timing baselines on these pulsars and obtain important constraints on orbital and temporal DM variations that will help in identifying the nature of the companion stars. Increasing the number of measured Neutron Star (NS) masses, as well as improving on current constraints has profound implications for NS internal structure and for stellar and binary evolution physics.

records.title: Long-term project observations for project L124 semester 2026APRS_14
records.description: We propose a long-term project to monitor a very active repeater, FRB 20190520B, with Murriyang's UWL system. Our previous observations show that FRB 20190520B is not only among the most active FRBs that can be observed with Murriyang, but also shows extreme rotation measure (RM) and dispersion measure (DM) evolution, along with distinctive behavior at 3GHz frequency. This makes the UWL receiver uniquely suited for detailed studies and long-term monitoring of this repeating FRB. Through this program, we anticipate detecting a large sample of bursts from this FRB. In collaboration with FAST, we aim to investigate the time evolution of various properties of FRB 20190520B, enhance our understanding of polarisation across an extremely wide bandwidth with high sensitivity, and gain deeper insights into the local environment and emission mechanisms of FRBs.

records.title: Long-term project observations for project L126 semester 2026APRS_24
records.description: We propose a modest program to continue monitoring 4 of the 6 known radio magnetars in order to achieve three primary science goals. The first is to characterise magnetar outbursts over long timescales, for which tracking their rotational, flux density, and polarisation properties provide a clear view of the impulse response of their magnetic fields. Second, understanding the links between magnetars the mysterious fast radio burst phenomenon through the discovery of rare emission and propagation effects, shared spectro-temporal phenomenology, and connections to high-energy (X-ray/gamma-ray) phenomena. Lastly, our continued monitoring has enormous benefit to the wider magnetar community, providing rapid alerts to changes in activity, adding context to unusual behaviour detected by high-energy observations, and a host of supplementary science through the teams extensive collaborative networks. The project and its precursors have been running since 2007 and have contributed to 22 publications since then. This is the first submission since the project was converted to long-term status.

records.title: Environmental DNA (eDNA) data from the RV Investigator Indian Ocean Territories surveys (IN2021_V04 and IN2022_V08)
records.description: This eDNA sequence data was collected aboard Australia’s Marine National Facility (MNF) vessel, the RV Investigator, during two research voyages, IN2021_V04 (July 2021) and IN2022_V08 (October 2022) traversing Australia’s Indian Ocean Territories. The data deposited here includes quality filtered sequenced data (16S rRNA [16S fish] and COI [COI Leray universal metazoan]) with an associated count table, sample/environmental metadata and fastq files. In addition, we have provided raw non-quality filtered sequence data in a demultiplexed (sample assigned) and primer trimmed format, ready for quality filtering and further processing. Quality filtered sequenced data: 1) Taxonomic assigned sequence data used for statistical analysis e.g. "dnaSeqData_IOT-eDNA_16SFish_Library_2021.xlsx" - the taxonomic assigned 16SFish amplicon data from voyage IN2021_V04. Associated environmental/sample metadata is in "metadata_IOT-eDNA.xlsx" 2) DADA2 output prior to blasting against NCBI Genbank and taxonomic assignment. This folder contains DADA2 quality filtered count tables and sequence fasta files (for blasting) for each assay/voyage. Raw data: 3) Unfiltered sequence data in fastq format, demultiplexed into individual samples (also split by assay/voyage). Demultiplexed sequence data has also been primer trimmed (5', but also screening 3' for sequencer run-through), so sequences are ready for quality filtering and further processing. The associated scientific publication in preparation is "Environmental DNA reveals new deep-sea fish records and spatial structuring across the Christmas Island Seamount Province", by Katrina West, Tim O’Hara, John Pogonoski, Sahan Jayasinghe, Stephanie Joyce, Tiffany Sih, Yi-Kai Tea, Sharon A. Appleyard & Bruce Deagle

records.title: Parkes observations for project P1420 semester 2026APRS_17
records.description: We propose the pilot of a Murriyang CryoPAF Pulsar Survey of the Southern Galactic Plane (CPS-LowLat Pilot). The revolutionary CryoPAF receiver delivers the highest pulsar survey speed in the Southern Hemisphere, exceeding L-band capability of MeerKAT by ~2x, with a sufficiently low data rate to enable archiving and reprocessing essential to maximizing survey yields. Population synthesis predicts ~300 new pulsars in the full CPS-LowLat. Up to ~90 pulsars are predicted from this Pilot in a rich region of the Galactic Plane (-15deg < l < -10deg, |b| < 3deg), including 5-10 millisecond pulsars. 2.5-hr pointings are proposed to provide the requisite transformational pulsar detection rate, while maintaining sensitivity across a wide range of binary orbital periods, including ultra-compact systems. A frequency range of 1.3-1.85 GHz will mitigate dispersion smearing and scattering. Well-developed GPU-based searches for accelerated / binary systems and efficient coherent folding algorithms will be deployed. New discoveries from CPS-LowLat will enable strong-field tests of general relativity, equation-of-state constraints from massive neutron stars, more accurate modeling of the neutron star merger rate, and probes of exotic stellar-evolution pathways and of the ionised interstellar medium. Besides its impressive pulsar yield and the associated scientific possibilities, the proposed pilot will demonstrate the end-to-end performance of the CryoPAF for pulsar surveys prior to commencing the full CPS-LowLat, and validate pulsar population models.

records.title: Parkes observations for project P1406 semester 2026APRS_10
records.description: NGC 362 is a post-core-collapse southern globular cluster (GC) where 12 pulsars have recently been discovered. The pulsar population is very diverse, containing extremely fast-spinning, mildly recycled and slow pulsars, the vast majority of which (11 out of 12) are part of binary systems with very different orbital periods and eccentricities. However, a full orbital characterization was possible only for three of these binaries. This is because the pulsars in NGC 362 are heavily affected by scintillation, and therefore are very elusive. Here, we propose to carry out a series of deep observations of NGC 362, taking advantage of the ultra-wide bandwidth of the UWL receiver, with the aim of determining the orbital parameters of the 8 binary pulsars that still lack characterization. This is of utmost importance, as it is the prerequisite for the derivation of their timing solutions. The latter would in turn allow a wealth of potential studies, such as probing the presence of a mass excess at the center of NGC 362, looking for optical and X-ray counterparts, studying the magnetic field at arcsecond scales, and more. These kinds of studies are only possible in clusters that host many pulsars. With its 12 pulsars, NGC 362 harbors a huge scientific potential, which we aim to unlock by characterizing its binaries. Moreover, we may discover additional pulsars thanks to fortuitous scintillation events.

records.title: Long-term project observations for project L100 semester 2026APRS_16
records.description: We request time to observe 270 pulsars on a regular basis in order to achieve three main science goals. The first is to understand pulsars: how do they spin down and what disrupts this process, how and why their profiles vary with time, whether they precess or have planetary mass companions, in short all the things that make pulsar timing noisier than the perfect clock. Secondly we want to understand the interstellar medium of our Galaxy through repeated monitoring of dispersion measure, rotation measure and flux density variations in conjunction with scintillation parameters. Finally, we provide these data as a community service both to the high-energy community where we have strong collaborative links (particularly to Fermi) and to the radio pulsar astronomers generally through the CSIRO archive. The project is on-going since 2007, we are (co-)authors on 107 papers arising from the P574 data. The data have contributed to the PhD theses of students from Bordeaux, Manchester, Oxford, Stanford, and Swinburne. We are seeking long-term project status with a view to continuing the project into the SKA era.

records.title: Legume Companion Cropping, Intercropping and Nitrogen Legacy Effects Field Trial Data, Perillup, Western Australia, 2024-2026
records.description: This collection contains observational data and metadata from a three-year field experiment conducted at Perillup, Western Australia, from 2024 to 2026. The experiment was established to evaluate legume-based nitrogen management strategies and mixed cropping systems as alternatives to synthetic nitrogen fertiliser in low-medium rainfall grain production systems. The experiment investigated the productivity, nitrogen contribution and nitrogen legacy effects of companion cropping, intercropping, grain legume and brown manure systems involving wheat, lupin, vetch and serradella. Treatments included monoculture wheat with contrasting nitrogen fertiliser rates, monoculture grain and brown manure legumes, wheat-legume companion crops with differing cereal-to-legume sowing ratios, and wheat-legume intercrops. Legume species included Coyote lupin, Morava common vetch and Margurita French serradella. The subsequent years assessed residual impacts on soil fertility and the performance of follow-on crops under contrasting nitrogen fertiliser regimes. The crop sequence comprised Scepter wheat in the establishment year (2024), Titan AX barley in the first legacy year (2025) and PY428R canola in the second legacy year (2026). Key research questions relating to: How do companion cropping and intercropping systems compare with legume grain and brown manure systems for nitrogen contribution and crop productivity? How do different legume species influence biomass production, biological nitrogen fixation and nitrogen cycling? What are the residual nitrogen benefits of legume-based systems to subsequent cereal and oilseed crops? How do cereal-to-legume sowing ratios affect crop competition, productivity and nitrogen dynamics? What are the trade-offs between grain harvest, brown manure systems, biomass production and nitrogen retention? The dataset includes plot-level, crop-component and subsample observations collected throughout the experiment. Measurements include crop establishment, plant height, biomass production, nodulation status, soil mineral nitrogen, crop yield and other agronomic variables collected at key growth stages. Associated metadata describe trial design, treatment structure, crop species, nitrogen fertiliser treatments, management practices, sampling stages and experimental layout. The current release does not include several datasets that are being processed and are intended for future publication. These may include drone-derived vegetation indices (such as NDVI, NDRE and fractional vegetation cover), plant nitrogen concentration and stable isotope (15N) measurements, estimated soil nitrogen stocks (kg N ha⁻¹), and other derived datasets associated with nitrogen fixation and nutrient cycling studies. The Perillup experiment forms part of a broader research program evaluating legume-based nitrogen management strategies across diverse production environments in Western Australia. Located within the medium-rainfall zone of the Western Australian Wheatbelt, Perillup provides a contrast to the lower-rainfall environments represented by the Goomalling and Avondale trial sites. Related experiments were conducted at Avondale (Avondale Trial 1, Avondale Trial 2 and Avondale Trial 3) and Goomalling (Goomalling Trial 1 and Goomalling Trial 2), each with distinct treatment structures, species combinations and research objectives. Users interested in cross-site analyses should consult the associated datasets and metadata for each trial to understand differences in experimental design, management practices and environmental conditions.

records.title: Parkes observations for project P1410 semester 2026APRS_15
records.description: Neutron stars are compact remnants formed in core-collapse supernovae of massive stars. A subset of these objects, known as pulsars, emit highly regular pulses of radiation that make them powerful tools for studying fundamental physics, stellar evolution, and the structure of our Galaxy. Despite decades of surveys, the known pulsar population remains incomplete: while about 4,800 pulsars are currently catalogued, population studies predict that roughly 10,000 or more radio-detectable pulsars should be observable with our current instrumentation. A significant fraction of the missing population is expected to consist of slowly rotating pulsars, which are difficult to detect with standard search pipelines. These pulsars often have very narrow pulse duty cycles and long spin periods, making them susceptible to reduced signal-to-noise ratios and contamination by low-frequency ("red") noise in Fourier-based searches. As a result, many such objects may remain hidden in archival survey data. Motivated by this, we reprocessed archival data from the Parkes Multibeam Pulsar Survey targeting narrow-duty-cycle signals and allowing to investigate lower signal to noise ratios for these candidates. This approach led to the identification of 12 highly credible new slow pulsar candidates that were missed in previous analyses. Several of these candidates show strong folded signal-to-noise ratios and physically plausible dispersion measures, indicating they are likely genuine pulsars. The primary goal of this proposal is to obtain targeted follow-up observations to confirm and time these newly identified pulsar candidates. Confirming them will help close the gap between predicted and observed pulsar populations and demonstrate the continued scientific value of archival radio survey data.

We will observe three of the best timed pulsars and compare the resulting observations with those from P456. These pulsars are J1909-3744, J1744-1134, and J1713+0747. In addition, we will also observe J0613-0200, J1017-7156, J1902-5105, J2129-5721, which show diminished signal-to-noise above 2 GHz, but are still important to the P456 observing programme. The results will be used to demonstrate pulsar timing techniques using the CryoPAF; demonstrate that the CryoPAF can be polarization and flux calibrated to a level required for high precision timing; provide high-precision timing data sets with the CryoPAF in order to ensure there are no timing offsets within the system; compare the UWL and CryoPAF results to determine which type of pulsars are best observed with the CryoPAF and which with the UWL.

records.title: Parkes observations for project P595 semester 2026OCTS_01
records.description: We propose to continue the PULSE@Parkes project in which high school students from Australia and around the World use the Parkes radio telescope in a remote observing model to observe and analyse pulsar data. The data from some PULSE@Parkes observations are used to support the space missions, other observations supplement the P456 Pulsar Timing Array project and the remainder were chosen in order to make a detailed analysis of pulsar timing irregularities and intermittency.

records.title: Leaf Dark Respiration and Associated Hyperspectral Reflectance Measurements from Multi-environment Wheat Field Experiments
records.description: This collection contains measurements of leaf dark respiration collected from wheat (Triticum aestivum L.) field experiments conducted across multiple Australian environments during the 2023 and 2025 growing seasons. The dataset combines field-based respiration measurements, laboratory-derived oxygen consumption assays, and linked leaf hyperspectral reflectance observations collected across multiple crop developmental stages. Leaf dark respiration was quantified using oxygen depletion assays on leaf tissue samples and expressed on both a leaf area basis and a dry matter basis. The collection includes measurements from field experiments conducted at Kabinga (NSW), Northam (WA), and Boorowa Agricultural Research Station (BARS, NSW), enabling the investigation of variation in respiratory activity across environments and growth stages. In addition to derived respiration traits, the dataset includes dissolved oxygen measurements collected through time during respiration assays. These measurements provide the underlying data used to estimate respiration rates from oxygen depletion. Associated metadata include site, year, sampling date, growth stage, assay plate and well identifiers, experimental run information, and plant identifiers. A linked dataset combines leaf dark respiration measurements with leaf hyperspectral reflectance observations, facilitating the development of spectral models for the prediction of respiratory traits and the investigation of relationships between plant physiological processes and leaf optical properties. The collection supports research in crop physiology, plant respiration, plant metabolism, spectroscopy, crop phenotyping, physiological trait prediction, and wheat breeding.

records.title: Leaf Gas Exchange, Hyperspectral Reflectance and Derived Photosynthetic Traits from Wheat Field Experiments
records.description: This collection contains leaf hyperspectral reflectance measurements, leaf gas exchange observations and derived photosynthetic trait estimates collected from wheat (Triticum aestivum L.) field experiments conducted in Australia between 2023 and 2025. Data were collected at Kabinga (NSW), Northam (WA) and Boorowa Agricultural Research Station (BARS, NSW) during booting, anthesis and post-anthesis growth stages. The collection is organised by year, site, growth stage and sampling date. Leaf gas exchange measurements were collected using LI-COR 6400 and LI-COR 6400XT portable photosynthesis systems. Raw instrument outputs are included within the collection together with associated files used for downstream processing and analysis. Measurements include photosynthetic assimilation, stomatal conductance, transpiration, intercellular CO2 concentration and associated chamber environmental conditions. Leaf hyperspectral reflectance measurements were collected using ASD FieldSpec spectroradiometers and NaturaSpec systems. Spectral observations characterise leaf optical properties across visible, red-edge and near-infrared wavelength regions. The collection also contains processed photosynthetic trait outputs derived from gas exchange response curve analyses. Depending on the experiment, derived variables include maximum Rubisco carboxylation capacity (Vcmax), electron transport capacity (J), photosynthetic assimilation at reference conditions (A400) and additional model-derived physiological traits. The collection contains raw instrument files, processed datasets, photosynthetic trait outputs and supporting metadata required to relate measurements across sites, years, growth stages and sampling campaigns. The data may be used for crop physiology, photosynthesis research, spectroscopy, physiological trait prediction, crop phenotyping and wheat breeding applications.

records.title: Molecular insights into diet and gut microbiome composition of myctophid fish in the Tasman Sea
records.description: This study provides a DNA-based characterisation of myctophid diets and stomach-associated bacterial communities in the Tasman Sea. We combined 18S rRNA metabarcoding of stomach contents with 16S rRNA metabarcoding of stomach-associated bacterial communities to examine trophic and microbial variation in D. hudsoni and M. ventralis from the Tasman Sea.

records.title: Low Moisture Extrusion Dataset for Six Plant Protein Isolates and Binary Blends in Textured Vegetable Protein (TVP) Production
records.description: This collection contains experimental data generated from a comparative study of six commercially relevant plant protein ingredients (soy, pea, chickpea, faba bean, lentil, and mung bean) processed via low moisture extrusion for dry textured vegetable protein (TVP) production. The dataset includes ingredient characterisation (RVA pasting behaviour, colour, water absorption capacity), extrusion process conditions (feed rate, screw speed, water flowrate, in-barrel moisture content, motor torque and specific mechanical energy), and extrudate properties (bulk and apparent density, expansion ratio, porosity, water holding capacity, colour, and texture (per-piece texture profile analysis recomputed from the raw force–deformation curves)). Binary 50:50 protein blends were also evaluated across multiple moisture levels to examine formulation–process interactions. The data were produced to support systematic comparison of protein-specific extrusion behaviour and to inform formulation-specific process optimisation strategies in plant-based meat analogue development. The dataset enables reuse for comparative analysis, modelling, meta-analysis, and process optimisation studies in food extrusion research.

records.title: Whole-genome sequencing of wild-caught barramundi (Lates calcarifer) from the Northern Territory, Australia
records.description: This dataset contains whole-genome sequence data from 10 wild-caught barramundi (Lates calcarifer, also known as Asian sea bass) sampled from 4 locations across the Northern Territory, Australia, between 2018 and 2022. Sampling sites include Bynoe Harbour, Middle Arm, Daly River & Mary River. Genomic DNA was extracted from fin clips and sequenced on Illumina NovaSeq X 10B as 150 bp paired-end reads to an average depth of approximately 27X. Sample metadata, including sampling location, sequencing details and coverage, are provided in the accompanying file barramundi_NT_WGS_sample_metadata.csv.

records.title: Parkes observations for project P1420 semester 2026APRS_18
records.description: We propose the pilot of a Murriyang CryoPAF Pulsar Survey of the Southern Galactic Plane (CPS-LowLat Pilot). The revolutionary CryoPAF receiver delivers the highest pulsar survey speed in the Southern Hemisphere, exceeding L-band capability of MeerKAT by ~2x, with a sufficiently low data rate to enable archiving and reprocessing essential to maximizing survey yields. Population synthesis predicts ~300 new pulsars in the full CPS-LowLat. Up to ~90 pulsars are predicted from this Pilot in a rich region of the Galactic Plane (-15deg < l < -10deg, |b| < 3deg), including 5-10 millisecond pulsars. 2.5-hr pointings are proposed to provide the requisite transformational pulsar detection rate, while maintaining sensitivity across a wide range of binary orbital periods, including ultra-compact systems. A frequency range of 1.3-1.85 GHz will mitigate dispersion smearing and scattering. Well-developed GPU-based searches for accelerated / binary systems and efficient coherent folding algorithms will be deployed. New discoveries from CPS-LowLat will enable strong-field tests of general relativity, equation-of-state constraints from massive neutron stars, more accurate modeling of the neutron star merger rate, and probes of exotic stellar-evolution pathways and of the ionised interstellar medium. Besides its impressive pulsar yield and the associated scientific possibilities, the proposed pilot will demonstrate the end-to-end performance of the CryoPAF for pulsar surveys prior to commencing the full CPS-LowLat, and validate pulsar population models.

records.title: Long-term project observations for project L100 semester 2026APRS_17
records.description: We request time to observe 270 pulsars on a regular basis in order to achieve three main science goals. The first is to understand pulsars: how do they spin down and what disrupts this process, how and why their profiles vary with time, whether they precess or have planetary mass companions, in short all the things that make pulsar timing noisier than the perfect clock. Secondly we want to understand the interstellar medium of our Galaxy through repeated monitoring of dispersion measure, rotation measure and flux density variations in conjunction with scintillation parameters. Finally, we provide these data as a community service both to the high-energy community where we have strong collaborative links (particularly to Fermi) and to the radio pulsar astronomers generally through the CSIRO archive. The project is on-going since 2007, we are (co-)authors on 107 papers arising from the P574 data. The data have contributed to the PhD theses of students from Bordeaux, Manchester, Oxford, Stanford, and Swinburne. We are seeking long-term project status with a view to continuing the project into the SKA era.

records.title: Long-term project observations for project L147 semester 2026APRS_28
records.description: We propose to carry out a deep Galactic Bulge pulsar survey (GBps), covering the core of the Bulge region using the new cryoPAF system on Murriyang, the Parkes radio telescope. Such a deep survey is expected to discover a population of millisecond pulsars in the Galactic Bulge and reveal their distribution and gamma-ray emissions. With these, we will lead pioneering studies on the origin of gamma-ray emission in the Galactic Bulge, a longstanding mystery in modern astronomy. The outcome of this project will significantly advance our knowledge of the formation and evolution of millisecond pulsars in the Galactic Bulge, the origin and properties of high-energy emissions, and the nature of dark matter annihilation in the Galactic Centre. A total of 200 observations with the cryoPAF is required to cover a 400 square degree region (|gl|<10 deg, |gb|<10 deg). The survey is expected to be carried out over four semesters, from April 2026 to October 2027.

records.title: Intermediate files for "Methylation changes in Barrett's metaplasia, dysplasia, and cancer"
records.description: The incidence rates of esophageal adenocarcinoma (EAC), one of cancers with the highest case-fatality ratios, has increased by sevenfold over the last half century. Clinical management of EAC, dependent on the accurate diagnosis of metaplasia or dysplasia in Barrett’s esophagus (BE), is hampered by the unreliable histopathological diagnosis of dysplasia and potential sampling errors. Here, we obtained whole-genome methylation profiles from samples across the disease progression spectrum, notably supplementing the scant existing methylation evidence for low-grade (LGD) and high-grade dysplasia (HGD). This collection contains the larger intermediate files that could not be uploaded to GitHub, e.g., publicly available human gene annotations and SNPs, and per-position/per-CpG methylation in a tabular form. Downstream scripts that process these files are available at https://github.com/lyijin/eac_emseq.

records.title: Parkes observations for project P1413 semester 2026APRS_30
records.description: We request 75 hours of Parkes observing time for dedicated radio follow-up observations of PSR J1635-5134, a promising candidate pulsar-subdwarf B (sdB) star binary system. PSR J1635-5134 is a non-recycled 340 ms pulsar in a nearly circular 18-hour orbit with a minimum companion mass of 0.26 solar mass. It lies in a sparsely populated region of binary-pulsars parameter space and may represent a short-lived evolutionary stage immediately following inefficient spin-up, thereby providing a missing link between canonical binaries and the millisecond pulsar-WD population. The system exhibits peculiar, orbital-phase-dependent dispersion-measure (DM) variability, with DM variations exceeding 30 pc/cc, indicating substantial ionised material plausibly associated with an outflow from the companion. Moreover, during prior monitoring with Parkes, the DM variations shifted from being predominantly modest to being persistently large, implying an evolving plasma environment that cannot be characterised with sparse or irregular observations. Determining whether these high-DM variations are intermittent or long-lived, and mapping how the excess material varies with orbital phase and epoch, are essential for constraining the origin and geometry of the plasma and for testing the hypothesis that an sdB wind supplies the required electron column. Through this proposal, we aim to (i) extend the timing baseline to improve astrometric precision to sub-arcsecond accuracy, enabling secure identification of the optical counterpart in a crowded field, and (ii) perform phase-targeted observations during eclipse/DM variation phases to understand the temporal behavior of excess DM.

records.title: Parkes observations for project P1449 semester 2026OCTS_01
records.description: We propose the pilot survey of the southern high-Galactic-latitude sky with the Murriyang telescope using its state-of-the-art CryoPAF receiver. Owing to their large Galactic scale heights, millisecond pulsars (MSPs) are preferentially found at intermediate and high Galactic latitudes, where lower sky temperatures, reduced interstellar scattering, and smaller dispersion measures favor the discovery of nearby, bright, and exceptionally stable systems. Despite containing a large fraction of the known MSP population and nearly half of the pulsar timing array (PTA) pulsars visible from Murriyang, the southern high-latitude sky has never been surveyed with sensitivity comparable to that achieved in the Galactic-plane. Population synthesis simulations predict that a full CryoPAF survey of the southern high-latitude sky would discover approximately 320 normal pulsars and 100 MSPs, including many binary systems. As a first step towards this objective, we propose a pilot survey of 600 degree square (278deg<l<321deg, 15deg<b<30deg). CryoPAF capabilities of covering a large filed of view, broad bandwidth, and low system temperature, provides a survey speed ~20 times greater than that the legacy multibeam receiver. Using 27-minute integrations, the proposed observations will be substantially more sensitive than previous large-area high-latitude surveys. The proposed pilot survey is expected to discover ~10 pulsars while establishing the optimal observing strategy for a future large-scale survey. It will also provide an assessment of receiver performance, sensitivity, radio-frequency interference conditions, data quality, and candidate yields under realistic observing conditions. The survey offers the opportunity to discover PTA-quality MSPs, compact binary systems, and potentially some of the fastest-spinning neutron stars known.

records.title: Long-term project observations for project P1032 semester 2026OCTS_01
records.description: With this proposal, we aim to continue P1032; measuring timing parameters of relativistic parameters of southern binary pulsar systems, by using data from the Parkes Ultra Wideband Low (UWL) receiver. With this Long Term Project, focus on rapid measurements of relativistic parameters, as well as parameters informing their orbital configuration, in order to enable tests of the theory of GR and constrain binary evolution scenarios, mainly via Neutron Star (NS) mass measurements. As the MeerTime project at the MeerKAT radio telescope ended in early 2024, observations with the UWL receiver now form the backbone for extending the timing baselines of many pulsars that have been part of this project. Since the source selection in the previous semesters was tailored such that the UWL receiver is the most (versatile and) suited instrument to achieve the proposed scientific goals for the chosen pulsars, we propose to continue these observations. We will use the UWL data to obtain significant orbital coverage and timing baselines on these pulsars and obtain important constraints on orbital and temporal DM variations that will help in identifying the nature of the companion stars. In addition to our main science goals, increasing the number of measured NS masses, as well as improving on current constraints has profound implications for understanding the NS internal structure.

records.title: Parkes observations for project P1437 semester 2026OCTS_01
records.description: This project is focussed on four pulsars in the globular cluster NGC6441. PSRJ1750-3703A is a 111 millisecond pulsar in a very eccentric and long period orbit around a companion star, with a total mass of 2.18Msun. The analysis of the available data gives indication that PSRJ1750-3703A can be the lightest neutron star known so far, but a firm upper limit that confirms this statement cannot be placed yet, because all previous observations do not uniformly cover all orbital phases: in fact, they are clustered around the the apoastron. PSRJ1750-3703B is another eccentric binary pulsar, for which the detection of the periastron advance allowed a first estimation of the total mass of the binary, but non precisely enough to determine the nature of the companion. PSRJ1750-3703C and PSRJ1750-3703E are two isolated pulsars with spin periods of 26.6 and 251 milliseconds, respectively. PSRJ1750-3703C, PSRJ1750-3703E, and also PSRJ1750-3703A, are in the top 10% of the slowest pulsars in globular clusters, thus raising the question on how these pulsars can be formed in some globular clusters. The proposed observations aim to observe PSRJ1750-3703A uniformly along its orbital motion, thus allowing us to measure the pulsar mass, by measuring either the Einstein delay gamma parameter, or the orbital inclination by addressing the covariance between gamma and the time derivative of the projected semi-mayor axis of the pulsar. The proposed observations will also allow to reduce by a factor of two the uncertainty on the total mass of PSRJ1750-3703B, and to improve the rotational and astrometric parameters for PSRJ1750-3703C and PSRJ1750-3703E.

records.title: Parkes observations for project P1420 semester 2026OCTS_01
records.description: We propose a transition from a Pilot to the full Murriyang CryoPAF Pulsar Survey of the Southern Galactic Plane (CPS-LowLat). The revolutionary CryoPAF receiver delivers the highest pulsar survey speed in the Southern Hemisphere, exceeding L-band capability of MeerKAT by ~2x, with a sufficiently low data rate to enable archiving and reprocessing essential to maximizing survey yields. Population synthesis predicts ~300 new pulsars in the full CPS-LowLat. New discoveries from CPS-LowLat will enable strong-field tests of General Relativity, equation-of-state constraints from massive neutron stars, more accurate modeling of the neutron star merger rate, and probes of exotic stellar-evolution pathways and of the ionised interstellar medium. Five pointings for the CPS-LowLat have been observed in 2026APRS since April 29, and preliminary, quick-look processing of the first three pointings has already yielded three excellent candidate pulsar discoveries. Re-detections of known pulsars suggests that we are achieving the expected end-to-end survey sensitivity. We propose to use 2026OCTS to transition our primary processing to CSIRO HPC resources, while continuing the survey, in preparation for commencement of the full CPS-LowLat in 2027APRS with a higher observation cadence. Up to ~50 pulsars are predicted from the 30 deg^2 2026OCTS survey region, including 3-6 millisecond pulsars, representing in itself an impressive yield and associated scientific promise. 2.5-hr pointings are proposed to provide the requisite transformational pulsar detection rate, while maintaining sensitivity across a wide range of binary orbital periods, including ultra-compact systems. A frequency range of 1.3-1.85 GHz will mitigate dispersion smearing and scattering.

records.title: Long-term project observations for project P456 semester 2026OCTS_01
records.description: The Parkes Pulsar Timing Array (PPTA) project has three primary goals: (a) detection of gravitational waves from astronomical sources, (b) establishment of a pulsar timescale, and (c) improvement of our understanding of Solar-system dynamics. We are now in an exciting regime where a signal detected in our (and other data sets) has the form expected for a gravitational wave background. We, along with the international community, are now working hard to either confirm or deny this result, and to determine the astrophysical origin of this signal. With this proposal, we aim to maintain our pre-eminent position in the field. This is a continuing proposal for which observations of millisecond pulsars (MSPs) will continue to improve bounds on ultra-low-frequency gravitational waves until they are detected with confidence. Continued Parkes observations will remain valuable at least until the first stage of the SKA is able to improve on our sensitivity and observing cadence. Even after the gravitational wave background is detected, continued observations will resolve the background origin and individual sources will be identified; advancing the nascent field of gravitational wave astronomy.

records.title: Parkes observations for project P1365 semester 2026OCTS_01
records.description: Following the successful demonstration of a pilot first-pass (shallow) search of a small fraction of the sky, the second-pass processing has commenced for the SMART pulsar survey, which involves deep searches of 80-minute observations. Over the past year, this second-pass processing has led to the discovery of 21 new pulsars (including two millisecond pulsars), bringing the total number of SMART discoveries to 25 when combined with the first-pass results. These outcomes hint at the exciting promise of this first southern-sky pulsar survey in the frequency band of SKA-Low. All new pulsars require timing observations to determine their spin and astrometric parameters. Another important aspect of timing newly discovered pulsars is to identify specialised targets for further detailed follow-ups. Since the MWA is currently not available for routine pulsar observations, timing follow-ups rely on other telescopes. The Parkes Murriyang telescope, with identical sky coverage, high sensitivity, and wide frequency coverage, offers the best option for timing SMART discoveries. We have refined the proposed targets from our previous proposal by removing six pulsars that will have accumulated a full year of Parkes timing data by the end of the current semester, and by adding six newly discovered sources, five from typical pulsar searching methods, and one from image-based transient searching techniques, thereby maintaining a total sample of 11 pulsars. The data will also allow us to study pulse profiles, polarisation, and flux densities from ~100 MHz to 4 GHz. The analysis/results will be included in a forthcoming publication.

records.title: Parkes observations for project P1428 semester 2026OCTS_01
records.description: Globular Clusters (GCs) are renowned to be the host of a wealth of radio pulsars, most of which are millisecond pulsars. The extreme stellar densities characterizing the central regions of GCs promote the formation of binary systems where neutron stars can be recycled, and the formation of pulsars and binaries with extreme or unconventional properties. GCs have therefore been prime targets for pulsar searching and, as of today, more than 360 pulsars have been found in 46 different clusters. The much larger computing power and much more modern algorithms available today have recently fostered the re-processing of archival Parkes GC data. This has led to the discovery of a few new pulsars, and several promising candidates. Here, we request 22 hours of observing time to re-observe a set of 10 GCs where 56 promising candidate pulsars have recently been found via reprocessing of archival Parkes data. The recently installed Ultra-Wide-band Low receiver, in combination with the modern APOLLO backend, will provide a sharp increase in sensitivity compared to the archival data. This will allow us to confirm or refute the candidates, and potentially even discover additional pulsars. Confirming at least one pulsar in a GC has a great scientific value, since it would allow us to know the approximate dispersion measure associated with cluster, greatly easing the search for additional pulsars in the cluster, and it would increase the total number of clusters known to host radio pulsars, contributing to our understanding of the population of pulsars in GCs.

records.title: Long-term project observations for project P455 semester 2026OCTS_01
records.description: This project is to continue timing and profile studies of the first double-pulsar system, a unique laboratory for gravitational physics. Important results published in our Phys. Rev. X paper (2021) include the first measurements of higher-order light-propagation effects and of the relativistic deformation of the orbit and highlight the importance of a long term observational campaign, including VLBI observations, for this remarkable system. The main aims of this proposal are to provide the strongest tests to date for general relativity and to measure for the first time the moment-of-inertia of a neutron star. Additionally, we will determine the system geometry, map the pulsar beams via geodetic precession, and search for the reappearance of Pulsar B. We exploit the high sensitivity and broad bandwidth of the UWL receiver. We are collaborating with the MeerKAT Double Pulsar Timing team to optimise combination of MeerKAT and UWL data.

records.title: Parkes observations for project P1054 semester 2026OCTS_01
records.description: With this proposal we ask time to continue our timing follow-up campaign of pulsars discovered with the MeerKAT telescope. Fiftytwo sources have been discovered in targeted observations of Fermi unidentified point sources, 2 towards Supernova Remnants, 27 in the Magellanic Clouds, 128 in Globular Clusters and 96 in a survey of the Galactic plane. A large fraction of the new discoveries are recycled pulsars (including a few relativistic systems, a pulsar with a planetary companion and several 'spider' binaries), or young pulsars. Timing observations have an essential role in exploiting the full potential of any pulsar discovery, allowing for the precise measurement of rotational, astrometric and orbital parameters which, in turn, give us powerful tools to improve our understanding of the physics in extreme environments as well as of the population of neutron stars as a whole. The UWL receiver of the Parkes telescope is a sensitive, versatile instrument that is allowing us to successfully time these new sources, in the bright-end of TRAPUM discoveries.

records.title: Parkes observations for project P1390 semester 2026OCTS_01
records.description: We propose 24 hours of Parkes UWL observations to continue timing and wideband monitoring of two nearby Extremely Variable Radio Bursters (EVRBs): J1606-0854 and J2357+2454. EVRBs are a newly defined population of neutron stars whose single-pulse fluence ratios exceed 10^4, bridging the gap between ordinary pulsars and FRBs. J1606-0854 (DM ~ 4.95 pc cm^-3) and J2357+2454 (DM ~ 8.06 pc cm^-3) have the lowest DMs among known RRATs, placing both within 1 kpc. Our 2026APRS pilot observations with Parkes UWL have demonstrated its unique capabilities: (i) J1606-0854 is detected at ~1 burst per 3 hours, with the UWL revealing narrow-band emission that drifts in frequency across the band. This behaviour is inaccessible to FAST's 1.0--1.5 GHz receiver, which entirely misses bursts falling outside its narrow window; (ii) J2357+2454 is detected at tens of bursts per hour, with the UWL uncovering strong scintillation across its full frequency range. FAST's limited bandwidth and flux-calibration issues for very bright bursts make Parkes UWL the uniquely suited instrument for characterising the intermediate-energy pulse population and full-band emission properties of both sources. We request 4 hours per month for 6 months (3 hr on J1606-0854, 1 hr on J2357+2454; 24 hours total).

records.title: Parkes observations for project P1411 semester 2026OCTS_01
records.description: Conventional blind pulsar surveys that search for periodic signals in high-time-resolution data are increasingly limited by interstellar scattering at high dispersion measure (DM), orbital modulation in compact binaries, scintillation effects, and intensive computational demands. The Australian Square Kilometre Array Pathfinder (ASKAP) Evolutionary Map of the Universe (EMU) survey provides ultra-deep radio continuum maps enabling complementary image-domain pulsar searches that bypass these limitations. We have discovered seven new pulsars through three targeted strategies: (1) identifying compact sources embedded in supernova remnants (SNRs) and pulsar wind nebulae (PWNe), (2) detecting highly variable sources via variance imaging, and (3) selecting highly circularly polarised compact sources. Our sample includes three highly scattered pulsars (PSR J1638-4713 , PSR J1643-4511, and PSR J1631-4722 with DM > 800 pc/cm^3) including two pulsars associated with PWNe. Two millisecond pulsars (PSR J0927-7641 and PSR J1838-5949) are in potential wide binary systems with orbital periods of several tens of days, and two additional normal pulsars (PSR J1153-7106 and PSR 2223-0654). We propose follow-up timing observations of these pulsars with Murriyang's Ultra-Wideband Low (UWL) receiver to obtain phase-connected timing solutions, measure precise positions and spin parameters, and determine orbital characteristics for the binary systems,. These observations will enable studies of pulsar formation mechanisms, binary evolution pathways, PWN-SNR interactions, and validate image-based discovery techniques as powerful complements to traditional blind surveys for detecting elusive pulsars.

records.title: Long-term project observations for project P1101 semester 2026OCTS_01
records.description: We propose a long-term project to monitor a very active repeater, FRB 20190520B, with Murriyang's UWL system. Our previous observations show that FRB 20190520B is not only among the most active FRBs that can be observed with Murriyang, but also shows extreme rotation measure (RM) and dispersion measure (DM) evolution, along with distinctive behavior at 3GHz frequency. This makes the UWL receiver uniquely suited for detailed studies and long-term monitoring of this repeating FRB. Through this program, we anticipate detecting a large sample of bursts from this FRB. In collaboration with FAST, we aim to investigate the time evolution of various properties of FRB 20190520B, enhance our understanding of polarisation across an extremely wide bandwidth with high sensitivity, and gain deeper insights into the local environment and emission mechanisms of FRBs.

records.title: Parkes observations for project P1452 semester 2026OCTS_01
records.description: We propose a search for pulsars, with the expectation of finding primarily millisecond pulsars, in pulsar candidates found in MeerKAT and Very Large Array imaging surveys of the Galactic Bulge and Plane. The candidates were identified primarily as steep-spectrum, circularly- and/or linearly-polarized sources, and to a lesser degree by the level of radio variability observed. We have chosen 20 pulsar candidates to target in this proposal, eleven that may be Bulge members and nine others in the Plane. We request two half-hour pointings per source with the UWL receiver, plus 15 minutes of overhead (setup and slewing) per two sources, for a total of 22.5 hours of observing time.

New discoveries from CPS-LowLat will enable strong-field tests of General Relativity, equation-of-state constraints from massive neutron stars, more accurate modeling of the neutron star merger rate, and probes of exotic stellar-evolution pathways and of the ionised interstellar medium. Five pointings for the CPS-LowLat have been observed in 2026APRS since April 29, and preliminary, quick-look processing of the first three pointings has already yielded three excellent candidate pulsar discoveries. Re-detections of known pulsars suggests that we are achieving the expected end-to-end survey sensitivity. We propose to use 2026OCTS to transition our primary processing to CSIRO HPC resources, while continuing the survey, in preparation for commencement of the full CPS-LowLat in 2027APRS with a higher observation cadence. Up to ~50 pulsars are predicted from the 30 deg^2 2026OCTS survey region, including 3-6 millisecond pulsars, representing in itself an impressive yield and associated scientific promise. 2.5-hr pointings are proposed to provide the requisite transformational pulsar detection rate, while maintaining sensitivity across a wide range of binary orbital periods, including ultra-compact systems. A frequency range of 1.3-1.85 GHz will mitigate dispersion smearing and scattering.

records.description: The atomic interstellar medium shows tiny-scale optical depth fluctuations on the scale of 0.1~10,000 AU, whose origin and nature are poorly understood.
