records.title: Parkes observations for project P1449 semester 2026OCTS_02
records.description: We propose the pilot survey of the southern high-Galactic-latitude sky with the Murriyang telescope using its state-of-the-art CryoPAF receiver. Owing to their large Galactic scale heights, millisecond pulsars (MSPs) are preferentially found at intermediate and high Galactic latitudes, where lower sky temperatures, reduced interstellar scattering, and smaller dispersion measures favor the discovery of nearby, bright, and exceptionally stable systems. Despite containing a large fraction of the known MSP population and nearly half of the pulsar timing array (PTA) pulsars visible from Murriyang, the southern high-latitude sky has never been surveyed with sensitivity comparable to that achieved in the Galactic-plane. Population synthesis simulations predict that a full CryoPAF survey of the southern high-latitude sky would discover approximately 320 normal pulsars and 100 MSPs, including many binary systems. As a first step towards this objective, we propose a pilot survey of 600 degree square (278deg<l<321deg, 15deg<b<30deg). CryoPAF capabilities of covering a large filed of view, broad bandwidth, and low system temperature, provides a survey speed ~20 times greater than that the legacy multibeam receiver. Using 27-minute integrations, the proposed observations will be substantially more sensitive than previous large-area high-latitude surveys. The proposed pilot survey is expected to discover ~10 pulsars while establishing the optimal observing strategy for a future large-scale survey. It will also provide an assessment of receiver performance, sensitivity, radio-frequency interference conditions, data quality, and candidate yields under realistic observing conditions. The survey offers the opportunity to discover PTA-quality MSPs, compact binary systems, and potentially some of the fastest-spinning neutron stars known.

records.title: Parkes observations for project P1437 semester 2026OCTS_02
records.description: This project is focussed on four pulsars in the globular cluster NGC6441. PSRJ1750-3703A is a 111 millisecond pulsar in a very eccentric and long period orbit around a companion star, with a total mass of 2.18Msun. The analysis of the available data gives indication that PSRJ1750-3703A can be the lightest neutron star known so far, but a firm upper limit that confirms this statement cannot be placed yet, because all previous observations do not uniformly cover all orbital phases: in fact, they are clustered around the the apoastron. PSRJ1750-3703B is another eccentric binary pulsar, for which the detection of the periastron advance allowed a first estimation of the total mass of the binary, but non precisely enough to determine the nature of the companion. PSRJ1750-3703C and PSRJ1750-3703E are two isolated pulsars with spin periods of 26.6 and 251 milliseconds, respectively. PSRJ1750-3703C, PSRJ1750-3703E, and also PSRJ1750-3703A, are in the top 10% of the slowest pulsars in globular clusters, thus raising the question on how these pulsars can be formed in some globular clusters. The proposed observations aim to observe PSRJ1750-3703A uniformly along its orbital motion, thus allowing us to measure the pulsar mass, by measuring either the Einstein delay gamma parameter, or the orbital inclination by addressing the covariance between gamma and the time derivative of the projected semi-mayor axis of the pulsar. The proposed observations will also allow to reduce by a factor of two the uncertainty on the total mass of PSRJ1750-3703B, and to improve the rotational and astrometric parameters for PSRJ1750-3703C and PSRJ1750-3703E.

records.title: Long-term project observations for project P1032 semester 2026OCTS_03
records.description: With this proposal, we aim to continue P1032; measuring timing parameters of relativistic parameters of southern binary pulsar systems, by using data from the Parkes Ultra Wideband Low (UWL) receiver. With this Long Term Project, focus on rapid measurements of relativistic parameters, as well as parameters informing their orbital configuration, in order to enable tests of the theory of GR and constrain binary evolution scenarios, mainly via Neutron Star (NS) mass measurements. As the MeerTime project at the MeerKAT radio telescope ended in early 2024, observations with the UWL receiver now form the backbone for extending the timing baselines of many pulsars that have been part of this project. Since the source selection in the previous semesters was tailored such that the UWL receiver is the most (versatile and) suited instrument to achieve the proposed scientific goals for the chosen pulsars, we propose to continue these observations. We will use the UWL data to obtain significant orbital coverage and timing baselines on these pulsars and obtain important constraints on orbital and temporal DM variations that will help in identifying the nature of the companion stars. In addition to our main science goals, increasing the number of measured NS masses, as well as improving on current constraints has profound implications for understanding the NS internal structure.

records.title: Parkes observations for project P1452 semester 2026OCTS_02
records.description: We propose a search for pulsars, with the expectation of finding primarily millisecond pulsars, in pulsar candidates found in MeerKAT and Very Large Array imaging surveys of the Galactic Bulge and Plane. The candidates were identified primarily as steep-spectrum, circularly- and/or linearly-polarized sources, and to a lesser degree by the level of radio variability observed. We have chosen 20 pulsar candidates to target in this proposal, eleven that may be Bulge members and nine others in the Plane. We request two half-hour pointings per source with the UWL receiver, plus 15 minutes of overhead (setup and slewing) per two sources, for a total of 22.5 hours of observing time.

records.title: Parkes observations for project P1406 semester 2026OCTS_01
records.description: NGC 362 is a post-core-collapse southern globular cluster (GC) where 12 pulsars have recently been discovered. The pulsar population is very diverse, containing extremely fast-spinning, mildly recycled and slow pulsars, the vast majority of which (11 out of 12) are part of binary systems with very different orbital periods and eccentricities. One of these pulsars, NGC 362B, is a millisecond pulsar in an eccentric binary system, for which the relativistic rate of advance of periastron is already measured to high precision. We propose continued timing observations of NGC 362B aimed at detecting a second post-Keplerian parameter, the Einstein delay. This, in combination with the advance of periastron, will enable precise measurements of the component masses of the system, improving our statistics of precisely measured neutron star masses. The same observations will be used to keep timing all the other pulsars in the clusters, as well as to search for new ones.

records.title: Parkes observations for project P1444 semester 2026OCTS_01
records.description: Central Compact Objects (CCOs) have long been considered a class of X-ray neutron stars lacking multi-wavelength counterparts. However, the recent discovery of radio pulsations from a CCO challenges this picture, suggesting that at least some members of this class can produce coherent radio emission. Nevertheless, whether CCOs are related to ordinary radio pulsars or represent buried magnetars remains unclear. We propose deep radio searches of southern CCOs using the Parkes UWL receiver to identify additional radio-emitting members. The wide bandwidth enables a sensitive search for faint pulsations while allowing a frequency-dependent assessment of detectability. The discovery of even one additional radio CCO would immediately establish that radio-emitting CCOs constitute a hidden population, offering key constraints on their unusual magnetic-field configuration and evolution. This survey will therefore provide a critical test of the origin of CCOs and their place within the neutron-star population.

records.title: Soil carbon-13 isoscape for continental Australia
records.description: This collection comprises a soil δ¹³C isoscape for continental Australia and the underlying soil stable isotope observations used in its development. Specifically, the collection comprises: • Soil δ¹³C README, observations and metadata (.xlsx): An Excel workbook (soil_d13C_observations_metadata.xlsx) containing 364 sample measurements of soil organic carbon δ¹³C (‰), sample coordinates, sample source, and other associated metadata. The workbook includes separate worksheets containing a README, data dictionary (Fields), site and sample metadata (Samples), and soil δ¹³C measurements (Measurements). • Soil δ¹³C observations, flattened dataset (.csv): A tab-delimited flat file (soil_d13C_observations_flatfile.csv) containing 364 sample measurements of soil organic carbon δ¹³C (‰), sample coordinates, sample source, and associated metadata. Data has been combined in this file into a single table to facilitate import and analysis in statistical software. • Continental soil δ¹³C isoscape (GeoTIFF): A 90 m resolution raster (EPSG:3577) providing spatial predictions of soil organic carbon-13 isotope values (δ¹³C) across continental Australia (australia_soil_d13C_isoscape_90m_v1.tif). • Prediction uncertainty layer (GeoTIFF): A 90 m resolution raster (EPSG:3577) providing a spatially explicit uncertainty surface derived from Quantile Regression Forest modelling, expressed as the width of the 95% prediction interval (australia_soil_d13C_uncertainty_90m_v1.tif). This collection provides the first nationally consistent soil δ¹³C isoscape for Australia and can be used to support research into carbon cycling, ecosystem function, vegetation dynamics, stable isotope ecology, land-use change, and environmental modelling. The dataset also provides a baseline resource for future investigations of spatial and temporal variation in soil carbon isotope composition. A manuscript describing the sampling design, laboratory methods, modelling framework and validation procedures in detail, "Continental-scale controls on soil δ¹³C reveal the importance of vegetation, microbial communities, and climate" (Munroe and Welti), is currently under peer review.

records.title: Parkes observations for project P1200 semester 2026OCTS_02
records.description: We propose to use a single CryoPAF beam for high precision pulsar timing experiments to determine whether pulsar timing projects, such as P456, should continue with the UWL or transition to the CryoPAF, which has a lower system temperature in the overlapping bands and no requirement for extra calibration observations. We will observe three of the best timed pulsars and compare the resulting observations with those from P456. These pulsars are J1909-3744, J1744-1134, and J1713+0747. In addition, we will also observe J0613-0200, J1017-7156, J1902-5105, J2129-5721, which show diminished signal-to-noise above 2 GHz, but are still important to the P456 observing programme. The results will be used to demonstrate pulsar timing techniques using the CryoPAF; demonstrate that the CryoPAF can be polarization and flux calibrated to a level required for high precision timing; provide high-precision timing data sets with the CryoPAF in order to ensure there are no timing offsets within the system; compare the UWL and CryoPAF results to determine which type of pulsars are best observed with the CryoPAF and which with the UWL.

records.title: Long-term project observations for project P1205 semester 2026OCTS_03
records.description: We propose to carry out a deep Galactic Bulge pulsar survey (GBps), covering the core of the Bulge region using the new cryoPAF system on Murriyang, the Parkes radio telescope. Such a deep survey is expected to discover a population of millisecond pulsars in the Galactic Bulge and reveal their distribution and gamma-ray emissions. With these, we will lead pioneering studies on the origin of gamma-ray emission in the Galactic Bulge, a longstanding mystery in modern astronomy. The outcome of this project will significantly advance our knowledge of the formation and evolution of millisecond pulsars in the Galactic Bulge, the origin and properties of high-energy emissions, and the nature of dark matter annihilation in the Galactic Centre. A total of 200 observations with the cryoPAF is required to cover a 400 square degree region (|gl|<10 deg, |gb|<10 deg). The survey is expected to be carried out over four semesters, from April 2026 to October 2027.

records.title: Restoring Island Ecosystems at Ashmore Reef Marine Park
records.description: Ashmore Reef Marine Park supports one of Australia's most significant concentrations of marine and terrestrial biodiversity. The four islands: West Island, Middle Island, East Island, and Splittgerber Cay, provide internationally recognised nesting habitat for seabirds and sea turtles, a critical staging ground for migratory shorebirds of the East Asian–Australasian Flyway, and a plant community that includes species found nowhere else in Australian territory. Yet the terrestrial ecosystems of these islands are under sustained and compounding pressure from a suite of invasive species, ongoing seabird-mediated habitat modification, and biosecurity risks associated with the reef's geographic position and vessel traffic. The project reported here, Restoring Island Ecosystems at Ashmore Reef Marine Park (2024 to 2026), represents the third phase of a structured, cumulative scientific program. Phase 1 (Keesing et al. 2021) provided the first comprehensive multi-taxon baseline of the terrestrial ecosystem. Phase 2 (Webber et al. 2023) translated that knowledge into an evidence-based restoration plan, ranking threats, identifying knowledge gaps, and prioritising management actions. Phase 3 was designed to implement the highest-priority near- and medium-term interventions from that plan, generate the empirical evidence needed to inform subsequent management decisions, and build Parks Australia's operational capacity for ongoing management. The project was delivered through a collaboration between CSIRO, the University of Western Australia, and Monash University, with Parks Australia staff embedded as active members of each field team. Three CSIRO-led research voyages were conducted between May 2024 and April 2025, with additional supplementary activities supported through a touristic bird-watching voyage in November 2024 and a Parks Australia rodent surveillance voyage in October to November 2025. The project addressed ten project Aims drawn directly from the Ashmore Reef Marine Park Restoration Management Plan (Webber et al. 2023).

records.title: The utility of eDNA monitoring eukaryote communities for catchment assessments
records.description: This study tested the efficacy of using environmental DNA biodiversity data as biological indicators of water quality using the Great Barrier Reef catchment as a case study. We passively sampled two catchment areas for ecosystem assessment with citizen scientists. Environmental DNA samples were collected in parallel with water quality sampling (nutrients, pesticides, sediments) to investigate trends between environmental parameters and eDNA eukaryote community composition. Sampling took place on three occasions.

records.title: Long-term project observations for project P885 semester 2026OCTS_01
records.description: We propose a modest program to continue monitoring 4 of the 6 known radio magnetars in order to achieve three primary science goals. The first is to characterise magnetar outbursts over long timescales, for which tracking their rotational, flux density, and polarisation properties provide a clear view of the impulse response of their magnetic fields. Second, understanding the links between magnetars the mysterious fast radio burst phenomenon through the discovery of rare emission and propagation effects, shared spectro-temporal phenomenology, and connections to high-energy (X-ray/gamma-ray) phenomena. Lastly, our continued monitoring has enormous benefit to the wider magnetar community, providing rapid alerts to changes in activity, adding context to unusual behaviour detected by high-energy observations, and a host of supplementary science through the teams extensive collaborative networks. The project and its precursors have been running since 2007 and have contributed to 22 publications since then. This is the first submission since the project was converted to long-term status.

records.title: Visualisation of geometric digital twin for additive manufacturing (gDT-AM): In-process part surface reconstruction and shape monitoring
records.description: Additive manufacturing (AM) faces critical challenges, particularly in achieving real-time quality control and precision. These challenges are heightened in complex geometries and high-deposition-rate robotic AM (HDRRAM) processes such as robotic Cold-Spray. Traditional quality control methods generally detect defects after the entire part is produced, leading to material waste and increased lead time and cost. The lack of real-time insight during production limits the ability to identify and correct the process variations as they occur. To address this, digital twin technology has emerged as a powerful tool within the intelligent manufacturing paradigm. This video shows a novel geometric digital twin framework, gDT-AM, specifically designed for HDRRAM. It continuously captures and maps the part’s geometry in real-time during printing. It incorporates two experimentally validated alternative methods for precise and fast surface reconstruction from sparse spatio-temporal 2D line profiler scans. Additionally, the gDT-AM introduces an automated layer-by-layer geometric deviation measurement technique. This enables the identification of potential defects during production, facilitating timely interventions that reduce waste and ensure quality. The proposed gDT-AM allows further research on optimising online process parameters and tool-path correction. Ultimately, integrating digital twins embodies the foundational principles of smart manufacturing by facilitating a closed-loop, self-optimising production environment characterised by connectivity, automation, data-driven decision-making, and adaptive process control.

records.title: Parkes observations for project P1411 semester 2026OCTS_02
records.description: Conventional blind pulsar surveys that search for periodic signals in high-time-resolution data are increasingly limited by interstellar scattering at high dispersion measure (DM), orbital modulation in compact binaries, scintillation effects, and intensive computational demands. The Australian Square Kilometre Array Pathfinder (ASKAP) Evolutionary Map of the Universe (EMU) survey provides ultra-deep radio continuum maps enabling complementary image-domain pulsar searches that bypass these limitations. We have discovered seven new pulsars through three targeted strategies: (1) identifying compact sources embedded in supernova remnants (SNRs) and pulsar wind nebulae (PWNe), (2) detecting highly variable sources via variance imaging, and (3) selecting highly circularly polarised compact sources. Our sample includes three highly scattered pulsars (PSR J1638-4713 , PSR J1643-4511, and PSR J1631-4722 with DM > 800 pc/cm^3) including two pulsars associated with PWNe. Two millisecond pulsars (PSR J0927-7641 and PSR J1838-5949) are in potential wide binary systems with orbital periods of several tens of days, and two additional normal pulsars (PSR J1153-7106 and PSR 2223-0654). We propose follow-up timing observations of these pulsars with Murriyang's Ultra-Wideband Low (UWL) receiver to obtain phase-connected timing solutions, measure precise positions and spin parameters, and determine orbital characteristics for the binary systems,. These observations will enable studies of pulsar formation mechanisms, binary evolution pathways, PWN-SNR interactions, and validate image-based discovery techniques as powerful complements to traditional blind surveys for detecting elusive pulsars.

Up to ~50 pulsars are predicted from the 30 deg^2 2026OCTS survey region, including 3-6 millisecond pulsars, representing in itself an impressive yield and associated scientific promise. 2.5-hr pointings are proposed to provide the requisite transformational pulsar detection rate, while maintaining sensitivity across a wide range of binary orbital periods, including ultra-compact systems. A frequency range of 1.3-1.85 GHz will mitigate dispersion smearing and scattering.

records.title: Long-term project observations for project P1321 semester 2026OCTS_07
records.description: The atomic interstellar medium shows tiny-scale optical depth fluctuations on the scale of 0.1~10,000 AU, whose origin and nature are poorly understood. The existence of this Tiny-Scale Atomic Structure (TSAS) has significant implications, potentially calling into question our fundamental understanding of heating, cooling and dynamical processes in the interstellar medium. Yet observations remain sparse. This long-term project plans to search for temporal variations in HI absorption spectra seen against background pulsars to characterise TSAS in the Milky Way interstellar medium (ISM). These observations constitute the largest number of sightlines and densest temporal sampling ever performed in a single experiment, and will test predictions that TSAS is the tail end of a turbulent cascade, constrain its minimum size scale (down to resolutions of ~0.05 AU) and potentially provide the first direct measurements of pressures in "large" TSAS features of > 1000 AU. We make use of the phase-resolved spectral line mode that we have recently implemented on Parkes, which has cut data rates and processing times by factors of ~1000 compared to past studies. This is an expansion of our pilot P1321 to a long term study.

records.title: Parkes observations for project P1444 semester 2026OCTS_03
records.description: Central Compact Objects (CCOs) have long been considered a class of X-ray neutron stars lacking multi-wavelength counterparts. However, the recent discovery of radio pulsations from a CCO challenges this picture, suggesting that at least some members of this class can produce coherent radio emission. Nevertheless, whether CCOs are related to ordinary radio pulsars or represent buried magnetars remains unclear. We propose deep radio searches of southern CCOs using the Parkes UWL receiver to identify additional radio-emitting members. The wide bandwidth enables a sensitive search for faint pulsations while allowing a frequency-dependent assessment of detectability. The discovery of even one additional radio CCO would immediately establish that radio-emitting CCOs constitute a hidden population, offering key constraints on their unusual magnetic-field configuration and evolution. This survey will therefore provide a critical test of the origin of CCOs and their place within the neutron-star population.

records.title: Parkes observations for project P1183 semester 2026OCTS_01
records.description: FRB 20220529 is the only repeating FRB known to exhibit rotation-measure (RM) flares (sudden, large-amplitude RM excursions lasting ~two weeks). Two such flares have now been detected: the first in December 2023 (only the decay captured) and the second in August--September 2025, ~19 months later. The second flare was observed with full temporal coverage, revealing a rise and decay of ~14 days each, an RM sign opposite to the first flare, and a prolonged post-flare quiescence. These two events alone cannot establish whether the recurrence is strictly periodic or stochastic. If periodic, the third flare is expected around March - April 2027, which is squarely within the 2026OCTS semester. Detecting a third flare with a similar waiting time would provide a "smoking gun" for a binary origin; a non-detection throughout the semester would rule out strict periodicity. Either outcome is decisive. We propose to continue monitoring FRB 20220529 with the Parkes UWL receiver at one session per fortnight throughout 2026OCTS.

records.title: Parkes observations for project P1054 semester 2026OCTS_03
records.description: With this proposal we ask time to continue our timing follow-up campaign of pulsars discovered with the MeerKAT telescope. Fiftytwo sources have been discovered in targeted observations of Fermi unidentified point sources, 2 towards Supernova Remnants, 27 in the Magellanic Clouds, 128 in Globular Clusters and 96 in a survey of the Galactic plane. A large fraction of the new discoveries are recycled pulsars (including a few relativistic systems, a pulsar with a planetary companion and several 'spider' binaries), or young pulsars. Timing observations have an essential role in exploiting the full potential of any pulsar discovery, allowing for the precise measurement of rotational, astrometric and orbital parameters which, in turn, give us powerful tools to improve our understanding of the physics in extreme environments as well as of the population of neutron stars as a whole. The UWL receiver of the Parkes telescope is a sensitive, versatile instrument that is allowing us to successfully time these new sources, in the bright-end of TRAPUM discoveries.

records.title: Long-term project observations for project P574 semester 2026OCTS_01
records.description: We request time to observe 270 pulsars on a regular basis in order to achieve three main science goals. The first is to understand pulsars: how do they spin down and what disrupts this process, how and why their profiles vary with time, whether they precess or have planetary mass companions, in short all the things that make pulsar timing noisier than the perfect clock. Secondly we want to understand the interstellar medium of our Galaxy through repeated monitoring of dispersion measure, rotation measure and flux density variations in conjunction with scintillation parameters. Finally, we provide these data as a community service both to the high-energy community where we have strong collaborative links (particularly to Fermi) and to the radio pulsar astronomers generally through the CSIRO archive. The project is on-going since 2007, we are (co-)authors on 107 papers arising from the P574 data. The data have contributed to the PhD theses of students from Bordeaux, Manchester, Oxford, Stanford, and Swinburne. We are seeking long-term project status with a view to continuing the project into the SKA era.

records.title: Parkes observations for project P1449 semester 2026OCTS_03
records.description: We propose the pilot survey of the southern high-Galactic-latitude sky with the Murriyang telescope using its state-of-the-art CryoPAF receiver. Owing to their large Galactic scale heights, millisecond pulsars (MSPs) are preferentially found at intermediate and high Galactic latitudes, where lower sky temperatures, reduced interstellar scattering, and smaller dispersion measures favor the discovery of nearby, bright, and exceptionally stable systems. Despite containing a large fraction of the known MSP population and nearly half of the pulsar timing array (PTA) pulsars visible from Murriyang, the southern high-latitude sky has never been surveyed with sensitivity comparable to that achieved in the Galactic-plane. Population synthesis simulations predict that a full CryoPAF survey of the southern high-latitude sky would discover approximately 320 normal pulsars and 100 MSPs, including many binary systems. As a first step towards this objective, we propose a pilot survey of 600 degree square (278deg<l<321deg, 15deg<b<30deg). CryoPAF capabilities of covering a large filed of view, broad bandwidth, and low system temperature, provides a survey speed ~20 times greater than that the legacy multibeam receiver. Using 27-minute integrations, the proposed observations will be substantially more sensitive than previous large-area high-latitude surveys. The proposed pilot survey is expected to discover ~10 pulsars while establishing the optimal observing strategy for a future large-scale survey. It will also provide an assessment of receiver performance, sensitivity, radio-frequency interference conditions, data quality, and candidate yields under realistic observing conditions. The survey offers the opportunity to discover PTA-quality MSPs, compact binary systems, and potentially some of the fastest-spinning neutron stars known.

records.title: Eastern water dragon fungal disease functional omics dataset
records.description: Proteomics, metabolomics and lipidomics analysis of serum samples collected from easter water dragons (Intellagama lesueurii) infected with a fungal pathogen (Nannizziopsis barbatae) and without infection. Produced to investigate how infection alters the reptile host physiological pathways and possible immune response.

records.title: Parkes observations for project P960 semester 2026OCTS_01
records.description: We aim to carry out receiver pointing and characterisation tests of Parkes receivers. Typically, these tests are carried out after the receiver package is installed, but time does not always allow for proper characterisation. Receivers for consideration include UWL, MARS and 13MM packages. In addition to cross-referencing C007 for flux calibration via pointing, we aim to conduct gain-elevation and system temperature experiments using the Moon, to ensure users of the Parkes Observatory have the most accurate information available for calibration purposes.

records.title: Long-term project observations for project P1032 semester 2026OCTS_04
records.description: With this proposal, we aim to continue P1032; measuring timing parameters of relativistic parameters of southern binary pulsar systems, by using data from the Parkes Ultra Wideband Low (UWL) receiver. With this Long Term Project, focus on rapid measurements of relativistic parameters, as well as parameters informing their orbital configuration, in order to enable tests of the theory of GR and constrain binary evolution scenarios, mainly via Neutron Star (NS) mass measurements. As the MeerTime project at the MeerKAT radio telescope ended in early 2024, observations with the UWL receiver now form the backbone for extending the timing baselines of many pulsars that have been part of this project. Since the source selection in the previous semesters was tailored such that the UWL receiver is the most (versatile and) suited instrument to achieve the proposed scientific goals for the chosen pulsars, we propose to continue these observations. We will use the UWL data to obtain significant orbital coverage and timing baselines on these pulsars and obtain important constraints on orbital and temporal DM variations that will help in identifying the nature of the companion stars. In addition to our main science goals, increasing the number of measured NS masses, as well as improving on current constraints has profound implications for understanding the NS internal structure.

records.title: Long-term project observations for project P456 semester 2026OCTS_02
records.description: The Parkes Pulsar Timing Array (PPTA) project has three primary goals: (a) detection of gravitational waves from astronomical sources, (b) establishment of a pulsar timescale, and (c) improvement of our understanding of Solar-system dynamics. We are now in an exciting regime where a signal detected in our (and other data sets) has the form expected for a gravitational wave background. We, along with the international community, are now working hard to either confirm or deny this result, and to determine the astrophysical origin of this signal. With this proposal, we aim to maintain our pre-eminent position in the field. This is a continuing proposal for which observations of millisecond pulsars (MSPs) will continue to improve bounds on ultra-low-frequency gravitational waves until they are detected with confidence. Continued Parkes observations will remain valuable at least until the first stage of the SKA is able to improve on our sensitivity and observing cadence. Even after the gravitational wave background is detected, continued observations will resolve the background origin and individual sources will be identified; advancing the nascent field of gravitational wave astronomy.

records.title: Parkes observations for project P1406 semester 2026OCTS_03
records.description: NGC 362 is a post-core-collapse southern globular cluster (GC) where 12 pulsars have recently been discovered. The pulsar population is very diverse, containing extremely fast-spinning, mildly recycled and slow pulsars, the vast majority of which (11 out of 12) are part of binary systems with very different orbital periods and eccentricities. One of these pulsars, NGC 362B, is a millisecond pulsar in an eccentric binary system, for which the relativistic rate of advance of periastron is already measured to high precision. We propose continued timing observations of NGC 362B aimed at detecting a second post-Keplerian parameter, the Einstein delay. This, in combination with the advance of periastron, will enable precise measurements of the component masses of the system, improving our statistics of precisely measured neutron star masses. The same observations will be used to keep timing all the other pulsars in the clusters, as well as to search for new ones.

records.title: Australian Government Consolidated Financial Statements Tables and Data
records.description: The Consolidated Financial Statements (CFS) since 1995-96 are available on the Department of Finance website at: http://www.finance.gov.au/publications/commonwealth-consolidated-financial-statements. The CFS for the Australian Government present the whole of government and general government sector (GGS) financial reports and are prepared in accordance with _AASB 1049 Whole of Government and General Government Sector Financial Reporting_. They are required by section 48 of the _Public Governance, Performance and Accountability Act 2013_ (formerly section 54 of the _Financial Management and Accountability Act 1997_). The CFS include the consolidated results for all Australian Government controlled entities as well as disaggregated information on the sectors of GGS, public non financial corporations and public financial corporations. This dataset provides an historical series of a collection of published CFS for the whole of government and GGS from 2008-09, including the: • Income Statement • Balance Sheet • Cash Flow Statement The Historical CFS series is provided to assist those who wish to access and analyse this data. Please note that this dataset represents published information and will not be recast. Figures may not be directly comparable over time due to changes of classification, accounting standards or budget treatments. This data is released by the Department of Finance.

records.title: Hourly near-surface air temperature grids for Australia
records.description: Note: This collection is now maintained on the TERN Data Discovery Portal (https://dx.doi.org/10.25901/h79h-jw68). The latest version includes a space- and time-varying coastal distance index for interpolation. This collection provides hourly near-surface (1.5 m) air temperature grids for Australia with a spatial resolution of 1 km. These data are spatially interpolated using quart-variate thin plate splines (full spline dependence on easting, northing, elevation, and time-varying coastal distance index), and include two key products: i) a long term climatology for every hour on every 5th day of the year (representing 1990-2019), and ii) a time-series of hourly air temperature data beginning on 01/Jan/2015.

records.title: Oat Crown Rust Resistance and Pathogen Dataset
records.description: This page will direct to key data repositories, and other links related to project 'Durable Resistance to Oat Crown Rust (CSP2204-007RTX)' 1) Collection of rust samples from across major Australian oat-growing regions and characterisation. The collection includes 214 Puccinia coronata f.sp. avenae (Pca) isolates representing oat growing seasons in Australia from 2022 -2024. This combined with other existing resources allowed to data from a total of 326 Pca isolates. The population dynamics and composition were analysed and compared to other existing international data. The project also was leveraged to enable the release of gapless chromosome level assemblies for 15 Australian Pca isolates and the acquisition of phenotypic and genotypic data. 2) Collection of oat lines that represent two independent differential sets to assign race codes. Multiple oat lines were accessed from the Australian Grains Genebank to replicate the existing panel used by the surveillance program in Australia (University of Sydney). In parallel, the project also accessed the panel used by the surveillance program at the USDA-ARS for the USA. DArTSeq genotypic data was acquired for these and in addition for the panel used by the University of Sydney for comparison. 3) Validation and implementation of molecular KASP markers closely linked to resistance genes. Publicly available molecular markers were examined and validated using oat differential sets and other oat germplasm. Whenever possible markers were improved to increase sensitivity. After KASP markers were validated, they were used to screen the OzOat panel. 4) Additional genotypic data and rust resistance data to enable gene discovery. This project examined two recombinant inbred line (RIL) mapping populations under Australian field conditions to identify QTL associated with rust resistance. These are ‘Provena x 94197A1-9-2-2-2-5’ and ‘CDC Boyer x 94197A1-9-2-2-2-5’—referred to as Provena x GS7 (n=92) and Boyer x GS7 (n=100), respectively (Babiker et al., 2015). The entire OzOat panel and other putative of resistance donors, particularly Adult Plant resistance, were also examined under field conditions. 5) RNASeq data from 50 oat lines under controlled growth conditions, including both infected with a mixture of rust isolates and non-infected (mock). 6) Hypoxia-induced necrosis phenotypes in the OzOat panel.

records.title: ASKAP Data Products for Project AS305 (A pilot survey of sub arcsecond scale sources with ASKAP for space weather and astrophysical studies): images and visibilities
records.description: We propose to combine the unique wide field survey capabilites of ASKAP with its high-fidelity snapshot imaging capability to use the phenomenon of interplanetary scintillation (IPS) to detect sub arcsec scale structure in large numbers of sources. The observations proposed here will: i) detect a source density of >5/sq. deg. which is unprecedented for compact sources, ii) map the solar wind in unprecedented detail, vastly improving on the current abilities to study space weather phenomenon as they evolve across interplanetary space, and iii) in concert with published Murchison Widefield Array IPS data and 20 GHz survey data, enable us to study statistical changes in compact source populations from high to low radio frequencies.

records.title: Long-term project observations for project P1205 semester 2026OCTS_04
records.description: We propose to carry out a deep Galactic Bulge pulsar survey (GBps), covering the core of the Bulge region using the new cryoPAF system on Murriyang, the Parkes radio telescope. Such a deep survey is expected to discover a population of millisecond pulsars in the Galactic Bulge and reveal their distribution and gamma-ray emissions. With these, we will lead pioneering studies on the origin of gamma-ray emission in the Galactic Bulge, a longstanding mystery in modern astronomy. The outcome of this project will significantly advance our knowledge of the formation and evolution of millisecond pulsars in the Galactic Bulge, the origin and properties of high-energy emissions, and the nature of dark matter annihilation in the Galactic Centre. A total of 200 observations with the cryoPAF is required to cover a 400 square degree region (|gl|<10 deg, |gb|<10 deg). The survey is expected to be carried out over four semesters, from April 2026 to October 2027.

records.title: Parkes observations for project P1452 semester 2026OCTS_03
records.description: We propose a search for pulsars, with the expectation of finding primarily millisecond pulsars, in pulsar candidates found in MeerKAT and Very Large Array imaging surveys of the Galactic Bulge and Plane. The candidates were identified primarily as steep-spectrum, circularly- and/or linearly-polarized sources, and to a lesser degree by the level of radio variability observed. We have chosen 20 pulsar candidates to target in this proposal, eleven that may be Bulge members and nine others in the Plane. We request two half-hour pointings per source with the UWL receiver, plus 15 minutes of overhead (setup and slewing) per two sources, for a total of 22.5 hours of observing time.

records.title: Parkes observations for project P1200 semester 2026OCTS_03
records.description: We propose to use a single CryoPAF beam for high precision pulsar timing experiments to determine whether pulsar timing projects, such as P456, should continue with the UWL or transition to the CryoPAF, which has a lower system temperature in the overlapping bands and no requirement for extra calibration observations. We will observe three of the best timed pulsars and compare the resulting observations with those from P456. These pulsars are J1909-3744, J1744-1134, and J1713+0747. In addition, we will also observe J0613-0200, J1017-7156, J1902-5105, J2129-5721, which show diminished signal-to-noise above 2 GHz, but are still important to the P456 observing programme. The results will be used to demonstrate pulsar timing techniques using the CryoPAF; demonstrate that the CryoPAF can be polarization and flux calibrated to a level required for high precision timing; provide high-precision timing data sets with the CryoPAF in order to ensure there are no timing offsets within the system; compare the UWL and CryoPAF results to determine which type of pulsars are best observed with the CryoPAF and which with the UWL.

records.title: Parkes observations for project P1390 semester 2026OCTS_02
records.description: We propose 24 hours of Parkes UWL observations to continue timing and wideband monitoring of two nearby Extremely Variable Radio Bursters (EVRBs): J1606-0854 and J2357+2454. EVRBs are a newly defined population of neutron stars whose single-pulse fluence ratios exceed 10^4, bridging the gap between ordinary pulsars and FRBs. J1606-0854 (DM ~ 4.95 pc cm^-3) and J2357+2454 (DM ~ 8.06 pc cm^-3) have the lowest DMs among known RRATs, placing both within 1 kpc. Our 2026APRS pilot observations with Parkes UWL have demonstrated its unique capabilities: (i) J1606-0854 is detected at ~1 burst per 3 hours, with the UWL revealing narrow-band emission that drifts in frequency across the band. This behaviour is inaccessible to FAST's 1.0--1.5 GHz receiver, which entirely misses bursts falling outside its narrow window; (ii) J2357+2454 is detected at tens of bursts per hour, with the UWL uncovering strong scintillation across its full frequency range. records.title: Yellow-tailed Black Cockatoo genomic data
records.description: Genomic data from paper: Joseph, L., D’Angelo, J., Schodde, R., Aplin, L., and Kearns, A.M. Molecular and morphological approaches to taxonomy and historical biogeography of Yellow-tailed Black-Cockatoos (Zanda funerea), Emu, in revision. Dataset represents raw reads and SNPs called from the DArTseq pipeline for 71 museum specimens collected across the range of Zanda funerea. Genetic data show little correlation with subspecies within Z. funerea beyond, possibly, differentiating large-bodied eastern mainland populations from all others.

records.title: AcceleTrait Hyperspectral Processing Pipelines and Trait Modelling Workflows
records.description: This collection contains software, processing pipelines and modelling workflows developed for the AcceleTrait Plus program to support UAV hyperspectral phenotyping, image processing, spectral data extraction and trait prediction. The repository includes workflows for processing hyperspectral imagery acquired from UAV platforms, including radiometric calibration, image registration, plot identification, pixel classification and representative spectrum extraction. The collection also contains modelling workflows for dataset generation, trait prediction, machine learning, deep learning and transformer-based pretraining approaches. Processing pipelines support imagery acquired from multiple hyperspectral platforms including HySpex Mjolnir and AFX17 systems. Modelling components include tools for preparing phenotyping datasets, developing predictive models and evaluating spectral relationships with physiological and agronomic traits. The collection includes R and Python code, project configuration files, workflow documentation, implementation notes and supporting utilities required to reproduce image-processing and modelling activities developed within the AcceleTrait Plus program. This collection is intended to support reproducibility, maintenance and continued development of hyperspectral processing and modelling workflows used in crop phenotyping and physiological trait prediction research.

records.title: Parkes observations for project P1054 semester 2026OCTS_05
records.description: With this proposal we ask time to continue our timing follow-up campaign of pulsars discovered with the MeerKAT telescope. Fiftytwo sources have been discovered in targeted observations of Fermi unidentified point sources, 2 towards Supernova Remnants, 27 in the Magellanic Clouds, 128 in Globular Clusters and 96 in a survey of the Galactic plane. A large fraction of the new discoveries are recycled pulsars (including a few relativistic systems, a pulsar with a planetary companion and several 'spider' binaries), or young pulsars. Timing observations have an essential role in exploiting the full potential of any pulsar discovery, allowing for the precise measurement of rotational, astrometric and orbital parameters which, in turn, give us powerful tools to improve our understanding of the physics in extreme environments as well as of the population of neutron stars as a whole. The UWL receiver of the Parkes telescope is a sensitive, versatile instrument that is allowing us to successfully time these new sources, in the bright-end of TRAPUM discoveries.

records.title: Parkes observations for project P595 semester 2026OCTS_06
records.description: We propose to continue the PULSE@Parkes project in which high school students from Australia and around the World use the Parkes radio telescope in a remote observing model to observe and analyse pulsar data. The data from some PULSE@Parkes observations are used to support the space missions, other observations supplement the P456 Pulsar Timing Array project and the remainder were chosen in order to make a detailed analysis of pulsar timing irregularities and intermittency.

records.title: Parkes observations for project P1200 semester 2026OCTS_04
records.description: We propose to use a single CryoPAF beam for high precision pulsar timing experiments to determine whether pulsar timing projects, such as P456, should continue with the UWL or transition to the CryoPAF, which has a lower system temperature in the overlapping bands and no requirement for extra calibration observations. We will observe three of the best timed pulsars and compare the resulting observations with those from P456. These pulsars are J1909-3744, J1744-1134, and J1713+0747. In addition, we will also observe J0613-0200, J1017-7156, J1902-5105, J2129-5721, which show diminished signal-to-noise above 2 GHz, but are still important to the P456 observing programme. The results will be used to demonstrate pulsar timing techniques using the CryoPAF; demonstrate that the CryoPAF can be polarization and flux calibrated to a level required for high precision timing; provide high-precision timing data sets with the CryoPAF in order to ensure there are no timing offsets within the system; compare the UWL and CryoPAF results to determine which type of pulsars are best observed with the CryoPAF and which with the UWL.

records.title: Long-term project observations for project P885 semester 2026OCTS_02
records.description: We propose a modest program to continue monitoring 4 of the 6 known radio magnetars in order to achieve three primary science goals. The first is to characterise magnetar outbursts over long timescales, for which tracking their rotational, flux density, and polarisation properties provide a clear view of the impulse response of their magnetic fields. Second, understanding the links between magnetars the mysterious fast radio burst phenomenon through the discovery of rare emission and propagation effects, shared spectro-temporal phenomenology, and connections to high-energy (X-ray/gamma-ray) phenomena. Lastly, our continued monitoring has enormous benefit to the wider magnetar community, providing rapid alerts to changes in activity, adding context to unusual behaviour detected by high-energy observations, and a host of supplementary science through the teams extensive collaborative networks. The project and its precursors have been running since 2007 and have contributed to 22 publications since then. This is the first submission since the project was converted to long-term status.

records.title: Parkes observations for project P1411 semester 2026OCTS_03
records.description: Conventional blind pulsar surveys that search for periodic signals in high-time-resolution data are increasingly limited by interstellar scattering at high dispersion measure (DM), orbital modulation in compact binaries, scintillation effects, and intensive computational demands. The Australian Square Kilometre Array Pathfinder (ASKAP) Evolutionary Map of the Universe (EMU) survey provides ultra-deep radio continuum maps enabling complementary image-domain pulsar searches that bypass these limitations. We have discovered seven new pulsars through three targeted strategies: (1) identifying compact sources embedded in supernova remnants (SNRs) and pulsar wind nebulae (PWNe), (2) detecting highly variable sources via variance imaging, and (3) selecting highly circularly polarised compact sources. Our sample includes three highly scattered pulsars (PSR J1638-4713 , PSR J1643-4511, and PSR J1631-4722 with DM > 800 pc/cm^3) including two pulsars associated with PWNe. Two millisecond pulsars (PSR J0927-7641 and PSR J1838-5949) are in potential wide binary systems with orbital periods of several tens of days, and two additional normal pulsars (PSR J1153-7106 and PSR 2223-0654). We propose follow-up timing observations of these pulsars with Murriyang's Ultra-Wideband Low (UWL) receiver to obtain phase-connected timing solutions, measure precise positions and spin parameters, and determine orbital characteristics for the binary systems,. These observations will enable studies of pulsar formation mechanisms, binary evolution pathways, PWN-SNR interactions, and validate image-based discovery techniques as powerful complements to traditional blind surveys for detecting elusive pulsars.

records.title: Long-term project observations for project P1032 semester 2026OCTS_06
records.description: With this proposal, we aim to continue P1032; measuring timing parameters of relativistic parameters of southern binary pulsar systems, by using data from the Parkes Ultra Wideband Low (UWL) receiver. With this Long Term Project, focus on rapid measurements of relativistic parameters, as well as parameters informing their orbital configuration, in order to enable tests of the theory of GR and constrain binary evolution scenarios, mainly via Neutron Star (NS) mass measurements. As the MeerTime project at the MeerKAT radio telescope ended in early 2024, observations with the UWL receiver now form the backbone for extending the timing baselines of many pulsars that have been part of this project. Since the source selection in the previous semesters was tailored such that the UWL receiver is the most (versatile and) suited instrument to achieve the proposed scientific goals for the chosen pulsars, we propose to continue these observations. We will use the UWL data to obtain significant orbital coverage and timing baselines on these pulsars and obtain important constraints on orbital and temporal DM variations that will help in identifying the nature of the companion stars. In addition to our main science goals, increasing the number of measured NS masses, as well as improving on current constraints has profound implications for understanding the NS internal structure.

records.title: Parkes observations for project P1444 semester 2026OCTS_05
records.description: Central Compact Objects (CCOs) have long been considered a class of X-ray neutron stars lacking multi-wavelength counterparts. However, the recent discovery of radio pulsations from a CCO challenges this picture, suggesting that at least some members of this class can produce coherent radio emission. Nevertheless, whether CCOs are related to ordinary radio pulsars or represent buried magnetars remains unclear. We propose deep radio searches of southern CCOs using the Parkes UWL receiver to identify additional radio-emitting members. The wide bandwidth enables a sensitive search for faint pulsations while allowing a frequency-dependent assessment of detectability. The discovery of even one additional radio CCO would immediately establish that radio-emitting CCOs constitute a hidden population, offering key constraints on their unusual magnetic-field configuration and evolution. This survey will therefore provide a critical test of the origin of CCOs and their place within the neutron-star population.

records.title: Long-term project observations for project P1205 semester 2026OCTS_06
records.description: We propose to carry out a deep Galactic Bulge pulsar survey (GBps), covering the core of the Bulge region using the new cryoPAF system on Murriyang, the Parkes radio telescope. Such a deep survey is expected to discover a population of millisecond pulsars in the Galactic Bulge and reveal their distribution and gamma-ray emissions. With these, we will lead pioneering studies on the origin of gamma-ray emission in the Galactic Bulge, a longstanding mystery in modern astronomy. The outcome of this project will significantly advance our knowledge of the formation and evolution of millisecond pulsars in the Galactic Bulge, the origin and properties of high-energy emissions, and the nature of dark matter annihilation in the Galactic Centre. A total of 200 observations with the cryoPAF is required to cover a 400 square degree region (|gl|<10 deg, |gb|<10 deg). The survey is expected to be carried out over four semesters, from April 2026 to October 2027.

records.title: Parkes observations for project P1428 semester 2026OCTS_02
records.description: Globular Clusters (GCs) are renowned to be the host of a wealth of radio pulsars, most of which are millisecond pulsars. The extreme stellar densities characterizing the central regions of GCs promote the formation of binary systems where neutron stars can be recycled, and the formation of pulsars and binaries with extreme or unconventional properties. GCs have therefore been prime targets for pulsar searching and, as of today, more than 360 pulsars have been found in 46 different clusters. The much larger computing power and much more modern algorithms available today have recently fostered the re-processing of archival Parkes GC data. This has led to the discovery of a few new pulsars, and several promising candidates. Here, we request 22 hours of observing time to re-observe a set of 10 GCs where 56 promising candidate pulsars have recently been found via reprocessing of archival Parkes data. The recently installed Ultra-Wide-band Low receiver, in combination with the modern APOLLO backend, will provide a sharp increase in sensitivity compared to the archival data. This will allow us to confirm or refute the candidates, and potentially even discover additional pulsars. Confirming at least one pulsar in a GC has a great scientific value, since it would allow us to know the approximate dispersion measure associated with cluster, greatly easing the search for additional pulsars in the cluster, and it would increase the total number of clusters known to host radio pulsars, contributing to our understanding of the population of pulsars in GCs.

records.title: Parkes observations for project P1379 semester 2026OCTS_01
records.description: We propose a simultaneous joint observation campaign using the Parkes radio telescope and the EP satellite to observation five magnetars with known radio emission. Under simultaneous observations, we aim to investigate the correlation between their radio and X-ray emissions, including pulse profiles, flux intensity, polarization evolution, correlated multi-wavelength behavior and timing behavior.

records.title: Parkes observations for project P1365 semester 2026OCTS_03
records.description: Following the successful demonstration of a pilot first-pass (shallow) search of a small fraction of the sky, the second-pass processing has commenced for the SMART pulsar survey, which involves deep searches of 80-minute observations. Over the past year, this second-pass processing has led to the discovery of 21 new pulsars (including two millisecond pulsars), bringing the total number of SMART discoveries to 25 when combined with the first-pass results. These outcomes hint at the exciting promise of this first southern-sky pulsar survey in the frequency band of SKA-Low. All new pulsars require timing observations to determine their spin and astrometric parameters. Another important aspect of timing newly discovered pulsars is to identify specialised targets for further detailed follow-ups. Since the MWA is currently not available for routine pulsar observations, timing follow-ups rely on other telescopes. The Parkes Murriyang telescope, with identical sky coverage, high sensitivity, and wide frequency coverage, offers the best option for timing SMART discoveries. We have refined the proposed targets from our previous proposal by removing six pulsars that will have accumulated a full year of Parkes timing data by the end of the current semester, and by adding six newly discovered sources, five from typical pulsar searching methods, and one from image-based transient searching techniques, thereby maintaining a total sample of 11 pulsars. The data will also allow us to study pulse profiles, polarisation, and flux densities from ~100 MHz to 4 GHz. The analysis/results will be included in a forthcoming publication.

records.description: This layer group describes multibeam echosounder data collected on RV Southern Surveyor voyage ss200509 titled "Nature and origin of the Naturaliste Plateau and Diamantina Zone: a key to understanding the assembly and breakup history of eastern Gondwana". records.title: Parkes observations for project P477 semester 2006APRS_01
records.description: Given the extremely fruitful results of the completed Parkes Multibeam Pulsar Survey, Parkes Multibeam High Latitude Pulsar Survey, and Parkes Multibeam Intermediate Latitude Swinburne Survey, we have undertaken a new deep search for pulsars, sampling the galactic plane in the direction of the Perseus Arm at galactic coordinates 200 deg <l<260 deg and |b|<5 deg. This experiment will complete the deep low latitude survey of the galactic plane strip visible from Parkes, providing an invaluable basis to any statistical study of the pulsar population and in particular improving the knowledge of the poorly known radial distribution of the pulsars in the outer regions of the Galaxy disk. Given the survey parameters and the sky coverage, this search will lead to the discovery of few tens of sources, with a good discovery rate (twice higher than for the two most recent large-scale searches performed at Parkes) and with a favorable ratio of millisecond over longer period pulsars. The requested range of Sidereal Time is complementary to other pulsar projects. We propose to continue this project and start the timing observations of the discovered pulsars.

records.title: Parkes observations for project P477 semester 2010APRS_01
records.description: This is a proposal to complete survey and timing observations for the Perseus Arm Pulsar Survey, covering the area of the sky enclosed between galactic coordinates 200<l<260 and b<|5|. Reobservation of 37 pointings, affected either by strong radio frequency interferences or by loss in sensitivity due to a fault in the parallactification of the 21-cm Multibeam receiver, is infact required in order to have a complete and uniform coverage of the selected area, crucial to fulfil the aims of this survey. Fourteen new pulsars have been to date discovered in the already observed portion of the survey, nine of which have a coherent timing solution. The five remaining objects, plus any that might be discovered in the last pointings to be observed, still require about a year of monthly timing observations, being only recently discovered. We hence require a total of 45 hours in this semester for a final tidying of the Perseus Arm Survey.

records.title: ASKAP Data Products for Project AS333 (NAASHI - A Northern ASKAP Absorption Search in HI ): images and visibilities
records.description: We propose to search for redshifted 21 cm HI absorption (at z = 0.4 to 1.0) in 156 northern ASKAP fields at declination +15 to +40 deg. The overlap between this region and the northern-hemisphere DESI optical spectroscopic survey allows us to carry out new multi-wavelength studies that lie outside the science goals of the (now-completed) ASKAP FLASH SSP. We focus on two main science areas: (i) the earliest stages in the evolution of powerful radio galaxies and the role of HI in this evolution; and (ii) the relationship between HI absorption and the optical NaD and MgII absorption lines that are used as proxies for cool gas in distant galaxies at cosmic noon and beyond. The observations proposed here will also have significant legacy value because of ASKAP's unique capability for wide-field spectral-line surveys.

records.title: Parkes observations for project P1054 semester 2026OCTS_07
records.description: With this proposal we ask time to continue our timing follow-up campaign of pulsars discovered with the MeerKAT telescope. Fiftytwo sources have been discovered in targeted observations of Fermi unidentified point sources, 2 towards Supernova Remnants, 27 in the Magellanic Clouds, 128 in Globular Clusters and 96 in a survey of the Galactic plane. A large fraction of the new discoveries are recycled pulsars (including a few relativistic systems, a pulsar with a planetary companion and several 'spider' binaries), or young pulsars. Timing observations have an essential role in exploiting the full potential of any pulsar discovery, allowing for the precise measurement of rotational, astrometric and orbital parameters which, in turn, give us powerful tools to improve our understanding of the physics in extreme environments as well as of the population of neutron stars as a whole. The UWL receiver of the Parkes telescope is a sensitive, versatile instrument that is allowing us to successfully time these new sources, in the bright-end of TRAPUM discoveries.

records.title: Long-term project observations for project P1321 semester 2026OCTS_19
records.description: The atomic interstellar medium shows tiny-scale optical depth fluctuations on the scale of 0.1~10,000 AU, whose origin and nature are poorly understood. The existence of this Tiny-Scale Atomic Structure (TSAS) has significant implications, potentially calling into question our fundamental understanding of heating, cooling and dynamical processes in the interstellar medium. Yet observations remain sparse. This long-term project plans to search for temporal variations in HI absorption spectra seen against background pulsars to characterise TSAS in the Milky Way interstellar medium (ISM). These observations constitute the largest number of sightlines and densest temporal sampling ever performed in a single experiment, and will test predictions that TSAS is the tail end of a turbulent cascade, constrain its minimum size scale (down to resolutions of ~0.05 AU) and potentially provide the first direct measurements of pressures in "large" TSAS features of > 1000 AU. We make use of the phase-resolved spectral line mode that we have recently implemented on Parkes, which has cut data rates and processing times by factors of ~1000 compared to past studies. This is an expansion of our pilot P1321 to a long term study.

records.title: Data and code from Modelling habitat suitability for multiple priority weed species to predict invasion hotspots for strategic management in complex landscapes
records.description: This dataset supports the manuscript "Modelling habitat suitability for multiple priority weed species to predict invasion hotspots for strategic management in complex landscapes". records.title: RV Investigator Voyage IN2026_T04 End of Voyage (EOV) Archive
records.description: This record describes the End of Voyage (EOV) data archive from the Marine National Facility (MNF) RV Investigator voyage IN2026_T04, titled "Collaborative Australian Postgraduate Sea Training Alliance Network (CAPSTAN) 06." The voyage took place between September 10, 2026 and September 23, 2026 (AEST), departing from Brisbane and returning to Lautoka. For further information please refer to the voyage documentation links. Instruments used and data collected include: Regular measurements: Acoustic Doppler Current Profiler (ADCP; 38, 75, 150 KHz ), Lowered ADCP (LADCP), Black Carbon sensor (Aethalometer), Greenhouse Gas Analysers (Picarro), Cloud Condensation Nuclei counter (CCN), Condensation Particle Counters (CPC), Disdrometer, Radon sensor, Micro Rain Radar (MRR), Mobility particle size spectrometer (MPSS), CTD, Hydrochemistry, Fisheries Echosounder (EK80), Multibeam Echosounder (EM712, EM124, EM2040), Sub-bottom Profiler (SBP29), GPS Positioning System, Doppler Velocity Log, Thermosalinographs (TSG), Fluorometer, Oxygen Optode, Infrared Sea Surface Temperature Autonomous Radiometer (ISAR), pCO2, Multiangle Absorption Photometer (MAAP), Ozone Sensor, Nephelometer, Atmospheric Temperature, Humidity, Pressure, Wind and Rain sensors, Photosynthetically Active Radiation (PAR) sensor, Precision Infrared Radiometer (PIR), Precision Spectral Pyranometer (PSP), Starboard and Portside Radiometers, Air Sampler, Ultra Short BaseLine Underwater Positioning System (USBL), Seabird detector (Jonathan), Environmental DNA Sampler (eDNA), Weather Radar, Expendable Bathythermographs (XBTs). Voyage-specific measurements: Kasten corer, Microplastics, Bongo Net, Core Argo floats, Deep Towed Camera (DTC), Sound Velocity Profile (SVP), Wildlife Observations (seabirds, cetaceans and seals). The archive for the IN2026_T04 EOV raw data is curated by the CSIRO National Collections and Marine Infrastructure (NCMI) Information and Data Centre (IDC) in Hobart, with a permanent archive at the CSIRO Data Access Portal (https://data.csiro.au/), providing access to voyage participants and processors of the data collected on the voyage. All voyage documentation is available electronically to MNF support via the local network. Applications to access voyage documentation by non-CSIRO participants can be made via HF-Data-Requests@csiro.au All processed data from this voyage are made publicly available through the MNF Data Trawler (in the related links)

records.title: GRDC mouse surveillance and modelling
records.description: The purpose of these projects is to predict house mouse abundance across grain growing regions to provide early warning of potential mouse plagues. This data has been collected by CSIRO and subcontractors; CSIRO has collated and cleaned this data into this joint dataset. House mice are surveyed in crops using three different methods: live-traps, active burrow counts and chew cards. Live trapping currently only occurs at three properties (two paddocks are monitored simultaneously). Active burrow counts and chew cards (i.e., rapid assessment) surveys are also conducted in each paddock simultaneously over one night. In all other sites, only rapid assessment surveys are conducted. In some instances, active burrow counts are not conducted as visibility of the burrows is too low due to dense crops or because of prolific soil cracks. In these cases, chew cards are still deployed, sometimes with higher effort. Each data type is provided as a separate CSV file, which contains a series of common variables denoting sites and times, as well as dataset-specific columns describing effort and results.

records.title: Parkes observations for project P1437 semester 2026OCTS_04
records.description: This project is focussed on four pulsars in the globular cluster NGC6441. PSRJ1750-3703A is a 111 millisecond pulsar in a very eccentric and long period orbit around a companion star, with a total mass of 2.18Msun. The analysis of the available data gives indication that PSRJ1750-3703A can be the lightest neutron star known so far, but a firm upper limit that confirms this statement cannot be placed yet, because all previous observations do not uniformly cover all orbital phases: in fact, they are clustered around the the apoastron. PSRJ1750-3703B is another eccentric binary pulsar, for which the detection of the periastron advance allowed a first estimation of the total mass of the binary, but non precisely enough to determine the nature of the companion. PSRJ1750-3703C and PSRJ1750-3703E are two isolated pulsars with spin periods of 26.6 and 251 milliseconds, respectively. PSRJ1750-3703C, PSRJ1750-3703E, and also PSRJ1750-3703A, are in the top 10% of the slowest pulsars in globular clusters, thus raising the question on how these pulsars can be formed in some globular clusters. The proposed observations aim to observe PSRJ1750-3703A uniformly along its orbital motion, thus allowing us to measure the pulsar mass, by measuring either the Einstein delay gamma parameter, or the orbital inclination by addressing the covariance between gamma and the time derivative of the projected semi-mayor axis of the pulsar. The proposed observations will also allow to reduce by a factor of two the uncertainty on the total mass of PSRJ1750-3703B, and to improve the rotational and astrometric parameters for PSRJ1750-3703C and PSRJ1750-3703E.

records.title: Parkes observations for project P1452 semester 2026OCTS_04
records.description: We propose a search for pulsars, with the expectation of finding primarily millisecond pulsars, in pulsar candidates found in MeerKAT and Very Large Array imaging surveys of the Galactic Bulge and Plane. The candidates were identified primarily as steep-spectrum, circularly- and/or linearly-polarized sources, and to a lesser degree by the level of radio variability observed. We have chosen 20 pulsar candidates to target in this proposal, eleven that may be Bulge members and nine others in the Plane. We request two half-hour pointings per source with the UWL receiver, plus 15 minutes of overhead (setup and slewing) per two sources, for a total of 22.5 hours of observing time.

records.title: Parkes observations for project P1365 semester 2026OCTS_10
records.description: Following the successful demonstration of a pilot first-pass (shallow) search of a small fraction of the sky, the second-pass processing has commenced for the SMART pulsar survey, which involves deep searches of 80-minute observations. Over the past year, this second-pass processing has led to the discovery of 21 new pulsars (including two millisecond pulsars), bringing the total number of SMART discoveries to 25 when combined with the first-pass results. These outcomes hint at the exciting promise of this first southern-sky pulsar survey in the frequency band of SKA-Low. All new pulsars require timing observations to determine their spin and astrometric parameters. Another important aspect of timing newly discovered pulsars is to identify specialised targets for further detailed follow-ups. Since the MWA is currently not available for routine pulsar observations, timing follow-ups rely on other telescopes. The Parkes Murriyang telescope, with identical sky coverage, high sensitivity, and wide frequency coverage, offers the best option for timing SMART discoveries. We have refined the proposed targets from our previous proposal by removing six pulsars that will have accumulated a full year of Parkes timing data by the end of the current semester, and by adding six newly discovered sources, five from typical pulsar searching methods, and one from image-based transient searching techniques, thereby maintaining a total sample of 11 pulsars. The data will also allow us to study pulse profiles, polarisation, and flux densities from ~100 MHz to 4 GHz. The analysis/results will be included in a forthcoming publication.

records.title: Parkes observations for project P1054 semester 2026OCTS_08
records.description: With this proposal we ask time to continue our timing follow-up campaign of pulsars discovered with the MeerKAT telescope. Fiftytwo sources have been discovered in targeted observations of Fermi unidentified point sources, 2 towards Supernova Remnants, 27 in the Magellanic Clouds, 128 in Globular Clusters and 96 in a survey of the Galactic plane. A large fraction of the new discoveries are recycled pulsars (including a few relativistic systems, a pulsar with a planetary companion and several 'spider' binaries), or young pulsars. Timing observations have an essential role in exploiting the full potential of any pulsar discovery, allowing for the precise measurement of rotational, astrometric and orbital parameters which, in turn, give us powerful tools to improve our understanding of the physics in extreme environments as well as of the population of neutron stars as a whole. The UWL receiver of the Parkes telescope is a sensitive, versatile instrument that is allowing us to successfully time these new sources, in the bright-end of TRAPUM discoveries.

records.title: Long-term project observations for project P1101 semester 2026OCTS_02
records.description: We propose a long-term project to monitor a very active repeater, FRB 20190520B, with Murriyang's UWL system. Our previous observations show that FRB 20190520B is not only among the most active FRBs that can be observed with Murriyang, but also shows extreme rotation measure (RM) and dispersion measure (DM) evolution, along with distinctive behavior at 3GHz frequency. This makes the UWL receiver uniquely suited for detailed studies and long-term monitoring of this repeating FRB. Through this program, we anticipate detecting a large sample of bursts from this FRB. In collaboration with FAST, we aim to investigate the time evolution of various properties of FRB 20190520B, enhance our understanding of polarisation across an extremely wide bandwidth with high sensitivity, and gain deeper insights into the local environment and emission mechanisms of FRBs.

records.title: Parkes observations for project P595 semester 2026OCTS_09
records.description: We propose to continue the PULSE@Parkes project in which high school students from Australia and around the World use the Parkes radio telescope in a remote observing model to observe and analyse pulsar data. The data from some PULSE@Parkes observations are used to support the space missions, other observations supplement the P456 Pulsar Timing Array project and the remainder were chosen in order to make a detailed analysis of pulsar timing irregularities and intermittency.

records.title: Parkes observations for project P1449 semester 2026OCTS_04
records.description: We propose the pilot survey of the southern high-Galactic-latitude sky with the Murriyang telescope using its state-of-the-art CryoPAF receiver. Owing to their large Galactic scale heights, millisecond pulsars (MSPs) are preferentially found at intermediate and high Galactic latitudes, where lower sky temperatures, reduced interstellar scattering, and smaller dispersion measures favor the discovery of nearby, bright, and exceptionally stable systems. Despite containing a large fraction of the known MSP population and nearly half of the pulsar timing array (PTA) pulsars visible from Murriyang, the southern high-latitude sky has never been surveyed with sensitivity comparable to that achieved in the Galactic-plane. Population synthesis simulations predict that a full CryoPAF survey of the southern high-latitude sky would discover approximately 320 normal pulsars and 100 MSPs, including many binary systems. As a first step towards this objective, we propose a pilot survey of 600 degree square (278deg<l<321deg, 15deg<b<30deg). CryoPAF capabilities of covering a large filed of view, broad bandwidth, and low system temperature, provides a survey speed ~20 times greater than that the legacy multibeam receiver. Using 27-minute integrations, the proposed observations will be substantially more sensitive than previous large-area high-latitude surveys. The proposed pilot survey is expected to discover ~10 pulsars while establishing the optimal observing strategy for a future large-scale survey. It will also provide an assessment of receiver performance, sensitivity, radio-frequency interference conditions, data quality, and candidate yields under realistic observing conditions. The survey offers the opportunity to discover PTA-quality MSPs, compact binary systems, and potentially some of the fastest-spinning neutron stars known.

records.title: Parkes observations for project P1428 semester 2026OCTS_05
records.description: Globular Clusters (GCs) are renowned to be the host of a wealth of radio pulsars, most of which are millisecond pulsars. The extreme stellar densities characterizing the central regions of GCs promote the formation of binary systems where neutron stars can be recycled, and the formation of pulsars and binaries with extreme or unconventional properties. GCs have therefore been prime targets for pulsar searching and, as of today, more than 360 pulsars have been found in 46 different clusters. The much larger computing power and much more modern algorithms available today have recently fostered the re-processing of archival Parkes GC data. This has led to the discovery of a few new pulsars, and several promising candidates. Here, we request 22 hours of observing time to re-observe a set of 10 GCs where 56 promising candidate pulsars have recently been found via reprocessing of archival Parkes data. The recently installed Ultra-Wide-band Low receiver, in combination with the modern APOLLO backend, will provide a sharp increase in sensitivity compared to the archival data. This will allow us to confirm or refute the candidates, and potentially even discover additional pulsars. Confirming at least one pulsar in a GC has a great scientific value, since it would allow us to know the approximate dispersion measure associated with cluster, greatly easing the search for additional pulsars in the cluster, and it would increase the total number of clusters known to host radio pulsars, contributing to our understanding of the population of pulsars in GCs.
