records.title: Parkes observations for project P1041 semester 2026OCTS_01
records.description: Omega Cen is the largest globular cluster in the Milky Way. It contains at least 18 known MSPs, and there are solid hints for the presence of an even larger pulsar population. We propose a regular monthly follow-up to refine the timing solutions of the five Parkes discoveries from 2020, and to find timing solutions for the 13 MeerKAT discoveries from 2023, in combination with six MeerKAT observations between 2021 and 2023, and future MeerKAT observations. These timing solutions should enable the detection of derivatives of the spin periods of these pulsars, allowing us to probe the dynamics of Omega Cen and the presence of a possible IMBH at its centre. Timing solutions will also enable the search for X-ray and gamma-ray pulsations in the multiple sources detected in this cluster. This study will allow us to better understand the populations of this globular cluster and its formation history. We request observations until 2030, when we expect to have measurements of the second period derivative of the five brighter discoveries, and first period derivative measurements for the later discoveries. These observations will also contribute to the study of eclipsing binaries, and may include future discoveries from pending searches in MeerKAT data.

records.title: Parkes observations for project P1041 semester 2026OCTS_02
records.description: Omega Cen is the largest globular cluster in the Milky Way. It contains at least 18 known MSPs, and there are solid hints for the presence of an even larger pulsar population. We propose a regular monthly follow-up to refine the timing solutions of the five Parkes discoveries from 2020, and to find timing solutions for the 13 MeerKAT discoveries from 2023, in combination with six MeerKAT observations between 2021 and 2023, and future MeerKAT observations. These timing solutions should enable the detection of derivatives of the spin periods of these pulsars, allowing us to probe the dynamics of Omega Cen and the presence of a possible IMBH at its centre. Timing solutions will also enable the search for X-ray and gamma-ray pulsations in the multiple sources detected in this cluster. This study will allow us to better understand the populations of this globular cluster and its formation history. We request observations until 2030, when we expect to have measurements of the second period derivative of the five brighter discoveries, and first period derivative measurements for the later discoveries. These observations will also contribute to the study of eclipsing binaries, and may include future discoveries from pending searches in MeerKAT data.

records.title: Parkes observations for project P1379 semester 2026OCTS_02
records.description: We propose a simultaneous joint observation campaign using the Parkes radio telescope and the EP satellite to observation five magnetars with known radio emission. Under simultaneous observations, we aim to investigate the correlation between their radio and X-ray emissions, including pulse profiles, flux intensity, polarization evolution, correlated multi-wavelength behavior and timing behavior.

records.title: Parkes observations for project P1444 semester 2026OCTS_08
records.description: Central Compact Objects (CCOs) have long been considered a class of X-ray neutron stars lacking multi-wavelength counterparts. However, the recent discovery of radio pulsations from a CCO challenges this picture, suggesting that at least some members of this class can produce coherent radio emission. Nevertheless, whether CCOs are related to ordinary radio pulsars or represent buried magnetars remains unclear. We propose deep radio searches of southern CCOs using the Parkes UWL receiver to identify additional radio-emitting members. The wide bandwidth enables a sensitive search for faint pulsations while allowing a frequency-dependent assessment of detectability. The discovery of even one additional radio CCO would immediately establish that radio-emitting CCOs constitute a hidden population, offering key constraints on their unusual magnetic-field configuration and evolution. This survey will therefore provide a critical test of the origin of CCOs and their place within the neutron-star population.

records.title: Long-term project observations for project P885 semester 2026OCTS_03
records.description: We propose a modest program to continue monitoring 4 of the 6 known radio magnetars in order to achieve three primary science goals. The first is to characterise magnetar outbursts over long timescales, for which tracking their rotational, flux density, and polarisation properties provide a clear view of the impulse response of their magnetic fields. Second, understanding the links between magnetars the mysterious fast radio burst phenomenon through the discovery of rare emission and propagation effects, shared spectro-temporal phenomenology, and connections to high-energy (X-ray/gamma-ray) phenomena. Lastly, our continued monitoring has enormous benefit to the wider magnetar community, providing rapid alerts to changes in activity, adding context to unusual behaviour detected by high-energy observations, and a host of supplementary science through the teams extensive collaborative networks. The project and its precursors have been running since 2007 and have contributed to 22 publications since then. This is the first submission since the project was converted to long-term status.

records.title: Parkes observations for project P630 semester 2011OCTS_21
records.description: We propose to carry out the most ambitious and comprehensive all-sky survey for pulsars and transient sources to date. Using the 20cm multibeam and a new digital filterbank array this survey will create a petabyte digital record of the sky that can be data mined in the future and used to search for relativistic binary and millisecond pulsars, RRATs, and extragalactic radio bursts. The survey should discover 100s of new millisecond and normal pulsars and help define the lower limit to pulsar periods, test theories of relativistic gravity, find transients and provide pulsars for gravitational wave detection.

records.title: IN2026_V03 Southern Ocean SOTS Bathymetry 5m - 210m Multi-resolution AusSeabed products
records.description: IN2026_V03 SOTS: Southern Ocean Time Series Scientific Objectives The primary objective is to first deploy a new set of SOTS moorings (SOFS-15 and SAZ-28) and then recover the existing SOTS moorings (SAZ-27). Each of the SOTS moorings deliver to specific aspects of the atmosphere-ocean exchanges: • the SAZ sediment trap mooring collects samples to quantify the transfer of carbon and other nutrients to the ocean interior by sinking particles and investigate their ecological controls. • the Southern Ocean Flux Station (SOFS) mooring measures meteorological and ocean properties important to air-sea exchanges, ocean stratification, waves, currents and biological productivity and ecosystem structure. Water samples are collected for more detailed nutrient and plankton investigations after recovery. Ancillary work will obtain supporting information on atmospheric and oceanographic conditions using CTD casts, and underway measurements. Deploy SOFS-15 meteorology/biogeochemistry mooring Deploy SAZ-28 sediment trap mooring Recover SAZ-27 sediment trap mooring CTD sampling (2 cast to 4550m, 2 to 600m) at the SOTS site, including collecting samples for nutrients, oxygen, dissolved inorganic carbon, alkalinity, and eDNA analyses Ship meteorological observations at SOFS buoys for comparisons Deployment of 2 x Argo Floats (1 at the nominal SOTS site, and one closer to Tasmania, in water 2000m deep, on return transit). Underway air and water sampling and sensor measurements, including bio-optics and bioacoustics CPR and Triaxus This dataset is published with the permission of CSIRO. Not to be used for navigational purposes. The dataset contains bathymetry grids of 5m to 210m resolution of the Southern Ocean area produced from the processed EM124, EM712 and EM2040MK2 bathymetry data.

records.title: IN2024_V03 Southeast Australia Bathymetry 5m - 210m Multi-resolution AusSeabed products
records.description: This layer group describes multibeam echosounder data collected on RV Investigator voyage IN2024_V03 titled "Untangling the causes of change over 25 years in the southeast marine ecosystem - Voyage 2". The voyage took place between May 1 and May 31, 2024, departing from Hobart (TAS) and arriving in Sydney (NSW). The purpose of this voyage was to repeat previous surveys to document changes and establish a new biological and environmental baseline to help answer three broad questions: 1. How and why have fish assemblages and species abundances changed in the southeast ecosystem, and can the causes be mitigated? 2. How this affects multiple-use management of the region, particularly conservation management and activity from fisheries, oil & gas, and renewable energy sectors? 3. What are the implications for marine spatial planning and adaptive management in the sectors that use the marine ecosystem? It is also testing new monitoring techniques: a. To measure fish presence and abundance using eDNA two sampling approaches, and how they compare to conventional sampling approaches. b. To detect and count seabirds using deck mounted video camera. IN2024_V03 is the second of four monitoring surveys planned to help answer the above questions. This dataset is published with the permission of CSIRO. Not to be used for navigational purposes. The dataset contains bathymetry grids of 5m to 210m resolution of Southeast Australia produced from the processed EM122 and EM710 bathymetry data.

records.title: Parkes observations for project P1420 semester 2026OCTS_04
records.description: We propose a transition from a Pilot to the full Murriyang CryoPAF Pulsar Survey of the Southern Galactic Plane (CPS-LowLat). The revolutionary CryoPAF receiver delivers the highest pulsar survey speed in the Southern Hemisphere, exceeding L-band capability of MeerKAT by ~2x, with a sufficiently low data rate to enable archiving and reprocessing essential to maximizing survey yields. Population synthesis predicts ~300 new pulsars in the full CPS-LowLat. New discoveries from CPS-LowLat will enable strong-field tests of General Relativity, equation-of-state constraints from massive neutron stars, more accurate modeling of the neutron star merger rate, and probes of exotic stellar-evolution pathways and of the ionised interstellar medium. Five pointings for the CPS-LowLat have been observed in 2026APRS since April 29, and preliminary, quick-look processing of the first three pointings has already yielded three excellent candidate pulsar discoveries. Re-detections of known pulsars suggests that we are achieving the expected end-to-end survey sensitivity. We propose to use 2026OCTS to transition our primary processing to CSIRO HPC resources, while continuing the survey, in preparation for commencement of the full CPS-LowLat in 2027APRS with a higher observation cadence. Up to ~50 pulsars are predicted from the 30 deg^2 2026OCTS survey region, including 3-6 millisecond pulsars, representing in itself an impressive yield and associated scientific promise. 2.5-hr pointings are proposed to provide the requisite transformational pulsar detection rate, while maintaining sensitivity across a wide range of binary orbital periods, including ultra-compact systems. A frequency range of 1.3-1.85 GHz will mitigate dispersion smearing and scattering.

records.title: Parkes observations for project PX135 semester 2026OCTS_01
records.description: Pulsar data from Parkes (Murriyang) Target of Opportunity (ToO) observations

records.title: Parkes observations for project P595 semester 2026OCTS_10
records.description: We propose to continue the PULSE@Parkes project in which high school students from Australia and around the World use the Parkes radio telescope in a remote observing model to observe and analyse pulsar data. The data from some PULSE@Parkes observations are used to support the space missions, other observations supplement the P456 Pulsar Timing Array project and the remainder were chosen in order to make a detailed analysis of pulsar timing irregularities and intermittency.

records.title: Parkes observations for project P1449 semester 2026OCTS_05
records.description: We propose the pilot survey of the southern high-Galactic-latitude sky with the Murriyang telescope using its state-of-the-art CryoPAF receiver. Owing to their large Galactic scale heights, millisecond pulsars (MSPs) are preferentially found at intermediate and high Galactic latitudes, where lower sky temperatures, reduced interstellar scattering, and smaller dispersion measures favor the discovery of nearby, bright, and exceptionally stable systems. Despite containing a large fraction of the known MSP population and nearly half of the pulsar timing array (PTA) pulsars visible from Murriyang, the southern high-latitude sky has never been surveyed with sensitivity comparable to that achieved in the Galactic-plane. Population synthesis simulations predict that a full CryoPAF survey of the southern high-latitude sky would discover approximately 320 normal pulsars and 100 MSPs, including many binary systems. As a first step towards this objective, we propose a pilot survey of 600 degree square (278deg<l<321deg, 15deg<b<30deg). CryoPAF capabilities of covering a large filed of view, broad bandwidth, and low system temperature, provides a survey speed ~20 times greater than that the legacy multibeam receiver. Using 27-minute integrations, the proposed observations will be substantially more sensitive than previous large-area high-latitude surveys. The proposed pilot survey is expected to discover ~10 pulsars while establishing the optimal observing strategy for a future large-scale survey. It will also provide an assessment of receiver performance, sensitivity, radio-frequency interference conditions, data quality, and candidate yields under realistic observing conditions. The survey offers the opportunity to discover PTA-quality MSPs, compact binary systems, and potentially some of the fastest-spinning neutron stars known.

records.title: Ground Validation of Hyperspectral Earth Observation Imagery - Rocklea Dome and Tambourah - Supporting Data
records.description: Optical Earth observation plays a critical role in monitoring and achieving many of the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals. For example, multi- and hyperspectral satellite imagery aid spatially contiguous characterisation of soils and minerals, important for the agriculture and mining industries, and, therefore, addressing SDG 2 (Zero Hunger) and SDG 9 (Industry, Innovation and Infrastructure). Similarly, the optical satellite imagery enables land cover classification and characterisation of vegetation, supporting SDG 15 (Life on Land). The advent of the latest hyperspectral satellite sensors enables the characterisation of minerals and vegetation at unprecedented detail from the local to continental-scale. The rapidly increasing availability of optical satellite imagery offers new opportunities towards an accurate inventory of natural resources. In the frame of the IEEE GRSS Geoscience Spaceborne Imaging Spectroscopy (GSIS) working group, ground validation campaigns were conducted at two sites in Western Australia (WA): Rocklea Dome (Hamersley Basin) and Tambourah (Eastern Pilbara Craton). The aim was to collect and make publicly available a suite of field and lab geoscience data that could be used by researchers and industry to evaluate optical remotely sensed imagery for geological mapping, mineral characterisation and data integration. Data presented in this report include: 1) hyperspectral satellite-derived mineral maps, 2) field spectrometer reflectance spectra (FieldSpec4 and Agilent 4300) collected along transects planned with previously generated mineral maps, 3) whole rock geochemistry, quantitative x-ray diffractometry (QXRD) and lab FTIR measurements collected from 40 rock samples representative of major igneous and metamorphic bedrocks. This data collection comprises all collected data, selected satellite hyperspectral imagery products and a GIS data base.

records.title: CASDA Virtual Observatory Tools v2.0
records.description: CASDA VO Tools is a highly customizable Java web application developed to serve astronomy data via Virtual Observatory protocols. Currently Table Access (TAP), Simple Cone Search (SCS), Simple Spectral Access (SSA), Simple Image Access v1 (SIA1), Simple Image Access v2 (SIA2) and Datalink protocols are supported. The application is designed to be reusable both within CSIRO and by other data centres. As a result it is fully configurable either via configuration files or through a user interface. CASDA VO Tools was developed as a part of the CSIRO Australian Square Kilometre Array Pathfinder Data Archive (CASDA) project. CASDA is a core component in the Australian Square Kilometre Array Pathfinder (ASKAP) system. It is essentially the primary point for storing, managing, sharing and using processed ASKAP data products.

records.title: Rosetta GBR: A shiny app for CCIP BR-04 - Analysing RJFMP Field Data
records.description: A shiny app exploring results from the COTS Control Innovation Program project CCIP BR-04: Analysing RJFMP Summer Field Data. This app allows the user to explore posterior results of COTS and coral cover estimates from one monitoring tool to another, as well as explore uncertainty around monitoring tools. This work accompanies the report submitted to the Great Barrier Reef Foundation.

records.title: Hydrodynamic and Vegetation Observations in Mangroves at Godwin Beach, QLD, 2025
records.description: This dataset compiles field observations and processed data supporting a study on wave attenuation by mangroves at Godwin Beach, QLD, from January to April 2025. The data consists of time series of pressure, velocity, and sea surface elevation both within the mangroves and offshore; measurements of vegetation morphology; and ground elevations. The data captures Tropical Cyclone (TC) Alfred, which travelled 10 km north of Godwin Beach on 8 March 2025. Processed hydrodynamic variables include time series of water depths, wave heights, wave periods, and wave attenuation parameters. Processed vegetation parameters include diameter at breast height, stem density, root height, root density, submerged volume fraction, and density multiplied by projected area.

records.title: Parkes observations for project P595 semester 2026OCTS_11
records.description: We propose to continue the PULSE@Parkes project in which high school students from Australia and around the World use the Parkes radio telescope in a remote observing model to observe and analyse pulsar data. The data from some PULSE@Parkes observations are used to support the space missions, other observations supplement the P456 Pulsar Timing Array project and the remainder were chosen in order to make a detailed analysis of pulsar timing irregularities and intermittency.

records.title: Parkes observations for project P1365 semester 2026OCTS_15
records.description: Following the successful demonstration of a pilot first-pass (shallow) search of a small fraction of the sky, the second-pass processing has commenced for the SMART pulsar survey, which involves deep searches of 80-minute observations. Over the past year, this second-pass processing has led to the discovery of 21 new pulsars (including two millisecond pulsars), bringing the total number of SMART discoveries to 25 when combined with the first-pass results. These outcomes hint at the exciting promise of this first southern-sky pulsar survey in the frequency band of SKA-Low. All new pulsars require timing observations to determine their spin and astrometric parameters. Another important aspect of timing newly discovered pulsars is to identify specialised targets for further detailed follow-ups. Since the MWA is currently not available for routine pulsar observations, timing follow-ups rely on other telescopes. The Parkes Murriyang telescope, with identical sky coverage, high sensitivity, and wide frequency coverage, offers the best option for timing SMART discoveries. We have refined the proposed targets from our previous proposal by removing six pulsars that will have accumulated a full year of Parkes timing data by the end of the current semester, and by adding six newly discovered sources, five from typical pulsar searching methods, and one from image-based transient searching techniques, thereby maintaining a total sample of 11 pulsars. The data will also allow us to study pulse profiles, polarisation, and flux densities from ~100 MHz to 4 GHz. The analysis/results will be included in a forthcoming publication.

records.title: Parkes observations for project P1406 semester 2026OCTS_05
records.description: NGC 362 is a post-core-collapse southern globular cluster (GC) where 12 pulsars have recently been discovered. The pulsar population is very diverse, containing extremely fast-spinning, mildly recycled and slow pulsars, the vast majority of which (11 out of 12) are part of binary systems with very different orbital periods and eccentricities. One of these pulsars, NGC 362B, is a millisecond pulsar in an eccentric binary system, for which the relativistic rate of advance of periastron is already measured to high precision. We propose continued timing observations of NGC 362B aimed at detecting a second post-Keplerian parameter, the Einstein delay. This, in combination with the advance of periastron, will enable precise measurements of the component masses of the system, improving our statistics of precisely measured neutron star masses. The same observations will be used to keep timing all the other pulsars in the clusters, as well as to search for new ones.

records.title: Parkes observations for project P1450 semester 2026OCTS_01
records.description: We propose the most sensitive uniform pulsar survey of the Large Magellanic Cloud (LMC) using the CryoPAF receiver on Murriyang. The LMC provides a unique opportunity to study neutron-star populations in an external, low-metallicity galaxy with a well-constrained distance. Despite more than four decades of searches, only 44 radio pulsars are currently known in the LMC, and no millisecond pulsars (MSPs) or binary radio pulsars have yet been discovered. We will survey the central 78 squared degrees of the LMC using 50 CryoPAF pointings with 4.8-hour integrations, covering the entire region that contains all known LMC pulsars and the galaxy's main HI distribution. The combination of CryoPAF's large field of view, wide bandwidth, and high sensitivity will enable the most sensitive wide-area pulsar survey of the LMC to date. It will probe substantially deeper into the pulsar luminosity function than previous surveys. Population-synthesis simulations predict the detection of ~90 pulsars, including about 50 new discoveries, which would double the known LMC pulsar population. The survey also has the potential to discover the first MSPs and binary pulsars in this galaxy. Such discoveries would provide the first statistically meaningful census of neutron stars in an external galaxy, constrain compact-object formation and evolution in a low-metallicity environment, and open new opportunities for studies of gravitational-wave astrophysics. This survey will establish the most complete survey of the LMC pulsar population and provide a legacy dataset for future pulsar and neutron-star studies.

records.title: Parkes observations for project P1054 semester 2026OCTS_09
records.description: With this proposal we ask time to continue our timing follow-up campaign of pulsars discovered with the MeerKAT telescope. Fiftytwo sources have been discovered in targeted observations of Fermi unidentified point sources, 2 towards Supernova Remnants, 27 in the Magellanic Clouds, 128 in Globular Clusters and 96 in a survey of the Galactic plane. A large fraction of the new discoveries are recycled pulsars (including a few relativistic systems, a pulsar with a planetary companion and several 'spider' binaries), or young pulsars. Timing observations have an essential role in exploiting the full potential of any pulsar discovery, allowing for the precise measurement of rotational, astrometric and orbital parameters which, in turn, give us powerful tools to improve our understanding of the physics in extreme environments as well as of the population of neutron stars as a whole. The UWL receiver of the Parkes telescope is a sensitive, versatile instrument that is allowing us to successfully time these new sources, in the bright-end of TRAPUM discoveries.

records.title: National ecosystem states template for the Nature Repair Market: Shrublands. A data collection for the Ecological Knowledge System
records.description: This collection contains information that describes the national ecosystem states template for shrublands used in the Ecological Knowledge System (EKS) for the Nature Repair Market (the market). The EKS is a partnership between CSIRO and the Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water (DCCEEW) to establish a transparent and authoritative source of information, biodiversity assessment and forecast capability for the market. The EKS team has collaborated with the Terrestrial Ecosystems Research Network (TERN) funded NatureStates project (see Related links) to develop a set of generalised ecosystem states templates. The three templates – covering forests and woodlands, shrublands, and grasslands – capture the major structural variation across Australian terrestrial ecosystems (excluding freshwater herbaceous wetlands, salt lakes, in-channel aquatic ecosystems and tidally influenced coastal ecosystems). The templates are intended to function as a flexible and scalable foundation for developing regionally specific state-and-transition models (STMs) for the EKS. Prober et al. (2026) and Richards et al. (2026). (see Related links) describe how the templates can be used to create state-and-transition models. The templates also support consistency and comparability across Nature Repair Market methods while allowing adaptation to reflect regional ecological variation, method-specific objectives, and differing restoration pathways. See the Related links for links to the data collections for the other two ecosystem states templates. The ecosystem states templates build on established frameworks including the Australian Ecosystem Models (AusEcoModels) Framework, the Vegetation Assets, States and Transitions (VAST) framework, and the Society for Ecological Restoration (SER) five-star recovery wheel. Each ecosystem state in the shrublands template is described using a two-layer approach that integrates the attributes of the defining shrub layer and the complementary tree/ground layers, resulting in a matrix of 16 core ecosystem states ranging from Close to reference to Collapsed/transformer. These core states are supplemented by intensive land-use states including cropping, intensively managed exotic pastures, cultivated woody systems and artificial surfaces and infrastructure. Each state is associated with indicative ecosystem condition ranges based on compositional similarity to a high-integrity reference state providing a consistent basis for assigning ecosystem condition scores to ecosystem states. This data collection is based on research created under the Project 'An Ecological Knowledge System for the Nature Repair Market scheme', which was funded by DCCEEW. The Commonwealth owns the intellectual property rights in any material developed while carrying out the Project. Copyright is retained by CSIRO (2026). To cite the template booklet, please use the citation specified in the report.

records.title: Hyperspectral techniques for gold exploration in the historical Bellchambers mining area, WA
records.description: This study represents a collaborative characterisation investigation between Venus Metals Corporation Ltd. and CSIRO Mineral Resources, focused on understanding the distribution of major minerals and the association with Au anomalies/mineralisation in both regolith and bedrock within the Bellchambers–Range View corridor of the Sandstone Greenstone Belt, Western Australia.

records.title: Maia XRF mapping at the Bellchambers gold deposit, WA
records.description: This project between CSIRO Mineral Resources and Venus Metals Corporation Ltd aimed to utilise the Maia XRF Mapper to inform on gold occurrences at the Bellchambers deposit. This was a pilot project using four samples from diamond drill hole 25BDD2 from the 2025 drilling campaign and may not fully represent the range of mineralisation types within the prospect or the region.

records.title: National Biodiversity Assessment System (NBAS) v2.1.1. A data collection for the Ecological Knowledge System
records.description: This collection contains derived datasets used in the National Biodiversity Assessment System (NBAS) v2.1.1, developed as part of the Ecological Knowledge System (EKS). The EKS is a partnership between CSIRO and the Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water (DCCEEW) to establish a transparent and authoritative source of information, biodiversity assessment and forecast capability for the Nature Repair Market. The NBAS is a software and data package that provides a nationally consistent approach to assessing a project site’s current contribution to conserving biodiversity and forecasting the biodiversity benefits expected to result from nature repair projects. This collection comprises information about the ecosystem typology used in the NBAS v2.1.1. It contains: •Ecosystem type and ecosystem significance table (.csv): a tab-delimited file (Ecosystem_Types_and_Significance_Scores.csv) that provides the unique ecosystem type ID number, its ecosystem significance score, and the identifying number and name of the MVG and the CMZ from which each ecosystem type is derived. •Ecosystem type raster (.tif): a raster (Ecosystem_Types_Oct2026.tif) that denotes the location and boundaries of the ecosystem types as defined in NBAS (i.e. the intersections between the National Vegetation Information System (NVIS) Major Vegetation Groups (MVGs) and Conservation Management Zones (CMZs)). Ecosystem types are represented by unique numeric identifiers. •Ecosystem type raster visualisation files (.qml, .txt): style and colour map files (QGIS_Style_File_EcosystemTypesOct2026.qml and QGIS_ColourMap_Ecosystem_Types.txt) containing the categorical colour assignments used to visualise the ecosystem types within the ecosystem type raster, enabling the reproduction of the maps as presented in The Ecological Knowledge System (EKS) for the Nature Repair Market: Technical Report Version 2 (see Related Links). The NBAS forecasts the change in biodiversity persistence expected to result from a Nature Repair Market project, where biodiversity persistence reflects the contribution that an area makes to the long-term nationwide persistence of the native species associated with its ecosystem type. Assessments are undertaken within a nationally consistent ecosystem typology that defines distinct ecosystem types across Australia. The change in biodiversity persistence attributable to a project is quantified as a function of the change in ecosystem condition expected within the project area, the contribution of the project to enhancing connectivity across the broader landscape, and the national-scale significance of the ecosystem type. The NBAS can be accessed via the PLANR tool (https://planr.gov.au/). This collection is based on research created under the Project "An Ecological Knowledge System for the Nature Repair Market", which was funded by DCCEEW. The Commonwealth owns the intellectual property rights in any material developed while carrying out the Project. Copyright is retained by CSIRO (2026).

records.title: HCAS 3.4 (1988-2025) base model estimate of Habitat Condition (90m grid), annual time-series and 95% confidence intervals for continental Australia
records.description: *** Note: 95% Confidence Intervals for selected epochs will be added to this data collection in the second release *** The HCAS v3.4 data collection spans 38 years, from 1988 to 2025, and comprises updated Habitat Condition estimates together with selected supporting, uncertainty and data-quality datasets. Details are provided in the Product Guide (see related links). In summary, the collection includes: • a 90 m gridded long-term Habitat Condition epoch (base model) for 1988–2025, in Australian Albers projection (EPSG:3577, GDA94), derived using 38-year averages of 14 remotely sensed ecosystem characteristics and representing relative ecosystem condition for predominantly terrestrial biodiversity • 36 short-term Habitat Condition epochs, ending annually from 1990 to 2025, derived from 3-year rolling averages of the same 14 remotely sensed ecosystem characteristics; the end year of each 3-year epoch is used as its epoch year • model-based uncertainty estimates of Habitat Condition for the long-term epoch and selected 3-year epochs, including lower and upper 95% confidence limits and confidence interval width derived using bootstrap resampling of reference ecosystem data • 14 remotely sensed ecosystem characteristics used as inputs to Habitat Condition estimation, comprising five spectral indices derived from Landsat GeoMedian data, three measures of spectral variability derived from GeoMAD data, and six fractional-cover characteristics representing photosynthetic vegetation, non-photosynthetic vegetation and bare soil. Annual datasets and the corresponding long-term and 3-year epoch datasets used in HCAS v3.4. • annual Red-Green-Blue (RGB) composite images provided as supporting visualisation products, comprising true-colour Landsat composites and fractional cover composites to assist visual interpretation and comparison of spatial and temporal patterns in the remotely sensed data • remote sensing data-quality datasets, including the Geoscience Australia annual source-observation count, annual fractional cover and GeoMedian/GeoMAD no-data flags, and epoch-level summed frequency (SNA) and proportion (PNA) of missing data among the 14 remotely sensed ecosystem characteristics; these datasets support identification of locations and epochs where missing source data required subsequent NA-data filling • analysis and data-collection extent masks, including masks used to define or constrain processing and the spatial extent of published outputs. Masks are included to support product transparency, including where they have not changed from earlier HCAS versions. Product Guide: Williams KJ / Giljohann KM, Valavi R, Levick SR, Lehmann EA, Collings S, Johnson S, Liu N, Munroe SEM, Paget M, Lyon P, Malley C, Tetreault-Campbell S and Ferrier S (2026) Habitat Condition Assessment System (HCAS) version 3.4: Guide to the 90-metre data collection. Technical report EP2026-4396, Edition 1, October 2026. CSIRO, Canberra, Australia. Landing page: https://publications.csiro.au/publications/publication/PIcsiro:EP2026-4396

records.title: National ecosystem states template for the Nature Repair Market: Grasslands. A data collection for the Ecological Knowledge System
records.description: This collection contains information that describes the national ecosystem states template for grasslands used in the Ecological Knowledge System (EKS) for the Nature Repair Market (the market). The EKS is a partnership between CSIRO and the Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water (DCCEEW) to establish a transparent and authoritative source of information, biodiversity assessment and forecast capability for the market. The comprehensive summary report for the grasslands ecosystem states template is currently available as a draft and the final booklet will be published in October 2026. The EKS team has collaborated with the Terrestrial Ecosystems Research Network (TERN) funded NatureStates project (see Related links) to develop a set of generalised ecosystem states templates. The three templates – covering forests and woodlands, shrublands, and grasslands – capture the major structural variation across Australian terrestrial ecosystems (excluding freshwater herbaceous wetlands, salt lakes, in-channel aquatic ecosystems and tidally influenced coastal ecosystems). The templates are intended to function as a flexible and scalable foundation for developing regionally specific state-and-transition models (STMs) for the EKS. Prober et al. (2026) and Richards et al. (2026). (see Related links) describe how the templates can be used to create state-and-transition models. The templates also support consistency and comparability across Nature Repair Market methods while allowing adaptation to reflect regional ecological variation, method-specific objectives, and differing restoration pathways. See the Related links for links to the data collections for the other two ecosystem states templates. The ecosystem states templates build on established frameworks including the Australian Ecosystem Models (AusEcoModels) Framework, the Vegetation Assets, States and Transitions (VAST) framework, and the Society for Ecological Restoration (SER) five-star recovery wheel. Each ecosystem state in the grasslands template is described using a two-layer approach that integrates the attributes of the defining ground layer and the complementary tree/shrub layers, resulting in a matrix of 16 core ecosystem states ranging from Close to reference to Collapsed/transformer. These core states are supplemented by intensive land-use states including cropping, intensively managed exotic pastures, cultivated woody systems and artificial surfaces and infrastructure. Each state is associated with indicative ecosystem condition ranges based on compositional similarity to a high-integrity reference state providing a consistent basis for assigning ecosystem condition scores to ecosystem states. This data collection is based on research created under the Project 'An Ecological Knowledge System for the Nature Repair Market scheme', which was funded by DCCEEW. The Commonwealth owns the intellectual property rights in any material developed while carrying out the Project. Copyright is retained by CSIRO (2026). To cite the template booklet, please use the citation specified in the report.

records.title: Parkes observations for project P1365 semester 2026OCTS_16
records.description: Following the successful demonstration of a pilot first-pass (shallow) search of a small fraction of the sky, the second-pass processing has commenced for the SMART pulsar survey, which involves deep searches of 80-minute observations. Over the past year, this second-pass processing has led to the discovery of 21 new pulsars (including two millisecond pulsars), bringing the total number of SMART discoveries to 25 when combined with the first-pass results. These outcomes hint at the exciting promise of this first southern-sky pulsar survey in the frequency band of SKA-Low. All new pulsars require timing observations to determine their spin and astrometric parameters. Another important aspect of timing newly discovered pulsars is to identify specialised targets for further detailed follow-ups. Since the MWA is currently not available for routine pulsar observations, timing follow-ups rely on other telescopes. The Parkes Murriyang telescope, with identical sky coverage, high sensitivity, and wide frequency coverage, offers the best option for timing SMART discoveries. We have refined the proposed targets from our previous proposal by removing six pulsars that will have accumulated a full year of Parkes timing data by the end of the current semester, and by adding six newly discovered sources, five from typical pulsar searching methods, and one from image-based transient searching techniques, thereby maintaining a total sample of 11 pulsars. The data will also allow us to study pulse profiles, polarisation, and flux densities from ~100 MHz to 4 GHz. The analysis/results will be included in a forthcoming publication.

records.title: Parkes observations for project P1054 semester 2026OCTS_10
records.description: With this proposal we ask time to continue our timing follow-up campaign of pulsars discovered with the MeerKAT telescope. Fiftytwo sources have been discovered in targeted observations of Fermi unidentified point sources, 2 towards Supernova Remnants, 27 in the Magellanic Clouds, 128 in Globular Clusters and 96 in a survey of the Galactic plane. A large fraction of the new discoveries are recycled pulsars (including a few relativistic systems, a pulsar with a planetary companion and several 'spider' binaries), or young pulsars. Timing observations have an essential role in exploiting the full potential of any pulsar discovery, allowing for the precise measurement of rotational, astrometric and orbital parameters which, in turn, give us powerful tools to improve our understanding of the physics in extreme environments as well as of the population of neutron stars as a whole. The UWL receiver of the Parkes telescope is a sensitive, versatile instrument that is allowing us to successfully time these new sources, in the bright-end of TRAPUM discoveries.

records.title: Long-term project observations for project P1205 semester 2026OCTS_07
records.description: We propose to carry out a deep Galactic Bulge pulsar survey (GBps), covering the core of the Bulge region using the new cryoPAF system on Murriyang, the Parkes radio telescope. Such a deep survey is expected to discover a population of millisecond pulsars in the Galactic Bulge and reveal their distribution and gamma-ray emissions. With these, we will lead pioneering studies on the origin of gamma-ray emission in the Galactic Bulge, a longstanding mystery in modern astronomy. The outcome of this project will significantly advance our knowledge of the formation and evolution of millisecond pulsars in the Galactic Bulge, the origin and properties of high-energy emissions, and the nature of dark matter annihilation in the Galactic Centre. A total of 200 observations with the cryoPAF is required to cover a 400 square degree region (|gl|<10 deg, |gb|<10 deg). The survey is expected to be carried out over four semesters, from April 2026 to October 2027.

records.title: Parkes observations for project P1183 semester 2026OCTS_03
records.description: FRB 20220529 is the only repeating FRB known to exhibit rotation-measure (RM) flares (sudden, large-amplitude RM excursions lasting ~two weeks). Two such flares have now been detected: the first in December 2023 (only the decay captured) and the second in August--September 2025, ~19 months later. The second flare was observed with full temporal coverage, revealing a rise and decay of ~14 days each, an RM sign opposite to the first flare, and a prolonged post-flare quiescence. These two events alone cannot establish whether the recurrence is strictly periodic or stochastic. If periodic, the third flare is expected around March - April 2027, which is squarely within the 2026OCTS semester. Detecting a third flare with a similar waiting time would provide a "smoking gun" for a binary origin; a non-detection throughout the semester would rule out strict periodicity. Either outcome is decisive. We propose to continue monitoring FRB 20220529 with the Parkes UWL receiver at one session per fortnight throughout 2026OCTS.

records.title: National Biodiversity Assessment System (NBAS) v2.1.1. A standalone codebase for the Ecological Knowledge System
records.description: This collection links to a GitHub repository housing a local standalone version of the National Biodiversity Assessment System (NBAS) used in PLANR (https://planr.gov.au/). It enables users to run NBAS independently of the PLANR website. The NBAS was developed as part of the Ecological Knowledge System (EKS). The EKS is a partnership between the Commonwealth Scientific and Industrial Research Organisation (CSIRO) and the Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water (DCCEEW) to establish a transparent and authoritative source of information, biodiversity assessment and forecast capability for the Nature Repair Market. The NBAS is a software and data package that provides a nationally consistent approach to assessing an area’s current contribution to biodiversity and forecasting the expected contribution to biodiversity following successful implementation of a given project within the Nature Repair Market. The standalone NBAS (version 2.1.1) produces the following metrics: • Contribution to landscape connectivity scores • Ecosystem significance scores • Contribution to biodiversity persistence scores The standalone version of NBAS is for advanced users to run assessments on a local computer, at scale, or as part of automated workflows. It assumes familiarity with command-line tools, Docker, and basic data handling. If you're only assessing a small number of locations, or prefer a guided interface, we recommend using PLANR. The NBAS GitHub repository was developed and is maintained by Haizea Analytics Pty Ltd. Released under a MIT License. Copyright (c) 2025 CSIRO, DCCEEW, ANU, Haizea Analytics. Disclaimer Results from this standalone desktop version of NBAS differ slightly from the NBAS service in PLANR due to slight differences in how areas are clipped from the full datasets. Biodiversity benefit scores will be reviewed by the Clean Energy Regulator as part of the project registration process. The NBAS code provides an estimate of biodiversity benefit only. We do not warrant the accuracy or completeness of any information contained in or calculated by the NBAS code, and users should use this information for estimation and guidance purposes only. The NBAS code should not be relied on to confirm eligibility for any particular project, program, scheme or entitlement, and users should undertake their own independent assessment and seek appropriate expert advice to confirm such eligibility. Do not rely solely on the NBAS code to make decisions about your project, as there may be a number of other factors to take into account. The NBAS will be updated as the market evolves, knowledge improves, and technology changes over time. As this happens, the scores that NBAS calculates may change.

records.title: National Biodiversity Assessment System (NBAS) v1.0 Data Collection
records.description: PLEASE NOTE: This collection was developed for and used in NBAS v1.0. It has since been superseded by NBAS v2.1.1. Users seeking data associated with the current operational version of NBAS should refer to the NBAS v2.1.1 data collection (see Related Links). This collection contains derived datasets utilised in the National Biodiversity Assessment System (NBAS) v1.0, developed as part of the Ecological Knowledge System (EKS). The EKS is a partnership between CSIRO and the Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water (DCCEEW) to establish a transparent and authoritative source of information, biodiversity assessment and forecast capability for the Nature Repair Market. The NBAS is a software and data package that provides a nationally consistent approach to forecasting the expected biodiversity benefits of a given project within the Nature Repair Market scheme. This collection comprises information about the ecosystem typology used in the NBAS v1.0. It contains (1) a raster that denotes the location and boundaries of the ecosystem types as defined in NBAS (i.e. the intersections between the National Vegetation Information System (NVIS) major vegetation groups (MVGs) and Conservation Management Zones (CMZs), (2) an ecosystem identification key for each ecosystem type in the raster, and (3) an NBAS ecosystem typology table which reports the pre-1750 and extant ecosystem extent data, excluding MVGs that represent unclassified ecosystems, bare ground, inland water, and predominately non-terrestrial based ecosystems. These datasets were used in the NBAS v1.0 to forecast expected biodiversity benefits of nature repair projects. The NBAS is implemented via the PLANR tool (https://planr.gov.au/). This data collection is based on research created under the Project An Ecological Knowledge System for the Nature Repair Market scheme, which was funded by DCCEEW. The Commonwealth owns the intellectual property rights in any material developed while carrying out the Project. Copyright is retained by CSIRO (2025). Background: The NBAS provides a nationally consistent approach to assessing a project site’s current contribution to conserving biodiversity and forecasting the biodiversity benefits expected to result from project activities. The NBAS uses proportional persistence of native biodiversity as the ‘common currency’ of project assessment. Biodiversity persistence estimates the proportion of biodiversity that could be expected to exist without significant loss or decline, both now and into the foreseeable future. The NBAS (Version 1) outputs the following metrics: • Ecosystem condition, which represents the capacity of an area to provide the structures and functions necessary for the persistence of all native species naturally expected to occur in that area if it were in an intact (or reference) state. Ecosystem condition scores range from 0.0 (ecosystem integrity extinguished, ecosystem completely removed) to a maximum of 1.0 (ecosystem integrity in reference condition). • Landscape connectivity, which estimates the system level contribution that a given area is estimated to make to enhancing the connectivity of habitat across the broader landscape. • The conservation significance of the ecosystem types being protected or enhanced, accounting for their natural rarity and their level of depletion and degradation. • The overall contribution that an area makes to enhancing biodiversity persistence at a system level, integrating the effects of the above three components.

records.title: GRADE: Global Review and Assessment of Datasets for the Environment
records.description: The GRADE collection provides a systematic assessment of global geospatial datasets suitable for measuring and monitoring the state of nature. It addresses the rapid growth and fragmentation of environmental data resources by identifying, screening, and evaluating datasets using a reproducible and standardised workflow. The collection aligns with global frameworks (e.g. SEEA Ecosystem Accounting, TNFD, SBTN) and provides a structured evidence base to support environmental reporting, research, and decision-making. Information is synthesised from over 32,000 candidate datasets, from which 176 datasets were identified as suitable for global applications based on eight key criteria. These datasets span 13 environmental metric categories, including ecosystem extent, vegetation characteristics, carbon stocks and fluxes, water supply, use and quality, biodiversity, climate regulation, soil quality, and disturbance processes. For each dataset, a comprehensive set of structured metadata fields is provided, capturing: - Dataset description and thematic classification - Spatial and temporal characteristics (extent, resolution, frequency) - Metrics and units - Methodological details (algorithms, input data, validation approaches) - Statistical performance and uncertainty (where available) - Access mechanisms, licensing, and code availability

records.title: Ecological Knowledge System: Regional Pilot State and Transition Models
records.description: Collection: This collection contains a suite of models and datasets for regionally specific State and Transition Models (STMs) developed during the pilot phase of the Ecological Knowledge System (EKS) project. The EKS is a partnership between CSIRO and the Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water (DCCEEW) to establish a transparent and authoritative source of information, biodiversity assessment and forecast capability for the Nature Repair Market (the market). STMs are used in the EKS to synthesise knowledge about the dynamics, management, and restoration of ecosystems. The three pilot regions were the Burnett-Mary Natural Resource Management (NRM) region in southern Queensland (BM), the North-Central Catchment Management Authority (CMA) region in Victoria (NCCMA), and the Brigalow Belt North and Brigalow Belt South bioregions (Brigalow Belt) which extends from central Queensland to northern NSW. This collection comprises three types of information: (1) comprehensive summary reports for STMs developed by the EKS during the pilot phase,(2) STM data in JSON and Excel format detailing the states, transitions, and disturbances for each model, and (3) Excel files with quantitative transition probabilities for STMs developed for the BM and NCCMA regions only. The data is the same between the two formats, but they have different purposes. The JSON format is widely used for data interchange between different systems and applications. The Excel format is more convenient for people to read and use and is made available for that reason. Supporting documentation includes a Data Dictionary which defines the different components of this collection and its characteristics. This data collection is based on research created under the Project “An Ecological Knowledge System for the Nature Repair Market scheme”, which was funded by DCCEEW. The Commonwealth owns the intellectual property rights in any material developed while carrying out the Project. Copyright is retained by CSIRO (2025). To cite individual models within this collection, please use the citation specified in the applicable model summary reports. Background: The EKS uses STMs to organise regional scale understanding of how ecosystem management, such as restoration activities, impact ecosystem condition and biodiversity. STMs are conceptual tools that describe the state of a particular ecosystem (which may vary, for example, from reference to removed, in terms of ecosystem integrity), and the drivers or agents (e.g. threats, restoration interventions) that cause transitions between states. STMs enable distinction among states that are similar in condition (in terms of departure from reference condition) but differ in ecosystem characteristics (such as species composition, structure, and function). STMs also estimate the expected outcomes of different management interventions over specific timeframes. They are constructed using the following key components: • Reference states: The dynamic state of an ecosystem that has the highest ecosystem integrity • Modified states: An ecosystem state that is not in reference condition due to disturbances external to the ecosystem (i.e. exogenous disturbances) such as land clearing or grazing. • Transitions: The pathway through which an ecosystem may pass from one state to another. Transitions can be triggered by disturbances or management interventions external to the ecosystem. STMs can be used to identify the ecosystem state and the actions that are required to improve ecosystem condition to support biodiversity by restoring ecosystem structure, function, and composition. They can also be used to predict the likely ecosystem state of an activity area after restoration activities have been completed over specific timeframes.

records.title: Parkes observations for project P1385 semester 2026APRS
records.description: A vital step to the formation of stars is the formation of molecular hydrogen from the vast reservoir of atomic hydrogen in the galaxy, as dense molecular clouds are observed to be where stars are formed. Yet, we still have trouble observing this transition between atomic and molecular hydrogen. This is the allowed rotational lines for molecular hydrogen are not brightly emitting in cold molecular gas, and our usual tracer of CO is now known to miss a significant fraction of molecular hydrogen known as "CO-dark" molecular gas. In this project we propose to map this "CO-dark" molecular gas in a high latitude molecular cloud in 18cm OH, far from the confusion of the Galactic Plane. This cloud is thought to be located near the southern Galactic pole, on the local bubble wall. From previous observations with the UWL, we know a significant fraction of the cloud (80%) is "CO-dark", but with a single-pixel instrument we are limited in our understanding of the spatial and kinematic distribution of the "CO-dark gas". This gas phase is well traced by 18cm OH, and we propose to observe all four ground state lines of OH (1612, 1665, 1667 and 1720 MHz) along with 1420 MHz HI with the new 72-beam CryoPAF receiver. This dataset will be an important benchmark for this new instrument, as well as a huge forward step in understanding the distribution of "CO-dark" gas in a nearby molecular cloud with the sensitive widefield mapping coverage allowed by the new 72-beam receiver.

records.title: Parkes observations for project P1428 semester 2026OCTS_06
records.description: Globular Clusters (GCs) are renowned to be the host of a wealth of radio pulsars, most of which are millisecond pulsars. The extreme stellar densities characterizing the central regions of GCs promote the formation of binary systems where neutron stars can be recycled, and the formation of pulsars and binaries with extreme or unconventional properties. GCs have therefore been prime targets for pulsar searching and, as of today, more than 360 pulsars have been found in 46 different clusters. The much larger computing power and much more modern algorithms available today have recently fostered the re-processing of archival Parkes GC data. This has led to the discovery of a few new pulsars, and several promising candidates. Here, we request 22 hours of observing time to re-observe a set of 10 GCs where 56 promising candidate pulsars have recently been found via reprocessing of archival Parkes data. The recently installed Ultra-Wide-band Low receiver, in combination with the modern APOLLO backend, will provide a sharp increase in sensitivity compared to the archival data. This will allow us to confirm or refute the candidates, and potentially even discover additional pulsars. Confirming at least one pulsar in a GC has a great scientific value, since it would allow us to know the approximate dispersion measure associated with cluster, greatly easing the search for additional pulsars in the cluster, and it would increase the total number of clusters known to host radio pulsars, contributing to our understanding of the population of pulsars in GCs.

records.title: Parkes observations for project P1073 semester 2026APRS
records.description: There are still unanswered questions regarding how the highest mass O- and B-type stars are able to accumulate so much mass during their formation. While it is accepted that episodic mass-accretion events play a major role in this accumulation, there is not yet a statistically meaningful collection of observations of such events. This project will correct this: through the use of the CryoPAF's large field of view we estimate that we will observe upwards of 100 maser flares per year, a more than 10-fold increase of that observed with the UWL.

records.title: Coupled Coastal Hazard Prediction System (CCHaPS) Hindcast for Australia
records.description: CCHaPS, the Coupled Coastal Hazard Prediction System, is a 2D hydrodynamic and wave model (Semi-implicit Cross-scale Hydroscience Integrated System Model and Wind Wave Model III, SCHISM-WWMIII), configured around the Australian coastline including the Great Barrier Reef, and extending out to deep offshore waters or neighbouring landmasses. The model simulates water levels due to astronomical tides, weather, waves and aspects of wave-flow interaction over multiple decades, allowing for full consideration of the dynamics of extreme sea levels and waves in the Australian region, at high spatial resolution from ~7km off-shore down to ~250m at the coast, and ~100m in major river mouths. The model is run on an unstructured (triangular) grid comprising over 1.4 million nodes, which extends overland up to a 12m elevation contour, to enable modelling of inundation events and sea level rise. The CCHaPS hindcast covers the 40-year period 1981 to 2020. As of September 2026, this is extended to 2025. The hindcast is forced with downscaled ERA5 winds and mean sea level pressure produced by BARRA-R2, water levels from ORAS5, tides from TPXOv9.2, and spectral wave forcing from WHACS (see Lineage). The model used is SCHISM-WWMIII v5.9, using ST4 wave physics, run on NCI's Gadi supercomputer. The dataset comprises hourly netCDF data on an unstructured grid, compliant with CF, ACDD and UGRID metadata conventions. A notebook demonstrating how to interact with the data will be attached under Supporting Documentation. Variables included are: depth (non-time varying), sea surface height, wet-dry node, currents, significant wave height, mean wave direction, peak wave direction, directional spreading, t01 and t02 mean wave period, peak wave period, peak directional spreading, peak direction (rad), and orbital velocity. The data is also stored on CSIRO infrastructure in the {ev-acs-wp3-cchaps} volume, and at NCI in /g/data/ia39/WP3/release/CCHaPS. Examples of how to work with the data in Python are provided in the accompanying notebook "CCHaPS_examples.ipynb" (see Supporting Documentation) A manuscript describing this dataset (Hernaman et al, 2026) can be found at https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ocemod.2026.102731

records.title: RACS-low3 and RACS-mid1 raw source catalogues and associated data without additional brightness scaling
records.description: This collection contains some of the files necessary to reproduce the cosmic dipole analysis in the related publication (see https://github.com/o-oayda/cracking-into-racs-i for instructions on how to use the files). This includes the unscaled source catalogues for the Rapid ASKAP Continuum Survey (RACS), specifically for the first epoch in the mid passband (1367.5 MHz; RACS-mid1) and the third epoch in the low passband (943.5 MHz; RACS-low3). 'Unscaled' means that the individual images have not been scaled to account for observation-dependent brightness scale fluctuations, as documented in e.g. Duchesne et al. (2023) PASA 40 e034 at section 2.6. The collection also includes the all-sky RMS noise maps for both low3 and mid1, as well as the per-antenna Phased Array Feed temperature time series, as recorded over the course of each epoch. This temperature data is needed to substantiate the proposition in the related publication that as the antennas heat up, the reported flux densities are suppressed.

records.title: Data for "Reproductive traits mediate density-dependent scleractinian coral fertilisation"
records.description: The dataset was derived from a global literature review which aimed to examine the trait-based drivers of variability in reproductive capacity across species of hermaphroditic spawning corals. Reproductive capabilities, like egg production and fertilisation efficiency, were examined as a function of geographic region, density distribution, and habitat preference. Fertilisation data and egg size values were gathered from the published literature and density and habitat specifications for each species and location were derived from an expert elicitation process. Global - this is a review paper so the data we compiled spans the GBR, parts of Asia (Taiwan, Philippines, Hong Kong), and the Caribbean/ western Atlantic (Florida Keys, Belize, Panama, Curacao, etc.)

records.title: New South Wales coal mine methane emissions dataset for 2023/2024
records.description: This dataset contains information on 60 coal mines and their fugitive methane emissions for the Australian financial year 2023/2024 (from July 1, 2023 to June 30, 2024) in New South Wales (NSW), Australia. The coal mines are categorised as either open-cut or underground mines, as well as either active, care-and-maintenance or decommissioned. Furthermore, the dataset provides a 2 km x 2 km spatial coal mine emission distribution grid, by allocating the emissions to the ventilation shaft locations, active mining areas of the open-cut mining pits, and the mining areas of decommissioned underground mines. The dataset has been compiled using publicly available data sources, such as Safeguard, annual reviews, greenhouse gas assessment reports, Google Maps and Copernicus Sentinel-2 satellite data. A full list of references used to compile the dataset is given in the file “References.csv”. Our dataset accounts for 94% of the total methane emissions in NSW as reported in the Australia National Greenhouse gas Accounts (ANGA) (DCCEEW, 2026) and can serve as a basis for studies that require spatial knowledge of fugitive methane emissions in NSW. The data is presented in multiple comma-separated values (CSV) formatted files, containing the emission, as well as the point coordinates of the ventilation shafts and polygon coordinates (WKT format) for the mine extents for open-cut and decommissioned underground mines. The coal mine methane emission grids are given as a NetCDF-formatted file, which contains the active open-cut, active underground, and decommissioned underground, as well as the total coal mine methane emission grid at 2 km x 2 km spatial resolution given in units of [kg m-2 s-1] or [Gg a-1 per grid cell]. The grid uses a Lambert conformal projection, specified under the variable “lambert_conformal”. The uncertainties of emissions are ± 12.6 % for underground mines, and ± 30.5 % for open-cut mines, according to the National Inventory Report 2024 (Australian Government, 2026). For decommissioned underground mines, we assigned an uncertainty of ± 50 % as described in the National Greenhouse and Energy Reporting (Measurement) Determination 2008 (Australian Government, 2008). The authors make no claims concerning the accuracy of the dataset. Users of the dataset must decide whether it is fit for their purpose. For the data directly sourced from the publicly available data sources, the "Notes" column often contains information on how these data have been used to calculate the fugitive coal mine methane emission. More information about the dataset and the methods used to generate the dataset can be found in Jandl et al. (2026). Australian Government: National Greenhouse and Energy Reporting (Measurement) Determination 2008, https://www.legislation.gov.au/F2008L02309/latest/text, compilation No. 21, Federal Register of Legislation, 2008. DCCEEW: Australia’s National Greenhouse Accounts, https://www.greenhouseaccounts.climatechange.gov.au/, last access: 2026-05-15, 2026. Jandl I., Shahrokhi N., Rayner P. J., Trudinger C. M., Hynes R. G., Garthwaite M. C., Gaines L., and Schofield R.: A coal mine methane inventory for New South Wales, Australia at 2 x 2 km resolution for 2023/2024, 2026.

records.description: This is Version 1 of the Australian Soil Inorganic Carbon products of the Soil and Landscape Grid of Australia. The creation of this dataset (national estimates of presence and absence, depth to, concentration, and stocks of soil inorganic carbon) was performed by Ng et al. (2025) and published in Geoderma that was tiled: Mapping the distribution and magnitude of soil inorganic and organic carbon stocks across Australia. The work is available at: https://doi.org/10.1016/j.geoderma.2025.117239. Soil Inorganic Carbon content are a set of six digital soil attribute maps, and their upper and lower confidence limits, representing the soil attribute at six depths: 0-5cm, 5-15cm, 15-30cm, 30-60cm, 60-100cm and 100-200cm. Classification maps of presence and absence of carbonates are a set of six digital soil attribute maps, representing the soil attribute at six depths: 0-5cm, 5-15cm, 15-30cm, 30-60cm, 60-100cm and 100-200cm. There is a single classification map showing depth to carbonates. Detailed information about the Soil and Landscape Grid of Australia can be found at - https://esoil.io/TERNLandscapes/Public/Pages/SLGA/index.html Attribute Soil Inorganic Carbon; Units: Classification maps of presence and absence of carbonates [0: absent; 1: carbonates are present]. depth_to_carbonates [0: Carbonates are absent, 1: Carbonates are present at depth of 100-200cm, 2: Carbonates are present at depth of 60-100cm, 3: Carbonates are present at depth of 30-60cm, 4: Carbonates are present at depth of 15-30cm, 5: Carbonates are present at depth of 5-15cm, 6: Carbonates are present at depth of 0-5cm]. Soil Inorganic Carbon content [%]; Period (temporal coverage; approximately): 1950-2021; Spatial resolution: 3 arc seconds (approx 90m); Total number of gridded maps for this attribute: 23; Number of pixels with coverage per layer: 2007M (49200 * 40800); Data license : Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 (CC BY); Target data standard: GlobalSoilMap specifications; Format: Cloud Optimised GeoTIFF;

records.title: RV Investigator Voyage IN2026_V05 End of Voyage (EOV) Archive
records.description: This record describes the End of Voyage (EOV) data archive from the Marine National Facility (MNF) RV Investigator voyage IN2026_V05, titled "Next Generation of Ocean LiDAR." The voyage took place between August 27, 2026 and September 07, 2026 (AEST), departing from Brisbane and returning to Brisbane. For further information please refer to the voyage documentation links. Instruments used and data collected include: Regular measurements: Acoustic Doppler Current Profiler (ADCP; 38, 75, 150 KHz ), Greenhouse Gas Analysers (Picarro), Cloud Condensation Nuclei counter (CCN), Condensation Particle Counters (CPC), Disdrometer, Radon sensor, Mobility particle size spectrometer (MPSS), Black Carbon sensor (Aethalometer), CTD, Hydrochemistry, Fisheries Echosounder (EK80), Multibeam Echosounder (EM712, EM124, EM2040), Sub-bottom Profiler (SBP29), GPS Positioning System, Doppler Velocity Log, Thermosalinographs (TSG), Fluorometer, Oxygen Optode, Infrared Sea Surface Temperature Autonomous Radiometer (ISAR), pCO2, Ozone Sensor, Nephelometer, Atmospheric Temperature, Humidity, Pressure, Wind and Rain sensors, Photosynthetically Active Radiation (PAR) sensor, Precision Infrared Radiometer (PIR), Precision Spectral Pyranometer (PSP), Starboard and Portside Radiometers, Air Sampler, Seabird detector (Jonathan), Environmental DNA Sampler (eDNA), Triaxus, ECO Triplet, Submersible Ultraviolet Nitrate Analyser (SUNA), Expendable Bathythermographs (XBTs). Voyage-specific measurements: Baby MQ LiDAR, Tic Toc MQ LIDAR, PALS LIDAR, Beam Trawl, Core Argo floats, DALEC Radiometer, Micro Rain Radar (MRR), Drone, Remotely Operated Vehicle (ROV), Temperature String, Video, Wildlife Observations (seabirds, cetaceans and seals). The archive for the IN2026_V05 EOV raw data is curated by the CSIRO National Collections and Marine Infrastructure (NCMI) Information and Data Centre (IDC) in Hobart, with a permanent archive at the CSIRO Data Access Portal (https://data.csiro.au/), providing access to voyage participants and processors of the data collected on the voyage. All voyage documentation is available electronically to MNF support via the local network. Applications to access voyage documentation by non-CSIRO participants can be made via HF-Data-Requests@csiro.au All processed data from this voyage are made publicly available through the MNF Data Trawler (in the related links)

records.title: Parkes observations for project P1343 semester 2026OCTS_01
records.description: Fast radio bursts (FRBs) are millisecond-duration radio bursts of extragalactic origin. Since the discovery of the first FRB in the archival Parkes/Murriyang multibeam data, a broad dichotomy in population has emerged. Some FRBs have been seen to be repeating, while others are not, despite a significant amount of follow-up using different radio telescopes. The commissioning of new dedicated FRB detection systems has led to an exponential increase in the detected FRBs over the last decade. Despite >700 FRBs published to date, there is still a lack of understanding about the physical mechanisms through which FRB emission is produced. Due to the possibility of detecting multiple bursts from the same source in a repeating FRB, it forms an ideal sample set to uncover the physics of the source (e.g., emission mechanism, progenitor surrounding media), and test possible progenitor models. The coherent upgrade to the FRB detection system to ASKAP is expected to detect ~1-2 FRB/week. However, due to the limited fractional bandwidth available with ASKAP and survey nature of the telescope, probing the spectro-polarimetric characteristics of repeating sources is non-optimal. Hence, the large bandwidth offered by the ultra wideband-low (UWL) on Parkes/Murriyang is an ideal instrument to follow-up repeating FRB sources discovered through CRACO. Over the next ~6 months, we expect to double the number of repeaters that have been studied through the UWL. This will provide unprecedented insight into the progenitor environment and the surrounding media of repeating FRBs. We propose using the UWL to follow up repeater-like sources to study their wideband spectro-polarimetric characteristics.

records.title: Fisher Island Short-tailed Shearwater dataset: 1947-2017
records.description: The Fisher Island Short-tailed Shearwater (Ardenna tenuirostris) dataset contains long-term demographic and capture-mark-recapture records from the Fisher Island breeding colony in the Furneaux Group, eastern Bass Strait, Tasmania, Australia. Breeding shearwaters in the colony have been monitored annually since 1947, making this one of the longest continuous seabird demographic datasets in the Southern Hemisphere. The dataset collates records from a range of sources, including historical banding records from the Tasmanian State Library Archives, researchers’ personal handwritten notebooks, electronic banding data from the Australian Bird and Bat Banding Schemes, historical handwritten index cards and field research notebooks. The collection includes records for approximately 4,000 individual Short-tailed Shearwaters, comprising approximately 16,000 observations or resights. Records were collected through annual field monitoring, including nest inspections undertaken during the breeding season to record adults, pre-breeders, breeding pairs, burrow use, eggs, chicks, banding records and resight information. The dataset supports research on seabird demography, breeding biology, population dynamics, climate variability, conservation management and environmental impact assessment, including baseline studies relevant to potential offshore windfarm developments. There are two files: STSH_Database and the Tas Fauna Board A (all_TFB) dataset

records.title: APSIM Simulation Outputs for Australian Grains Cropping Systems, Emissions and Greenhouse Gas Mitigation
records.description: This data collection contains the APSIM outputs of 30+ year simulations of grain cropping systems where nitrogen fertiliser management and crop rotation are varied to understand the potential impact on greenhouse gas emissions and crop production. This covers 50 grain-growing sites across Australia, on three soil types from each site, using 7-11 relevant cropping rotation sequences per site. The simulations were repeated for three nitrogen fertiliser management strategies (Actual, Best Practical and Optimised) using cropping areas, sowing rules, N application, and rotations based on statistics and expert knowledge from two growing seasons 10 years apart (Baseline_2005 and Current_2015). These simulations output a range of crop production data, for example, yield, biomass, grain N and protein, as well as a range of carbon and N₂O emissions data, and detail impacts on soil nitrogen and carbon. The data collection contains two subfolders: the ‘Simulation data’ and the ‘Metadata’. The Simulation data subfolder contains a “Complete dataset.csv” file (complete dataset, 371 MB) and two folders of files where the Complete dataset.csv has been divided into files based on site (Site folder) and mitigation strategy (MitStrategy folder). Further information on site locations and other details can be found in the 05_Site and rotation information.xlsx file in the ‘Metadata’ folder. Descriptions of the mitigation strategies, after which the files were named, can be found in the Metadata subfolder > 06_Emission mitigation strategy information.xlsx. These files are analysis-ready and have been designed for filtering and querying the dataset. The Metadata folder contains all the relevant information required to understand the dataset, and more information on this can be found in the 01_ReadMe file in this folder. Each .csv file contains 56 columns of simulation details, filterable metadata, crop production, emissions data, and soil water and nutrient variables. A full list of variables, descriptions, and units is described in detail in the 04_Dataset Detail.docx file in the Metadata subfolder. This data aims to give grain growers and consultants a practical means to explore options to reduce their greenhouse gas emissions using data based on scientific research. The intent is that the end user can explore parameters, such as fertiliser application or crop rotations, to improve emissions and understand the potential impacts, either positive or negative, that those changes have on crop production. Currently in a raw state, these datasets will be summarised and presented in a more user-friendly manner.
